`AGENTS.md`:

```md
# TotK Recomp

Static recompilation of *Tears of the Kingdom* (Switch, ARM64) into a native Windows x86-64 exe with a Vulkan renderer. Design: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md). Toolchain, build commands and tests: [docs/building.md](docs/building.md).

## Game content boundary

This repository is public. Game data lives outside it and every derived file stays in ignored folders.

- The user's game and key paths are in `config.local.toml` (ignored). Pass the keys file path to tools; the tools read it themselves. Key values stay out of your output, logs, commands and files.
- Everything extracted or generated goes under `build/` or `generated/`.
- Every file the code generator emits carries the marker defined as `GENERATED_MARKER` in `tools/check_content.py`.
- Run `python tools/check_content.py --staged` before proposing a commit. It is the same check CI runs.

## Reusing code

`refs/` holds the upstream checkouts (`tools/fetch_refs.sh` recreates it). Read-only.

- Copy only MIT, BSD, ISC, zlib or Apache-2.0 code, keep its header, and add a row to `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- yuzu, suyu, OpenSmash-Ultimate and other GPL code: read for behaviour, write our own.
- `tools/vendor/` stays byte-identical to upstream; Windows changes go in `tools/extract.py`.

## Code

- Build C with MSYS2 UCRT64 Clang (`C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin`). Generated C uses GNU extensions, so `cl.exe` is out. Call Ninja from that directory by full path or put it first on PATH.
- Two Python environments: `.venv` (3.12) for the lifter and the build, `.venv-py314` for the extraction and shader scripts, which need `compression.zstd`.
- Generated C is never edited by hand: change the generator (`recomp/`).
- Every lifter change passes the differential tests against Unicorn ([docs/building.md](docs/building.md), "Checks"). After changing `recomp/jumptables.py`, `tests\jumptables_check.py` reports 0 disagreements on 1.2.1 and 1.4.3.
- `recomp/layout.py` alone decides module bases.
- Graphics bugs: [docs/maxwell.md](docs/maxwell.md) lists the Maxwell behaviour the Vulkan path must match and the TotK bugs other ports fixed.
- Comments say what the code does and why, in words that stand on their own. Cite our code by file plus function (a line number may follow as a hint) and upstream code by project, file and function: `refs/` moves, so its line numbers rot. Commit hashes belong to the attribution of copied code.

## Writing

Code, comments, docs and commit messages are in English. Commit messages are plain sentences without type prefixes.

```

`CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```md
# Contributing

## The one hard rule

Nothing that came out of the game goes into the repository: no game files, keys, extracted data, recompiled C, compiled binaries, shaders, shader caches, fonts, audio or movies. Not in commits, not in issues, not in pull requests. Only information about the game goes in: addresses, hashes, patch code we wrote, shader and bind-state identifiers.

Two checks enforce this:

- CI runs `tools/check_content.py` on every push and pull request.
- The same check runs before each local commit once you enable the hook:

  ```sh
  git config core.hooksPath .githooks
  ```

A failing check is never bypassed with `--no-verify`. If it flags a file by mistake, change the check in a separate pull request and say why.

Links to game files, keys or firmware in issues or pull requests get the issue closed and the content removed.

## Code from other projects

Code may be copied only from projects under MIT, BSD, ISC, zlib or Apache-2.0. Each copy keeps its original header and gets a row in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) with the source commit.

GPL projects (yuzu, suyu, OpenSmash-Ultimate, Unicorn inside the game binary) can be read to understand behaviour, but their code is not copied. Unicorn is fine as a separate test tool.

## Reporting bugs

Use the issue form. Include the port version and game update from the title line of the settings menu (F1), your GPU and driver (Copy system info in the menu's Advanced tab copies them), the log (`logs\totk.log` next to `totk.exe`; after a crash, copy it before you start the game again), and the steps to reproduce. Screenshots are fine; recordings of long gameplay are not needed.

## Pull requests

- One topic per pull request.
- Describe the problem, then what changed.
- Say how you tested it: which version, which scene, how long.
- A change to the lifter (`recomp/`) or the CPU headers passes the differential tests in [docs/building.md](docs/building.md), "Checks".
- Commit messages are plain sentences, without `feat:` or other prefixes.
- AI-assisted code is welcome. You are responsible for having read and run it.

## Code and docs

- Code, comments, commit messages and documentation are in English.
- Generated code is never edited by hand: change the generator.

```

`README.md`:

```md
# TotK Recomp

**TotK Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom* (Nintendo Switch, 2023) into a native Windows x86-64 application ([docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tears of the Kingdom*, dumped from your own console: the base game and the 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update. Instructions for obtaining those files will not be provided.
>
> The game is built from your files on your machine, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use. Do not share it.

## Status

Early development. The game is playable on Windows; visual bugs and crashes are still expected.

Report problems as issues, following [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Features

- Native code, not emulation
- Game updates 1.2.1 and 1.4.3, with saves that carry over between them
- 60 fps by default; up to 144 fps or the monitor's refresh rate (experimental)
- Custom resolutions (1080p, 2k...), supersampling and AMD FSR 1 upscaling
- In-game settings menu (F1) and performance overlay (F10)
- Keyboard, mouse and gamepad with remapping, rumble and gyro
- Xbox button prompts: a layout that keeps the Switch button positions and shows the Xbox labels
- Shaders prepared at install instead of during play

## Planned

- Linux and the Steam Deck
- Mods made for emulators: unpack a mod into a `mods` folder
- Ultrawide on 1.2.1 (1.4.3 has it for 2560x1080, 3440x1440, 3840x1600 and 5120x2160; other shapes get the wide camera with a 16:9 HUD)
- VRR

## Installing

Requirements: Windows 10 or later, an x86-64 CPU with AVX2, a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`, about 36 GiB free during setup (20 GiB after).

1. Download `TotK-Setup-<version>-windows.zip` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and unpack it.
2. Start `TotK-Setup.exe`. If SmartScreen warns about an unsigned app, choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
3. Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press *Start*. The setup builds the game once.
4. Play `totk.exe` from the install folder.

To update, run a newer `TotK-Setup.exe` on the same folder; saves and settings are kept. Settings are in the in-game menu and in `totk.ini` ([totk.ini.example](totk.ini.example) lists every key). Controls: [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md).

## Credits

TotK Recomp builds on the projects below. What was taken from each, with its license, is listed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

- [LAS Recomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp)
- [MacNativeGames](https://github.com/ly05010419/MacNativeGames)
- [d2r-mobile](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile) and [nxnative](https://github.com/seedds/nxnative)
- [SavageWindRecomp](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp)
- [Ryujinx](https://github.com/Ryujinx/Ryujinx)
- [deko3d](https://github.com/devkitPro/deko3d)
- [hactool](https://github.com/SciresM/hactool)
- [SDL 3](https://libsdl.org), [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), [AMD FSR 1](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Effects/FidelityFX-FSR), [Vulkan Memory Allocator](https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/VulkanMemoryAllocator), [libopus](https://opus-codec.org), [libvpx](https://chromium.googlesource.com/webm/libvpx), [Zstandard](https://github.com/facebook/zstd)
- [Switchbrew](https://switchbrew.org) and the Switch homebrew community

## License

The project's own code is under the [MIT License](LICENSE); third-party code keeps its own license ([THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)). The license grants nothing for Nintendo's game.

TotK Recomp is an independent, non-commercial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. *The Legend of Zelda*, *Tears of the Kingdom* and *Nintendo Switch* are trademarks of Nintendo.

## Building from source

[docs/building.md](docs/building.md) lists the toolchain and the steps. Everything the build writes stays under `build\` and `generated\`, which git ignores; run `tools/check_content.py` before a commit. Testers: [docs/tester-guide.md](docs/tester-guide.md).

Most of the code and documentation is written by AI coding agents (Claude Code) under the maintainer's direction; the maintainer plays every build and decides what is merged. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) holds the rules they work under.

## Compiler runtime in a source build

A build with the MSYS2 UCRT64 toolchain of `docs/building.md` links these into `totk.exe`. The installer release builds with llvm-mingw instead (its row below).

| Component | Version | License | How it is used |
|---|---|---|---|
| GCC runtime (`libstdc++`) | 16.2.0 | GPL-3.0 with the GCC Runtime Library Exception | linked into `totk.exe` |
| winpthreads (mingw-w64) | 14.0.0 | MIT / BSD | linked into `totk.exe` |
| libiconv | 1.19 | LGPL-2.1+ | `libiconv-2.dll`, unmodified, next to `totk.exe`: MSYS2's `SDL3.dll` imports it |

| hactool (SciresM @ `1d64a83450e025622f3468c28fc4164dad2c5ef6` plus `tools/hactool/portable.patch`, from MacNativeGames' `build_hactool()`: `MNG_TITLE_KEYS` and relaxed BKTR layout checks; our `tools/hactool/unicode.patch`: an embedded manifest that makes UTF-8 the process code page), built by `tools/build_hactool.py` with MSYS2 UCRT64 gcc; imports only KERNEL32 and the UCRT | https://github.com/SciresM/hactool | ISC | `bin/hactool.exe` |

`docs/architecture.md`:

```md
# Architecture

How the Switch build of *Tears of the Kingdom* becomes a native Windows x86-64 program. The upstream projects it builds on are listed under Credits in the [README](../README.md).

## Starting points

Two MIT projects cover different halves of the problem:

| | LAS Recomp | MacNativeGames |
|---|---|---|
| Game | *Link's Awakening* | *Tears of the Kingdom* 1.0.0–1.4.3 |
| CPU | ARM64 lifted to C, runs on x86-64 | Original ARM64 code runs directly on Apple silicon |
| OS boundary | IPC services and SVCs | ~163 `nn::*` SDK functions replaced by symbol, 38 SVCs |
| Graphics | Own NVN layer on Vulkan, own Maxwell translator | NVN front end + Metal 4 back end, Ryujinx translator |
| Useful to us | Lifter, NEON-to-C lowering, Windows memory layer, tests | Everything TotK-specific: host behaviour, NVN front end, version tables, patches, shader list |

MacNativeGames cannot run on x86-64 as is: its CPU path executes ARM64 code natively. LAS Recomp's host only covers what *Link's Awakening* calls. The port takes the CPU half from LAS Recomp and the game half from MacNativeGames, and writes the parts neither has: a lifter that scales to TotK, and a Vulkan back end for the NVN front end.

## Pipeline

### 1. Input

- Base 1.0.0 (`0100F2C0115B6000`) and one cumulative update (`0100F2C0115B6800`), NSP or XCI, plus the keys of the user's console.
- ExeFS and RomFS extraction: MacNativeGames' Python extractor (Python 3.14 for `compression.zstd`, `.venv-py314`).
- Update merging: hactool at `1d64a83` with MacNativeGames' BKTR patches, built by `tools/build_hactool.py`.
- Verification: MacNativeGames' `expected-v*.json` hashes of ExeFS, RomFS and fonts.
- Primary version: 1.4.3, the last update; performance work targets it. It replaced all three modules of the earlier updates (new SDK 20.5.22, RELR relocations, audio renderer REV15) and builds with `--version v143`, `recomp/patches-v143.txt`. 1.2.1 is a second target on the same build path; 1.0.0, 1.1.2 and 1.2.1 share `sdk`, `subsdk0` and `rtld` byte for byte, so only `main` differs among them. Saves load on either.
- Windows driver: `tools/extract.py` runs the vendored extractors (`tools/vendor/macnativegames/`) and identifies the update by the SHA-256 of its `main`. hactool has no Darwin `funopen` here, so the base Program NCA is copied out of the NSP before the BKTR merge (about 17 GB of temporary space).

### 2. CPU: lift ARM64 to C

- Modules: `main`, `sdk`, `subsdk0`. `rtld` is dropped and linking is done by the host, as MacNativeGames does.
- Base: LAS Recomp's hand-written decoder (`lifter.py`) and NEON/FP lowering (`simd_c.py`, `simd.h`), MIT. Output: one C function per guest function, direct calls for `BL`, an address-keyed table for indirect branches.
- Rewritten for TotK scale:
  - generator runs in parallel processes, with bounded memory per worker;
  - jump tables resolved by our own symbolic pass instead of Unicorn, which keeps GPL code out of the shipped generator;
  - `LDXP`/`STXP` (128-bit exclusive pairs) supported;
  - no 64 MB limit on `main`; `subsdk*` loaded;
  - NZCV and the six most used general registers of each function kept in C locals instead of the `Cpu`
    (`recomp/flags.py`, `recomp/regs.py`): registers are stored back where they changed, before calls, SVCs and
    exits, and reloaded after them. A call reloads only X0-X18 and X30, as AAPCS64 has the callee preserve X19-X29 and
    SP; `gen.py --no-callee-saved-trust` reloads those too.
- Coverage oracle: MacNativeGames' NSO rewriter lists every site where game code touches the OS (SVCs, TLS reads, counter reads, `x18`, exclusive windows, jump tables): 68,968 sites in 1.4.3 `main`. The lifter must handle every one.
- Memory: guest address equals host address, all below 2^39 (IPC encodes 39-bit addresses). The heap, stacks and the alias region are reserved with `MEM_WRITE_WATCH`, so the graphics back end can ask which pages the CPU wrote since the last upload (`runtime/memory.c`).
- Indirect branches go through `rt_dispatch` (`runtime/dispatch.c`), which looks the target up in the address table and tail-calls it.
- Testing: LAS Recomp's differential harness, every lifted instruction class checked against Unicorn (test-only, never linked into the game).

### 3. Host

- Portable C from MacNativeGames: threads and synchronisation, IPC, memory services, fs/RomFS, time, account, applet, audio renderer and effects. The Apple pieces (mach VM, CommonCrypto, AudioToolbox, GameController) are replaced with Win32 and SDL3.
- SDK boundary at the `nn::*` function level, matching MacNativeGames. Only `audren:u` and `sm:` are real IPC services.
- Window, keyboard and mouse: Win32 (`gfx_window.c`, `input_win.c`). Gamepad and audio output: SDL3. Voice: libopus (BSD). Movies: the SDK's `movie::Decoder` is replaced by a host VP9 decoder over libvpx (BSD, static; `runtime/ov_movie.c`), because FFmpeg from MSYS2 is a GPL build.
- zstd: most RomFS files of 1.4.3 are zstd frames. The patch set `zstd` sends the game's two decoder entry points to
  libzstd on the host (`ov_zstd.c`, `TOTK_ZSTD_NATIVE`); the lifted decoder took almost three times as long.
- Settings and menu: every key with its default is in one table (`cfg.c`), read from `totk.ini` and `TOTK_*`
  variables and written back when the in-game menu changes it. The menu and the performance overlay are Dear ImGui,
  drawn into the swapchain image (`runtime/ui/`); their text is in `ui_text.c` (English, Russian).
- OS calls the host makes go through `runtime/platform/` (`platform.h`, `win32.c`), so a Linux or macOS host adds one file instead of touching the rest. The split is not finished: `tools/check_platform.py` lists the Win32 uses left in the other files.

#### Threads and cores

Every guest thread is a host thread. TotK assumes Horizon's scheduler: three application cores, a thread runs only on a core in its affinity mask, and a higher-priority thread takes a core from a lower-priority one. The game keeps per-core data without locks and relies on that, so the host models it (`runtime/kernel.c`):

- Three virtual cores. A guest thread runs guest code only while it holds a core; the others wait in a priority-ordered list.
- Preemption. When a waiting thread has a better priority than a holder on a core it may use, exactly one holder is flagged. The holder checks the flag at its next SVC and at every indirect call (`rt_dispatch`: two loads when nobody waits), checks again under the kernel lock that a better thread still waits, and only then hands its core over. The indirect-call check comes from SavageWindRecomp's BotW port; checking only at SVCs left a better thread waiting up to 26 ms.
- Asynchronous preemption (from MacNativeGames 8bf0893, on unless `TOTK_ASYNC_PREEMPT=0`). Game code can run for
  milliseconds with neither (`TOTK_CORE_DIAG=1` measures it): a waiter that has spun 250 us suspends the holder and,
  if its host rip is in lifted code at host depth 0 (not inside a host call or SVC), moves it to `kern_ap_stub`, which
  saves the volatile registers and gives the core up there. A holder of a guest mutex counts at the priority of its
  best waiter, and one inside an SDK spin lock (TLR+0x100 `disable_count`) is not preempted: its interrupt flag is set
  and the switch happens at SVC 0x36. `TOTK_ASYNC_PREEMPT=2` keeps those two without interrupting. The interruption is
  Win32 (SuspendThread, SetThreadContext); another host needs a signal handler there, as MacNativeGames has.
- Host work gives the core back. Queue submits, presents, GPU waits, shader translation, `nn::fs` calls and NVN memory pool setup run without a core (`NVN_BLOCKING`, `kern_core_away`), as the Switch blocks those threads in IPC, so a thread blocked in the driver or on a file does not hold up guest threads.
- Spin waits. Loops that only another thread can end (857 in 1.4.3, 864 in 1.2.1, found by `tools/spin_waits.py`, the
  nxnative search) send their back-edges through `rt_spin_gate`, which pauses the core once per pass and hands it to a
  waiter after 50 us of polling (`TOTK_SPIN`, `TOTK_SPIN_HANDOFF_US`).
- `TOTK_FREE_CORES=1` turns the gate off, for experiments.

### 4. Graphics

- NVN front end from MacNativeGames (`nvn_api_*.c`, `nvn_obj.h`, texture layout and deswizzle). The game records command buffers through it; nothing reaches the GPU until the game submits.
- Vulkan 1.3 back end in place of MacNativeGames' Metal one. At `QueueSubmitCommands` the recorded NVN commands are replayed into Vulkan command buffers (`vk_exec*.c`).
- Memory pools. Apple's unified memory let MacNativeGames use the game's pools zero-copy. The back end imports the pools as host memory (`VK_EXT_external_memory_host`). On a discrete GPU, pools bound as buffers are mirrored in device-local memory and the pages the CPU wrote (write watch, above) are uploaded before a replay; idle pool regions are made read-only so the write-watch queries skip them (`vk_memory.c`). GPU-rendered textures are written back when the CPU reads them: on a pool invalidate, on a CPU copy, and for small targets once the CPU waits for a fence (`vk_texture.c`).
- Replay thread. `TOTK_REPLAY_ASYNC=1` moves the replay off the submitting thread onto a queue at most one frame behind the game; reads of GPU results wait for the newest writer instead of draining the queue (`vk_backend.c`). It is off by default because no timing has shown a gain yet.
- Recorder thread. The Vulkan calls the replay makes into its command buffer are made by a thread of their own (`vk_rec.c`, after Savage Wind Recomp and LAS Recomp): each `vkCmd*` copies its arguments into a packet of a ring and the recorder makes the calls in order; calls into other command buffers are made at once; the recorder also ends the command buffer, and the submit waits until it has. In the town on an RX 9070 the replay takes 17% less time on the submitting thread. `TOTK_VK_RECORDER=0` makes every call on the submitting thread.
- Uniform snapshot. The game rewrites per-object uniform blocks on other threads soon after it submits the frame
  that reads them, while the replay still records it. At the start of a submission's replay every uniform range it
  binds from CPU-written pools is copied, and the draws bind the copy (`vk_usnap.c`, after MacNativeGames'
  `TOTK_UBO_SNAPSHOT`); without it, late draws read another object's matrix.
- Driver data. The NVN driver keeps a per-stage constant bank (c0) that shaders read for things like point size, dispatch size and base instance. The back end fills it the way the driver does.
- Shaders: the Ryujinx translator 1.3.2 with MacNativeGames' patches and ours (`tools/xlate/patches/`), built with .NET 10 NativeAOT as `totk_xlate.exe` and run as a separate process. Its SPIR-V goes to Vulkan directly. `tools/prepare_shaders.py` and `totk.exe --prepare-shaders` translate and compile the variants of MacNativeGames' shared list ahead of play (29,587 for 1.4.3); the rest are translated on first use and cached on disk.
- Pipelines: `VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library` where the driver has it. Shader stages are compiled ahead into libraries; a draw that meets a new state links them at once (fast link), and an optimised pipeline replaces the linked one when a background thread finishes it. Pipeline keys seen in play are saved and built at boot. A draw whose pipeline is not ready is skipped when one of its pass's targets was rendered in the previous frame, and waits otherwise, so one-shot passes are never lost; a full-screen draw is skipped as well rather than waiting (`TOTK_PIPE_SKIP`); the stage libraries a waiting draw needs are built on idle workers in parallel (`TOTK_PIPE_WAIT`). Without the extension, a missing pipeline is built on a worker and the draw waits or is skipped by the same rule.
- Resolution. Patch sets make the game read its output, swapchain and scene sizes from the patch page
  (MacNativeGames' sites); `resolution.c` sets them from `output_res` and `render_scale` and grows the texture heap
  and the application pool to match. When the window is larger than the output, `vk_fsr.c` runs AMD FSR 1 (EASU,
  RCAS) on the present. An `output_res` that is not 16:9 (more than 1% off, `res_is_16x9`) also switches on the
  `aspect` patch set (1.4.3 only), which hands the output's ratio to the camera, and `romfs.c` `overlay_init` loads the
  `romfs-patches-<w>x<h>` overlay for it when it exists (`tools/make_romfs_patches.py --aspect`, laid out by
  `tools/ultrawide_layout.py`; the installer builds four sizes: 2560x1080, 3440x1440, 3840x1600, 5120x2160). Other
  shapes, such as 16:10 or 32:9, get the wide camera and the 16:9 HUD stretched over it. 1.2.1 has no camera patch: a
  wide size there keeps the 16:9 view. The `aspect` setting (`fit`, the default; `stretch`) decides what the present does
  when the window's shape differs from the output's: `fit` letterboxes, where a 16:9 game in a wider window used to be
  stretched.
- Occlusion queries never block the CPU; a result that is not ready counts as visible.
- ASTC textures are uploaded as they are where the device reports `textureCompressionASTC_LDR`, and decoded by a compute shader everywhere else (`vk_astc.c`, `TOTK_ASTC`). The CPU decoder (`tex_astc*.c`) is the fallback and the test oracle.
- Draw state. A draw whose program, bound state and textures repeat reuses the previous draw's shaders and skips rebuilding its descriptor sets; descriptor sets are written through update templates (`vk_exec_draw.c`, `vk_pipeline.c`).
- Allocation: Vulkan Memory Allocator. Debugging: Vulkan validation layers, per-pass frame dumps (`TOTK_DUMP`, `vk_dump.c`) and a flight recorder (`TOTK_FLIGHT`). RenderDoc cannot capture, because it hides `VK_EXT_external_memory_host` from the application.

Maxwell behaviour the back end has to match, and the TotK bugs other ports fixed: [maxwell.md](maxwell.md).

Why Vulkan rather than D3D12 or wgpu:

- The translator emits SPIR-V, which Vulkan consumes as is. D3D12 would add a SPIR-V to DXIL step; wgpu would add SPIR-V to WGSL through Naga and drop features the game uses (bindless textures, some atomics).
- LAS Recomp's Vulkan back end is a working reference on Windows.
- The same back end runs on Linux.

### 5. Toolchain

- Generated C: MSYS2 UCRT64 Clang + LLD. The generated code uses GNU extensions (`__int128`, `musttail`, vector types) that `cl.exe` cannot compile.
- Host code: the same Clang, C11.
- Builds: `tools/build_game.py` writes a Ninja file and runs MSYS2 Ninja. Every object is hashed before linking, because a faulty RAM module once flipped bits in stored objects.
- Analysis: Ghidra with the Switch loader, Capstone, `llvm-objdump`.
- Players: the installer ([installer.md](installer.md)) builds the game code on the player's machine with a bundled llvm-mingw, so no recompiled code is ever distributed.


```

`docs/building.md`:

```md
# Building from source

Windows 10 or later, an x86-64 CPU with AVX2, and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`. Allow about
60 GB for the work folder. Extraction wants about 55 GB free while it runs and keeps about 35 GB afterwards.

Players who only want to play can use the [installer](installer.md) instead: it builds the game on their machine
without this toolchain.

## Toolchain

Versions are the ones the build was verified with; newer patch releases are fine.

| Tool | Version | Install | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSYS2 UCRT64 | clang/lld 23.1.3 | msys2.org installer to `C:\msys64`, packages below | compiling the generated C and the runtime |
| Visual Studio Build Tools | 2026, C++ workload, Windows SDK 10.0.26100 | winget `Microsoft.VisualStudio.BuildTools` with `--add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Workload.VCTools --includeRecommended` | the linker .NET NativeAOT calls |
| .NET SDK | 10.0 | winget `Microsoft.DotNet.SDK.10` | the shader translator (`totk_xlate.exe`) |
| Vulkan SDK | 1.4.363 | winget `KhronosGroup.VulkanSDK` | validation layers, `vulkaninfo` |
| uv | 0.13 | standalone installer from astral.sh | the two Python environments |
| hactool | 1.4.0 @ `1d64a83` | `.venv\Scripts\python tools\build_hactool.py`, see below | NCA and update extraction |

MSYS2 packages, after `pacman -Syuu` (run it twice; the first pass updates the core and exits):

```sh
pacman -S --needed --noconfirm mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-{clang,lld,ninja,gcc,make,pkgconf,sdl3,opus,libvpx,zstd,vulkan-devel,\
vulkan-memory-allocator,vulkan-validation-layers,shaderc,spirv-tools} base-devel git unzip
```

`ffmpeg` from MSYS2 is a GPLv3 build and is never linked; the movies go through libvpx.

PATH:

- Add `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer` to the user PATH: NativeAOT needs `vswhere.exe`, or
  the publish fails at the link step (MSB3073).
- Another `cmake` or `ninja` earlier on PATH (a 32-bit winlibs MinGW, for example) is picked up by accident. The build
  scripts call Ninja from `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` themselves; from a shell, put `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` first.

### hactool

`tools/build_hactool.py` fetches SciresM/hactool at `1d64a83` into `toolchain\src\hactool`, applies the two patches in
`tools/hactool/` and builds a static `toolchain\hactool\hactool.exe` with MSYS2 UCRT64 gcc (a few seconds):

- `portable.patch`: the parts of MacNativeGames' `build_hactool()` that run on Windows, the `MNG_TITLE_KEYS` variable and
  the two BKTR fixes in `nca.c` for the subsection table padding and the subsection layout of newer cumulative updates;
- `unicode.patch`: a manifest with `<activeCodePage>UTF-8</activeCodePage>`, so paths under a non-ASCII user profile
  reach it intact.

hactool reads `-k <prod.keys>`; MSYS2 shells set `HOME`, which hides its default key location, so pass `-k` there.

## Build

From the repository root, in PowerShell. Every step that depends on the game version takes it as `<ver>`: `v143` for
1.4.3 or `v121` for 1.2.1. The tools default to `v121` when `--version` is left out. Saves load on either version.

1. Python environments (once). `.venv` runs the lifter and the build; `.venv-py314` runs the extraction scripts, which
   need the stdlib `compression.zstd` of Python 3.14:

   ```powershell
   uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
   uv pip install --python .venv/Scripts/python.exe -r tools/requirements.txt
   uv venv --python 3.14 .venv-py314
   uv pip install --python .venv-py314/Scripts/python.exe -r tools/requirements-py314.txt
   ```

2. Copy `config.example.toml` to `config.local.toml` and set the paths to your base game, the update and your console's
   keys file. `config.local.toml` is ignored by git. The tools read the keys file themselves.

3. Extract and verify. This writes `build\extracted\v0` (1.0.0) and `build\extracted\<ver>` for each update in
   `updates`, identified by its hash; a hash mismatch stops the run:

   ```powershell
   .venv-py314\Scripts\python tools\extract.py
   ```

4. Shader translator (once; no game files). This publishes `build\xlate\totk_xlate.exe`:

   ```powershell
   .venv\Scripts\python tools\build_xlate.py
   ```

5. Lift the modules to C, write the RomFS half of the frame-rate patches, then compile and link `build\<ver>\totk.exe`:

   ```powershell
   .venv\Scripts\python recomp\gen.py --exefs build\extracted\<ver>\exefs --out generated\<ver> --patches recomp\patches-<ver>.txt
   .venv-py314\Scripts\python tools\make_romfs_patches.py --version <ver>
   .venv\Scripts\python tools\build_game.py --version <ver>
   ```

   Lifting takes about 15 s, a clean compile about 200 s on 24 threads; later builds recompile only what changed.
   `--patches` builds in the frame-rate, resolution and other patch sets, switchable at run time. The link copies
   `SDL3.dll`, `libiconv-2.dll` and `libopus-0.dll` next to the exe.
   For Xbox button prompts, run `make_romfs_patches.py` once more with `--xbox-prompts`: it writes
   `build\<ver>\romfs-patches-xbox` ([controls.md](controls.md), "Xbox button prompts"); `build_game.py` copies it next
   to `totk.exe` like `romfs-patches`.

6. Prepare the shaders (once per build folder and translator). It needs `refs\MacNativeGames` (`tools\fetch_refs.sh`)
   for the shared shader list:

   ```powershell
   .venv-py314\Scripts\python tools\prepare_shaders.py build\<ver> --version <ver>
   ```

   Without this step the first launch compiles shaders and pipelines during play and stutters until the caches fill.
   The AMD driver keeps its pipeline cache per exe path and holds a limited amount: preparing another build folder can
   evict this one's. `totk.exe --warm-shaders` rebuilds it from the shader cache.

7. Run. Keep the window in the foreground; an unfocused window stalls the game.

   ```powershell
   build\<ver>\totk.exe
   ```

Settings live in `totk.ini` next to `totk.exe` ([totk.ini.example](../totk.ini.example) lists them). Saves go to
`build\profile` for `v121` and `build\profile-<ver>` for other versions (`build_game.py --profile` changes it).

### Portable folder

`.venv\Scripts\python tools\package_build.py --version <ver>` writes `build\<ver>-portable`, which runs on another of
your machines without MSYS2, Python or .NET. `romfs.bin` stays out unless you pass `--with-romfs`; otherwise put it in
`romfs\` next to the exe or point `TOTK_ROMFS` at its folder. Run `totk.exe --prepare-shaders` once in the copied
folder. The folder holds code and data derived from your game: for your own machines only.

## Checks

Before a commit:

- `python tools/check_content.py --staged`: nothing game-derived is staged. CI runs the same check;
  `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` runs it before each local commit.
- `build\<ver>\totk.exe --selftest`: layout, dispatch table and host-function registry, without game files.

The lifter (`recomp/`) and the CPU headers (`runtime/cpu.h`, `runtime/simd.h`) are checked against Unicorn. Every lifter
change passes these, all run with `.venv`:

| Test | Checks | Game files |
|---|---|---|
| `tests\diff\lift.py` | instructions sampled from the extracted modules; `--coverage` lists every word the lifter rejects or traps | yes |
| `tests\diff\simd.py` | the whole FP/SIMD encoding space | no |
| `tests\diff\atomic.py` | exclusive load/store sequences and ARMv8.1 atomics | no |
| `tests\diff\func.py` | whole functions as the generator emits them, loops, jump tables and calls included (calls go to a stub that checks the registers at the call) | yes |
| `tests\flags_check.py` | the function-local flag helpers of `runtime\cpu.h` against its packed ones | no |
| `tests\excl_mt.py` | the exclusive monitor helpers under contention and ABA, on several threads | no |
| `tests\jumptables_check.py` | `recomp/jumptables.py` against a Unicorn oracle; must report 0 disagreements, on 1.4.3 too | yes |

Runtime probes, each a mode of `totk.exe` (the list is at the top of `runtime/main.c`): `--probe-kernel`,
`--probe-vkexec`, `--probe-nvn-tex` and `--probe-shader` cover most runtime changes.

Shaders: `.venv-py314\Scripts\python tools\shader_census.py --version <ver> --translate` extracts every Maxwell shader
to `build\<ver>\shaders\` and runs it through the translator and `spirv-val`; failure groups go to `failures.txt`.
`tools\xlate_smoke.py` checks the translator alone, without game files.

## Reverse engineering (optional)

- Ghidra 12.1.2 with Adubbz's Ghidra-Switch-Loader in `toolchain\ghidra\` (JDK 21) opens the game modules (NSO).
- `tools\fetch_refs.sh` clones the upstream projects this port builds on into `refs\`, read-only.

`docs/controls.md`:

```md
# Controls

Input comes from the first SDL3 gamepad, the keyboard and the mouse, merged into one Switch controller (`runtime/input_win.c`). Buttons are ORed; each stick takes the source with the larger deflection. Keys and mouse buttons count only while the game window is in the foreground. `TOTK_INPUT=none` disables both (automated runs). `TOTK_*` settings can also be set in `totk.ini` next to `totk.exe` (`input = none`, `motion = 0`, `rumble = 0`); the environment overrides the file. `TOTK_RUMBLE_STRENGTH` is the rumble strength in percent (0 to 300, default 130; 0 is the same as `rumble = 0`). `TOTK_RUMBLE_CURVE` is the exponent applied to the amplitude before the strength (0.2 to 1.5, default 0.6; lower makes weak pulses stronger, 1 is linear). `TOTK_RUMBLE_TRIGGERS=1` also drives the impulse triggers of an Xbox pad.

`TOTK_PAD_LAYOUT` (`pad_layout`, the *Button layout* row on the Controls tab, live) picks which face button is Switch A:

- `nintendo`: by position, as on a Switch (the table below).
- `xbox`: south A, east B, west X, north Y, as an Xbox pad labels them; on a PlayStation pad cross is A, circle B, square X, triangle Y.
- `auto` (default): `nintendo` for a pad whose east button SDL reports labelled A (Switch Pro Controller, Nintendo-layout pads), `xbox` for the others.
- `xbox_prompts`: the buttons as `nintendo`, and the game's prompts name the Xbox labels (see Xbox button prompts below).

The log names the layout in effect (`input: gamepad layout ...`); the menu shows it under *Automatic*. With `nintendo`, `xbox` and `auto` the game's button prompts stay Switch letters; `xbox_prompts` changes them.

| Switch | Gamepad (by position, Nintendo layout) | Keyboard and mouse | Action in the world |
|---|---|---|---|
| Left stick | left stick | W A S D | move |
| Right stick | right stick | mouse; arrow keys as a second source | camera |
| Y | west | left mouse button | attack |
| ZL | left trigger (over 50%) | right mouse button, Z | shield, lock on |
| ZR | right trigger (over 50%) | F, X | bow |
| X | north | Space | jump |
| B | south | Left Shift | run, cancel |
| A | east | E | interact, pick up |
| L | left shoulder | Q | abilities |
| R | right shoulder | R | throw weapon |
| Left stick click | left stick click | Left Ctrl | crouch |
| Right stick click | right stick click | C | first-person view |
| D-pad left, up, right, down | D-pad | 1 2 3 4 | quick-select |
| Plus | Start | Tab | menu, inventory |
| Minus | Back | M | map |

Esc is unbound in the game; it opens the settings menu and releases the mouse cursor (see Mouse camera). Z and X duplicate ZL and ZR so menu pages turn with two neighbouring keys; the menu tabs (L, R) are Q and R. The mouse wheel is unbound. The bindings are the tables of `input_map` in `runtime/input_map.c`: the keys (platform-neutral key ids) and one gamepad table per layout (gamepad inputs by position); `runtime/input_win.c` translates Win32 virtual keys and SDL buttons.

## Xbox button prompts

`pad_layout = xbox_prompts` (*Xbox prompts (A right)* on the Controls tab) is for an Xbox pad played by position. The buttons work as with `nintendo`: the right button, labelled B, does Switch A (interact, confirm), and the bottom one, labelled A, does Switch B (run, cancel). The letters the game shows are swapped to match the labels, A with B and X with Y, so each prompt names the button to press. The other layouts leave the prompts alone: with `xbox` the Switch letters already match the labels.

The swapped letters are part of the game's textures, fonts and messages, so they follow the layout and not the bindings. A button remapped with a `bind_` line or on the Controls tab keeps the letter the game draws for it, and the prompt then names the wrong button. Use `xbox_prompts` with the default bindings.

The buttons change at once, but the game reads its UI archive and fonts once at boot, so the prompts change at the next start (the menu says *prompts change after restart*). `xbox_prompts` loads `romfs-patches-xbox` next to `romfs-index.bin` in place of `romfs-patches` (`runtime/romfs.c`, `overlay_init`): the same 60 fps patches, with the swap made from the game's own files by `tools/make_romfs_patches.py --xbox-prompts`, which the setup runs next to the plain one:

- the action prompt (`DoCommand_00`) draws the letter images `Nt_KeyTexA/B/X/Y_00`, whose image data is swapped, in a diamond that names the other face buttons. The diamond's letters are text the game takes from `LayoutMsg/DoCommand_00.msbt` of each language's `Mals` archive (and the layout's own text panes behind it); both are swapped. The diamond's shape shows the button's position and stays.
- every other prompt is text in the button font (`scft/External.bfotf` in each `Font/Font*.Nin_NX_NVN.bfarc.zs`, glyphs U+E040 to U+E043); the A and B, X and Y glyphs are swapped.

Without the folder (an install made by an older setup, or one where the setup could not prepare it and showed a warning) the menu says the files are missing, the log has `RomFS overlay: pad_layout = xbox_prompts, but ...`, and the Switch prompts stay; running the setup again on the install folder writes it. In a source build, `.venv-py314\Scripts\python tools\make_romfs_patches.py --version <ver> --xbox-prompts` writes `build\<ver>\romfs-patches-xbox`.

## Window keys

| Key | Gamepad | Action |
|---|---|---|
| F1 or Esc | Minus and Plus together | open or close the settings menu; the game gets no input while it is open |
| F10 | | performance overlay: off, frame rate, full panel |
| F11 | | borderless fullscreen on or off, saved to `totk.ini` |

The Minus+Plus combo never reaches the game. In the menu the arrow keys, the D-pad or the left stick move, Enter or A selects, Q and E or L and R switch tabs, Esc or B goes back (Switch button names, as in the table above).

## Remapping

The *Controls* tab of the settings menu lists, under the button layout, every Switch button and the eight stick directions the keys drive (movement and camera), each with two key cells and a controller cell. Select a cell, press A or Enter, then press the new key, mouse button or controller button; Esc or five seconds without a press cancel, and a controller button cancels a key cell. Delete, Backspace or X clears the selected cell. A key another action has moves to the new one (the description names the action it left); a controller button swaps with the one it replaces. A remapped controller button is physical: from then on the face buttons (A B X Y) stay where they are in both layouts, until the buttons are put back as the layout in use has them or *Reset all buttons* is chosen. F1, F8, F10, F11 and Esc cannot be bound (the menu, the flight recorder and the window keep them). Punctuation keys are named by their place on a US keyboard; the menu shows the character the keyboard layout in use puts there.

The tab writes `totk.ini` lines, one per Switch button or stick direction: `bind_<button> = <entry>, <entry>, ...`. The button is `A B X Y L R ZL ZR PLUS MINUS LEFT UP RIGHT DOWN LCLICK RCLICK`, or a stick direction `LSTICK_LEFT LSTICK_UP LSTICK_RIGHT LSTICK_DOWN` (movement, W A S D by default) and `RSTICK_...` (camera, the arrow keys). An entry is `pad:<name>` or `key:<name>`:

- pad names: `south east west north l r zl zr start back lstick rstick dpad_left dpad_up dpad_right dpad_down lpaddle1 rpaddle1 lpaddle2 rpaddle2` (`zl`, `zr` are the triggers; the paddles are the back buttons of an Xbox Elite, DualSense Edge or Steam Controller, upper pair 1, lower pair 2, and no Switch button has them by default)
- key names: `a` to `z`, `0` to `9`, `f2` to `f7`, `f9`, `f12`, `num0` to `num9`, `space tab enter backspace lshift rshift lctrl rctrl lalt capslock insert delete home end pageup pagedown up down left right`, `num_add num_sub num_mul num_div num_decimal`, `minus equals lbracket rbracket semicolon apostrophe comma period slash backslash grave`, `mouse_l mouse_r mouse_m mouse_x1 mouse_x2`
- `key:default` and `pad:default` keep that part's defaults (`pad:default` is each layout's own button).
- `none` leaves the button unbound.

A line replaces every default of that button, pad and keyboard, so list the keys you still want or use `key:default`. Pad names are physical positions, so a line means the same in both layouts and replaces the layout's own button for that Switch button. Stick directions take keys only: the controller's sticks and the mouse camera always work. Buttons without a line keep the table above. Names are case-insensitive. An invalid entry logs one `input: bind ...` line and is skipped; a line without a valid entry changes nothing. The `TOTK_BIND_<button>` environment variables work like any other setting. A changed line applies at once (`runtime/input_win.c` builds the tables again at its next poll).

A pad that reports its face buttons swapped (A/B and X/Y, as some GuliKit models do) is fixed with:

```
bind_A = pad:south, key:E
bind_B = pad:east, key:lshift
bind_X = pad:west, key:space
bind_Y = pad:north, key:mouse_l
```

## Mouse camera

Mouse motion (raw input) becomes right-stick deflection. Each presented frame takes the counts moved since the last frame, divides by the frame time and sets the deflection to `counts per second * TOTK_MOUSE_SENS / 3000` of full, held for that frame, so the turn rate does not depend on the frame rate. This is not mouselook: the game's stick curve and dead zone still apply, so very slow movements do nothing and a fast flick saturates. The mouse deflection competes with the gamepad and arrow keys by the larger-deflection rule.

`TOTK_MOUSE_SENS` (0 to 10, default 1; higher turns faster, 0 turns the mouse camera and the cursor capture off). While the window is the foreground window the cursor is hidden and confined to the client area. It is released on focus loss, minimise, while F11 changes the window, during a size or move loop and while a text entry is open. Esc releases it by hand: the cursor shows, the mouse camera and mouse buttons stop, and the window can be moved, minimised or closed. A mouse click inside the client area captures it again; that click does not reach the game. Activating the window by a click on its title bar or border does not capture, so it can be dragged or closed right away; Alt+Tab or a click in the client area captures as before. `TOTK_INPUT=none` disables the capture too.

`TOTK_STICK_DEADZONE` (0 to 50, default 8) is the gamepad stick dead zone in percent of full deflection, the same for both sticks. It is round: a stick inside the circle reads centred, and the rest of its travel is scaled to start at 0 at the edge, so full deflection still reaches full. Raise it for a stick that drifts. The game's own dead zone applies after it.

The stick direction bits (`StickLLeft` to `StickRDown`) are derived from the sticks at 50% deflection. A gamepad plugged in later is picked up within one second; with none connected the log says `input: no gamepad`.

## Scripted input

`TOTK_INPUT_SCRIPT=<file>` replays presses. It is ORed with real input and still applies under `TOTK_INPUT=none`. One event per line, `#` starts a comment:

```
<frame> <button> [hold_frames]            # A B X Y L R ZL ZR PLUS MINUS LEFT UP RIGHT DOWN LCLICK RCLICK; hold defaults to 4
<frame> LSTICK|RSTICK <x> <y> [hold_frames]   # -32767..32767, up is +y
@<ms> <button> [hold_ms]                  # timed on the world clock
@<ms> LSTICK|RSTICK <x> <y> [hold_ms]
```

`<frame>` counts 60 Hz ticks of game time since the first frame (presented frames at 60 fps), so the title menus get the presses at the same game time at any frame limit. `@<ms>` counts milliseconds of the world clock: game time stepped since the end of the first save load (the player leaves the title screen's origin), so a timed event lands at the same game time at any frame rate and load length. A later load, such as fast travel, still shifts what follows. In a script with timed lines the untimed ones stop when the world clock starts, as the load ends at another tick in each run. Each event logs once (`input: script frame N tick T: A`). `tools/input/load_save.txt` loads the first save from the title screen.

`TOTK_INPUT_RECORD=<file>` (`input_record` in `totk.ini`, or Input recording in the menu) writes the merged input in the same format, one line per button press and per stick segment: events before the world clock starts by tick, the rest timed; a button or stick held when the world clock starts is cut there and goes on as a timed event. The file replays as a script, which makes it the repro to attach to a bug report.

`TOTK_TEST_PAD=<lx>,<ly>,<rx>,<ry>` attaches an SDL virtual gamepad at start whose sticks rest at these raw SDL axis values (-32768 to 32767, down is +y), so a drifting or held stick can be tested without a controller: the values go through the gamepad mapping and `TOTK_STICK_DEADZONE` like a real pad's, and `TOTK_INPUT_RECORD` shows what reached the game.

## RenderDoc capture (blocked)

`TOTK_RDOC=<frame>[,...]` (`runtime/rdoc_win.c`; `TOTK_RDOC_DIR`, `TOTK_RDOC_DLL`) loads RenderDoc before `vkCreateInstance`. RenderDoc hides `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`, which the back end requires for guest pool imports (`runtime/vk_memory.c`), so device creation fails under it. A capture needs a copy-based pool fallback first.

```

`docs/installer.md`:

```md
# Installer

A public release that turns the player's own game files into a playable TotK folder. The release carries no game
data and no code derived from the game: the installer builds the game on the player's machine. The installed folder
holds only the game; the installer and its tools stay outside it.

## What the player does

1. Downloads `TotK-Setup-<version>-windows.zip` from GitHub Releases (none is published yet), unpacks it anywhere and
   starts `TotK-Setup.exe`.
2. Picks:
   - the base game (XCI or NSP) and the 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update (NSP);
   - their `prod.keys`;
   - the game language and the install folder.
3. Waits for the setup, one time. The window shows each step and its progress.
4. Plays `totk.exe` from the install folder. The installer and the source NSP or XCI can be deleted.

The install folder (`main.c` `portable_paths()` reads this layout; it stays portable):

```
<install folder>/
  totk.exe, SDL3.dll, libopus-0.dll, totk_xlate.exe
  totk.ini                       language; the other keys as commented defaults (totk.ini.example)
  exefs/, romfs/                 extracted from the player's files
  profile/                       saves
  logs/                          totk.log of the last run, totk.1.log to totk.4.log of the runs before it
  shader and pipeline caches     prepared by the setup; shader-cache/shader-cache.pack holds the translations
  totk-install.json              what built this folder: release version, input hashes, finished steps
```

## Updating the port

The player runs a newer installer on the same folder. It reads `totk-install.json`, keeps `romfs/`, `exefs/`,
`profile/` and `totk.ini` after checking their hashes, rebuilds `totk.exe` and re-prepares the shaders. A newer
release that changes nothing game-derived skips the rebuild.

Given another update file than the recorded one (1.2.1, then 1.4.3), the installer extracts and builds again from it and
keeps `profile/`. Saves carry over both ways: 1.4.3 converts a 1.2.1 save on load, and 1.2.1 loads the saves 1.4.3 wrote.

## Setup steps

1. **Check** before writing anything: the files open with the keys, the update is 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 (by hash, as
   `tools/extract.py`), the keys are new enough for the update, enough space is free on the target disk (about 36 GiB at the peak of a
   first install, 20 GiB after it), the CPU has
   AVX2 (`-march=x86-64-v3`), a Vulkan 1.3 GPU exists. Each failure is one clear message.
2. **Extract** ExeFS and RomFS into the install folder and verify the hashes.
3. **Lift** the ExeFS to C (`recomp/gen.py`, `recomp/patches-v121.txt` or `patches-v143.txt`) into a temp folder next
   to the installer.
4. **Compile** the generated C, `modules.c`, `romfs.c`, `patches.c` and `ov_zstd.c` (they bake the per-install layout, RomFS
   hashes and the game version's patch page) and link
   them with the prebuilt runtime library into `totk.exe` (`build_game.py --runtime-lib`; about 3 min on 24 cores).
5. **Prepare** the RomFS patches and the shaders (`tools/make_romfs_patches.py`, `tools/prepare_shaders.py`,
   `totk.exe --prepare-shaders`) in the install folder, then fold the shader cache's loose files (four per shader, about
   117,000) into `shader-cache/shader-cache.pack` (`tools/pack_shader_cache.py`). totk.exe reads the pack first and
   writes the translations it makes in play as loose files; running the tool again with the game closed folds those in.
   The patches are written twice: `romfs-patches` and `romfs-patches-xbox` (`--xbox-prompts`, the A/B and X/Y prompts
   swapped for `pad_layout = xbox_prompts`).
6. **Clean up** the temp folder (generated C and objects, about 1.3 GB).

A cancelled or failed setup resumes from the last finished step (`totk-install.json`).

## Command line

`installer/` (stdlib only; `installer/layout.py` maps the release folder and, in a repository, the dev toolchain):

```
python -m installer --base FILE --update FILE --keys FILE --lang CODE --dest DIR [--root DIR] [--temp DIR] [--verify]
```

- On a folder with `totk-install.json` only `--dest` is needed; the game files only when the extraction must run again.
- stdout: one JSON event per line, types `start`, `plan`, `step` (started, done, skipped), `progress` (step, phase,
  done/total/unit), `space` (bytes needed and free on the install disk and the temp disk), `warning`, `error`, `end` (`installer/events.py`). Messages are ids with parameters;
  `installer/text/en.json` holds their English text. The human-readable log goes to `<temp>/logs/`.
- Exit codes: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 bad command line, 3 cancelled. The window cancels with Ctrl+Break to the
  installer's process group.
- Each step records a key over its inputs (runner.py). A step with the recorded key and intact output is skipped, so
  resume and update are one rule; output kept from another release is re-hashed first.
- Peak space on the install disk is about 36 GiB, not 22: the extraction copies both Program NCAs (16.3 GiB) next to
  the merged RomFS (15.9 GiB) before it deletes them. The check computes the exact figure.
- Window (`python -m installer.gui`, `installer/gui.py` draws, `installer/guilogic.py` decides): form, step list with
  progress, space line, collapsible log, Cancel (Ctrl+Break to the CLI's process group, then it waits for the exit),
  finish screen with Open folder. English or Russian, chosen from the Windows display language, switchable in the
  window; every sentence is an id in `installer/text/<en|ru>.json`. A folder with `totk-install.json` needs only the
  folder. `--selftest [--shots DIR]` builds every screen in both languages and closes itself.
- `tests/installer_gui_test.py`: event model, form, catalogs, cancel, the self-closing window and one end-to-end run
  of the CLI in `--verify` mode (needs `build/install-test` and `build/extracted/v121`; see its docstring).
- `tests/installer_test.py`: bookkeeping with fake steps. `tests/installer_e2e.py`: a dev-mode run with the files of
  `config.local.toml`.

## Release layout

The unpacked release; `tools/make_release.py` assembles it and `--zip` packs it:

```
TotK-Setup.exe        starts python/pythonw.exe -m installer.gui (installer/launcher/launcher.c, no console)
installer/            the installer: steps, CLI, window, en/ru text catalog
python/               Python 3.14.9 embeddable + numpy, lz4, cryptography, cffi, pycparser (+ tkinter for the window)
recomp/, tools/       the lifter and the build, extraction and shader scripts the steps run (copied from the repo)
llvm/                 llvm-mingw, x86_64-only subset (Apache-2.0 with LLVM exception; mingw-w64 parts permissive)
runtime/              libtotkrt.a and the headers the generated code and modules.c/romfs.c/patches.c include
bin/                  totk_xlate.exe, hactool.exe, SDL3.dll, libopus-0.dll, ninja.exe
data/                 shader_list.tsv (MacNativeGames, MIT)
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
totk.ini.example, VERSION  the default ini; the release string (the repository's VERSION plus the commit)
```

- SDL3 comes from the upstream release, not MSYS2: MSYS2's DLL imports the LGPL libiconv.
- Every bundled third-party piece gets a row in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- The release contains nothing game-derived; `make_release.py` runs `tools/check_content.py` over the folder before it
  finishes.

## Constraints

- The installer steps contain no Win32 calls: Linux follows with its own compiler and the same steps.
- The keys file path is passed to the tools; key values never appear in the UI, logs or files.
- The window is a front end over the CLI (`python -m installer --base ... --update ... --keys ... --lang ... --dest
  ...`), which prints one JSON progress event per line. Tests and CI use the CLI.
- Paths may hold any Unicode characters (a Cyrillic user name puts the temp and install folders under it). Every exe
  the setup runs or builds reads its arguments and paths as UTF-8 through an `activeCodePage` manifest: hactool
  (our patch, [building.md](building.md)), totk.exe (`runtime/totk.rc`), ninja (upstream). The Python steps write
  their files and logs as UTF-8, and `build_game.py` quotes paths with spaces on its Ninja command lines.
- A game file whose data fails its hash checks or ends early stops the setup with `check.input_damaged`, which names
  the file and asks to copy it again (`extract.DamagedFile`). A failed merge checks the base Program NCA alone to tell
  which file is damaged.
- Unsigned exe: SmartScreen warns on first start.

## Later

- Re-warm the driver cache on start after a move, GPU or driver change.
- NSZ and XCZ input. Linux release.

```

`docs/maxwell.md`:

```md
# Maxwell / NVN behaviour a port must reproduce

Reference for diagnosing graphics bugs. Each item: what Maxwell (GM20B, 3D class `B197`, compute `B1C0`) and NVN do,
what Vulkan / AMD (RDNA4, our GPU0) do instead, how emulators and ports handle it, and the source. Items are ordered by
how likely they are to cause visible artifacts. "Ours:" marks what our runtime does (grep-level look, see section 7;
our code is cited by file and function). Licensing: yuzu/suyu are GPL, cited for behaviour only.

Source shorthands:

- **OGD**: NVIDIA open-gpu-doc `classes/3d/clb197.h`, `classes/compute/clb1c0.h` (MIT-style),
  <https://github.com/NVIDIA/open-gpu-doc/tree/master/classes>. Offsets below are method offsets in `clb197.h`.
- **G80TEX**: Mesa nouveau `src/gallium/drivers/nouveau/nv50/g80_texture.xml.h` (MIT),
  <https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/main/src/gallium/drivers/nouveau/nv50/g80_texture.xml.h>.
- **RYU-SU**: Ryujinx `Ryujinx.Graphics.Gpu/Engine/Threed/StateUpdater.cs` (MIT), mirror at 1.1.1137:
  <https://git.dawidpotocki.com/mirror/ryujinx/plain/src/Ryujinx.Graphics.Gpu/Engine/Threed/StateUpdater.cs?h=1.1.1137>.
- **RYU-SH**: Ryujinx shader translator vendored at `refs/MacNativeGames/vendor/ryujinx/src/Ryujinx.Graphics.Shader/`
  (Ryujinx 1.3.2, MIT). Paths below are relative to it.
- **NXN**: nxnative's graphics notes, `refs/nxnative/docs/agents/` (MIT). nxnative has rewritten them since; each
  row states the behaviour and fix it took from them.
- **MNG**: `refs/MacNativeGames` @ `b75be8cfa704df3701e86130c8ced268e79d6b11` (MIT); line numbers below are at that
  commit.
- **DK3D**: `refs/deko3d` @ `373bfd43d8b2d805fa2eb7d406dbb823032df958` (zlib, fincs), the homebrew Maxwell driver for Switch. Written
  against the hardware, not the NVN API: what it programs is what the GPU needs. Paths relative to `source/`. `.def` files give
  methods as word indices (`engine_3d.def`); byte offset = index x 4, so `0x5A1` = OGD `0x1684`. No conditional rendering, no
  provoking-vertex conversion, no 8-bit indices in it.
- **YZ-2305 / YZ-2306**: yuzu progress reports May / June 2023,
  <https://yuzu-mirror.github.io/entry/yuzu-progress-report-may-2023/>,
  <https://yuzu-mirror.github.io/entry/yuzu-progress-report-jun-2023/> (behaviour only).
- **VKSPEC**: Vulkan 1.4 specification, <https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html>;
  **GLSL450**: SPIR-V GLSL.std.450 extended instructions, <https://registry.khronos.org/SPIR-V/specs/unified1/GLSL.std.450.html>.

## 1. Render targets

| # | Maxwell / NVN | Vulkan / AMD | Emulators / ports | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | **Colour target the fragment shader does not write keeps its old texel**, even with blending enabled. | Undefined value written/blended. | NXN: zero write mask and no blend for unwritten outputs (`reflection colors`). Already fixed here. | NXN; MNG `games/totk/tests/metal_semantics/probe.m:5` |
| 1.2 | **Unwritten vertex outputs read as (0, 0, 0, 1)** in the next stage, including the unwritten components of a partly written output (VS writes xyz, FS divides by w). | FS input with no VS output: interface mismatch, value undefined; an unwritten component of a written output is undefined (AMD: whatever the register holds, often 0). | Ryujinx initialises exactly the components the next stage reads, but only when stages are linked (`Translation/Translator.cs:212-227`, `NextInputAttributesComponents`); position starts (0,0,0,1) (`:259`). NXN Link's Awakening: sun shadow lookups divided by w = 0, scene dim, no shadows. Ours: missing outputs padded with (0, 0, 0, 1), unlinked outputs initialised by translator patch 0006 (section 7, check 2). | NXN |
| 1.3 | **Clears honour the scissor and the clear's own channel / stencil write mask**, and may come between draws inside a pass. `SET_CLEAR_SURFACE_CONTROL` (0x10f8) has `RESPECT_STENCIL_MASK`, `USE_CLEAR_RECT`, `USE_SCISSOR0`, `USE_VIEWPORT_CLIP0`. | `vkCmdClearAttachments` takes a rect but **ignores the colour write mask**; load-op clears are whole-attachment. | NXN/MNG draw a triangle with the clear's mask (`clear_color_tri`, `clear_ds_tri`); TotK uses mid-pass, partial-mask and partial-scissor clears (NXN). yuzu: "red dot" was clears hitting the wrong RT index (YZ-2305, PR 10243). Hardware recipe (DK3D): `CLEAR_BUFFERS` (`0x674` = 0x19d0) carries the colour channel mask (bits 2-5), depth (0), stencil (1), target id (6-9) and layer (10-20) in one word; `ClearBufferFlags` (`0x43E` = 0x10f8) is set once to `StencilMask | Scissor` (`maxwell/gpu_3d_base.cpp:69`), so every clear is cut by scissor 0 and its stencil bits by the stencil front write mask register, and DK3D's colour clear does not program `ColorWriteMask` (`0x680`). A stencil clear writes `StencilFrontMask` (`0x4E7`) and `ClearStencil` (`0x368`) just before the clear and restores the shadowed state after (`gpu_3d_base.cpp:497-510`). Multisample raster is switched off around a colour clear (`:459, :465`). Arrays: an MME macro repeats the clear for every layer (`maxwell/clear_buffers.mme:5-22`). No pass concept: clears sit between draws. Ours: masked colour and stencil clears are **skipped** (check 3). | OGD 0x10f8; NXN; DK3D `maxwell/gpu_3d_base.cpp:444-512`, `engine_3d.def:305, 644` |
| 1.4 | **Conditional rendering** (`SET_RENDER_ENABLE_A..C` 0x1550-0x1558, NVN `SetRenderEnableConditional`) compares two 64-bit counters at `addr` and `addr+16` on the GPU, in command order. TotK wraps nearly every clear in it. A `TIMESTAMP` report writes 0 to the counter field. | `VK_EXT_conditional_rendering` tests one 32-bit word against zero. | NXN: honouring it fixed the black 3D scene (light-volume depth never cleared). deko3d has no conditional rendering at all (no `SET_RENDER_ENABLE` in `engine_3d.def`), so it cannot settle the compare rule. Ours: evaluated on the CPU at record time; a report from an unfinished submission counts as 0 (check 5). | OGD; NXN |
| 1.5 | **Depth mode** is runtime state: `nvnDeviceSetDepthMode` near = -w (GL, NVN default) or 0. Register `SET_VIEWPORT_Z_CLIP` (0x0d7c) `NEGATIVE_W_TO_POSITIVE_W` / `ZERO_TO_POSITIVE_W`. | Vulkan clips z < 0 unless `VK_EXT_depth_clip_control` `negativeOneToOne`. | Ryujinx infers the mode from the viewport transform, falling back to the register (`GetDepthMode`, RYU-SU). NXN: wrong mode either clips everything (black window) or puts all depth in 0.5..1 (DOF blurs the screen). Ours: `negativeOneToOne` from NVN state. DK3D programs both halves: `SetDepthMode` (`0x35F` = 0xd7c) selects the pre-transform clip range, and the viewport transform maps z to [near, far] itself: scale z = `0.5 * (far - near)` and offset z = `0.5 * (near + far)` for -1..1, scale `far - near` and offset `near` for 0..1 (`maxwell/gpu_3d_base.cpp:143-147, 336-343`). Same maths as Vulkan `negativeOneToOne`. | OGD 0x0d7c; NXN-64, NXN; DK3D `maxwell/gpu_3d_base.cpp:136-147, 321-362` |
| 1.6 | **Depth clamp / clip**: `SET_VIEWPORT_CLIP_CONTROL` (0x193c) has separate `PIXEL_MIN_Z`/`PIXEL_MAX_Z` CLIP or CLAMP and geometry-clip modes. | `depthClampEnable` also disables z clipping (unless `VK_EXT_depth_clip_enable`). RADV had a dynamic depth clamp driver bug causing TotK vertex explosions. | Ryujinx: clamp = `!(clip & DepthClampDisabled)` (RYU-SU `UpdateDepthClampState`). yuzu disabled dynamic depth clamp on affected RADV (YZ-2305, PR 10262). DK3D has one switch, `depthClampEnable`, and writes `VIEW_VOLUME_CLIP_CONTROL` (`0x64F` = 0x193c) with `0x101A` when on and `0x181D` when off (default at setup is `0x181D`); it labels the bits "todo: figure out what this actually does". Bits 3-4 (`DepthClampNear/Far`) are set in both values, bits 0-2 and 11 differ. There is no separate depth-clip toggle. The viewport near/far registers (`Viewport` array words 2-3) carry the clamp range and are swapped when far < near (`:349-350`). Vulkan clamp to [min, max] of the viewport depth matches. | OGD 0x193c; DK3D `maxwell/gpu_3d_state.cpp:42`, `gpu_3d_base.cpp:135-139, 349-350`, `engine_3d.def:621` |
| 1.7 | **Depth formats**: D24S8 is native; D24 quantises to 2^-24 everywhere in 0..1. Polygon offset units are in D24 steps for D24 targets; `SET_DEPTH_BIAS_CONTROL` (0x1110) `DEPTH_FORMAT_DEPENDENT`. | RX 9070 has no D24S8 attachment; D32F has finer steps near 0 and a per-primitive exponent-based r. EQUAL / LEQUAL tests between a pre-pass and a later pass, and decal biases, behave differently. | yuzu rescales depth-bias units when D24 is emulated as D32F; Ryujinx passes `units / 2` (register is twice the API value) (RYU-SU `UpdateDepthBiasState`). MNG: D16 load-clear 0.5 → 32767 vs fragment 0.5 → 32768 made Ultrahand/Recall classification tiles visible. Ours: D24S8 → D32_SFLOAT_S8, bias not rescaled (check 4). DK3D writes `PolygonOffsetUnits` (`0x56F` = 0x15bc) as `constantFactor * 2.0f`, clamp to `0x61F`, factor to `0x55B` (`maxwell/gpu_3d_state.cpp:148-157`), confirming the x2 register. | OGD 0x1110, 0x15bc, 0x156c; MNG `docs/how-it-works.md:57-61`; DK3D `maxwell/gpu_3d_state.cpp:154` |
| 1.8 | **Position invariance**: identical position math gives identical depth across programs (pre-pass then EQUAL / LEQUAL). | Only for outputs declared `Invariant`. | Ryujinx decorates position `Invariant` (`CodeGen/Spirv/Declarations.cs:571`) and marks float ops `NoContraction` unless `QueryHostReducedPrecision` (`CodeGen/Spirv/Instructions.cs:2047`). NXN: Odyssey ground z-fought without it; LA's foliage drawn with depth EQUAL vanished when the pre-pass failed. Ours: translator default (all NoContraction). | NXN |
| 1.9 | **Sampling a texture that is also a bound render target**: Maxwell's texture cache is not coherent with ROP writes; NVN requires `nvnCommandBufferBarrier(INVALIDATE_TEXTURE)` between writing and sampling (methods `INVALIDATE_TEXTURE_DATA_CACHE` 0x1338, `..._NO_WFI` 0x1288). Reading a different level/layer, or read-only depth while testing, is fine. | Same image as attachment and sampled in one pass is a feedback loop: undefined unless `VK_EXT_attachment_feedback_loop_layout`; on AMD DCC/HTILE-compressed data is not readable by the sampler without decompression. | yuzu: pixelated Ultrahand glow fixed with barriers on attachment feedback loops (YZ-2305, PR 10402). BotW black textures on GCN worked around with `AMD_DEBUG=nohyperz` (HTILE off) (<https://git.openpunk.com/OpenPunk/yuzu/wiki/commit/bd401539420182cbbf8bc638b042536a7e690c3f>). Ours: an NVN barrier ends the pass and inserts a full memory barrier; no detection of a sampled texture that is a current attachment (check 10). DK3D barrier recipe (`maxwell/gpu_base.cpp:49-115`): the ordering part and the cache part are separate. Ordering: Tiles = `TiledCacheBarrier` (`0x3DF`), Fragments = `FragmentBarrier` (`0x378`), Primitives = `WaitForIdle` (`0x44`), Full = gpfifo `SetReference` + new gpfifo entry with `NoPrefetch`, so later command and indirect-parameter fetch happens after everything finished. Tiles and Fragments need an implicit WFI before a cache invalidate. Caches (each opt-in): texture data `InvalidateTextureDataCache` (`0x3DD`, WFI) or `..NoWfi` (`0x4A2`); shader `InvalidateShaderCaches` (`0x369`: instruction, global data, constant); descriptors `InvalidateTextureHeaderCacheNoWfi` (`0x50A`) + `InvalidateSamplerCacheNoWfi` (`0x509`); zcull `0x4B2`; L2 gpfifo `MemOpB` `L2FlushDirty` + `L2SysmemInvalidate`. The texture-cache invalidate is its own flag; ordering alone does not refresh it. Every queue flush ends with image + shader + descriptor + L2 invalidation "to ensure the visibility of CPU updates between flushes" (`:28-47`): CPU writes into textures and descriptors reach the GPU at the next submit boundary, not mid-submit (2.2). | OGD; DK3D `maxwell/gpu_base.cpp:28-115` |
| 1.10 | **Duplicate attachments**: the same texture bound at two colour slots with write mask 0 on one does not interfere (ROP writes only enabled channels). | Tile-based or compressed attachments may store the unwritten copy over the written one. | NXN BotW G-buffer (c1 = c2, c3 = c4): leaves the duplicate slot unattached (`rt_dup_slot`). | NXN |
| 1.11 | **Per-target write masks**: `RtColorMask[i]`, or entry 0 for all when `RtColorMaskShared`. `SET_SINGLE_CT_WRITE_CONTROL` (0x0f90). A colour target with format 0 is disabled. | Per-attachment `colorWriteMask`. | RYU-SU `UpdateRtColorMask`, `IsRtEnabled` ("Colors are disabled by writing 0 to the format"). | OGD 0x0f90 |
| 1.12 | **sRGB render target views**: NVN encodes on write when the view format is sRGB over a linear texture. Maxwell also has a global `SET_SRGB_WRITE` (0x15b8). | Format of the attachment view decides; needs `MUTABLE_FORMAT`. | NXN Mario: attaching the base texture stored linear values, picture darker. Ours: RT views take the view format (`view_format`). | OGD 0x15b8; NXN |
| 1.13 | **Compressed and 3D targets**: agl's GPU BC4 encoder renders blocks through an `RGBA16UI` view, one plane of a 32×32×32 BC4 3D texture per pass. NVN renders a 3D texture slice by slice. | Needs `BLOCK_TEXEL_VIEW_COMPATIBLE` + `EXTENDED_USAGE`, `2D_ARRAY_COMPATIBLE`. | NXN shadow textures (`bcrt_attach`). yuzu: wrong block depth on 3D slices gave Gloom textures on terrain (YZ-2305, PR 10433). Already fixed here. | NXN |
| 1.14 | **Draw with no render target** (fragment shader only writes an SSBO, 1×1 viewport) runs normally. | Needs an attachment-less pass with explicit render area. | NXN `bare_dims`: cave ambient light came back. Ours: area of viewport 0 (`vk_exec.c` `resolve_rt`). | NXN |
| 1.15 | **Window origin**: NVN default lower-left (GL); TotK switches to upper-left. Y flip and scissor flip follow. | Vulkan upper-left; negative viewport height to flip. | Ryujinx flips scissor against screen height when Y-negate is on (RYU-SU `UpdateScissorState`). | NXN |
| 1.16 | **Multiple viewports / scissors** (16), selected by `ViewportIndex` output. | Needs `multiViewport` and `shaderOutputViewportIndex`. | Ours: one viewport, one scissor; differing scissors logged (`nvn_api_cmd.c`). | OGD 0x192c |
| 1.17 | **Fragment output saturation** per target: `SET_PS_SATURATE` (0x13a8) clamps output n to 0..1 or -1..1 in fixed function. NVN does not expose it (GLSLC emits `.SAT` in code). | None. | Not emulated by Ryujinx; listed so a clamp difference is not chased in the wrong place. | OGD 0x13a8 |
| 1.18 | **New memory reads as zero** (fresh pool pages); feedback effects never clear their state texture. | New image content undefined. | NXN `tex_zero_fill`. | NXN |
| 1.19 | **MSAA**: `nvnCommandBufferDownsample` resolves; depth-stencil downsamples are copies the game does itself. | `vkCmdResolveImage` colour only; integer formats pick one sample. | NXN LA: stencil lost in the half-size depth copy, no AO. | NXN |

## 2. Textures and samplers

| # | Maxwell / NVN | Vulkan / AMD | Emulators / ports | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | **Automatic block height**: NVN truncates `height_in_blocks * 1.5 / 8` before picking the GOB power of two (deko3d rounds up). Wrong H reads padding: 160×160 BC3 warp pad half black. Allocation size is the same, so size checks do not catch it. Mip levels shrink the block height while the level fits in half of it. | Opaque optimal tiling. | MNG fixed (40 SDK-measured cases, `games/totk/tests/texture_auto_layout/probe.c`). Ours: truncating form already (`runtime/nvn_tex.c`, the block-height pick). DK3D reads: height in block rows (rounded up), x 1.5, then `(h + 7) / 8` rounded up, then the largest power of two <= that, capped at 16 GOBs (`dk_image.cpp:444-447`, `pickTileSize` `:13-20`); 3D uses `depth + depth / 2` directly as the GOB count (`:451-454`); video images are fixed at 2 GOBs (`:438`). Per level, the shift drops while `unit << (shift - 1) >= level dimension` with unit 8 rows / 1 slice (`adjustTileSize` `:23-37`, used at `:89-91`), width tile is always 0. Array layers are padded to the block shrunk to the full height / depth (`alignLayerSize` `:57-72`). Every one of these matches `nvn_tex.c` except the rounding. | MNG `docs/how-it-works.md:47-53`; DK3D `dk_image.cpp:13-37, 57-72, 80-103, 436-455` |

| 2.7 | **Swizzles** per texture and per view (`TextureBuilderSetSwizzle`, `TextureViewSetSwizzle`); BotW layout captures rebuild a texture on the same storage with (1, 1, 1, R) or alpha 1. | 2.8 | **Sample dimension comes from the instruction**: a non-array sample of an array texture reads layer 0; 1,512 BotW shaders sample a cube as a cube array. | View type must match the declared type. | NXN: 2D array bound as 2D gave one pale colour (washed-out scene); cubes created as 6-layer arrays with cube / cube-array views.
