`installer/ini.py`:

```py
"""totk.ini: set the game language and keep everything else (keys and syntax as runtime/cfg.c reads them).

A new file starts from totk.ini.example, whose lines are all commented defaults. The language goes into `lang`
(a Switch language code, runtime/ov_system.c): an active `lang = ...` line is rewritten in place, else the commented
`# lang = ...` line of the example is activated, else the line is added to [language] (created at the end if
missing). Other lines, comments and line order stay as they are.
"""
import os
import re
from pathlib import Path

# runtime/ov_system.c: the codes TOTK_LANG offers. Each language appears once, under the code the game accepts.
LANGUAGES = ('ja', 'en-US', 'en-GB', 'fr', 'fr-CA', 'de', 'it', 'es', 'es-419', 'nl', 'pt', 'pt-BR', 'ru', 'ko',
             'zh-Hans', 'zh-Hant')
# Older installer builds wrote these two codes; they are read as the canonical ones and rewritten on the next install.
ALIASES = {'zh-CN': 'zh-Hans', 'zh-TW': 'zh-Hant'}
# Their text falls back to the Switch shared fonts (runtime/ov_system.c), which the installer does not extract.
NEED_SHARED_FONTS = ('ko', 'zh-Hans', 'zh-Hant')

ACTIVE = re.compile(r'^(\s*)(?:totk_)?lang(\s*=\s*)(.*?)(\s*)$', re.IGNORECASE)
COMMENTED = re.compile(r'^\s*[#;]\s*(?:totk_)?lang\s*=.*$', re.IGNORECASE)
SECTION = re.compile(r'^\s*\[(.*)\]\s*$')


def canonical_language(lang):
    """The code LANGUAGES lists for lang: an alias of an older installer build is mapped, anything else is kept."""
    return ALIASES.get(lang, lang)


def set_language(text, lang):
    """text with `lang = <lang>` (an alias written as its canonical code); see the module docstring."""
    lang = canonical_language(lang)
    lines = text.splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = ACTIVE.match(line)
        if m:
            lines[i] = f'{m.group(1)}lang{m.group(2)}{lang}'
            return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if COMMENTED.match(line):
            lines[i] = f'lang = {lang}'
            return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = SECTION.match(line)
        if m and m.group(1).strip().lower() == 'language':
            lines.insert(i + 1, f'lang = {lang}')
            return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'
    if lines and lines[-1].strip():
        lines.append('')
    lines += ['[language]', f'lang = {lang}']
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'


def get_language(text):
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = ACTIVE.match(line)
        if m:
            return m.group(3)
    return None


def write(dest, lang, example=None):
    """Write dest/totk.ini with lang; an existing file keeps its other lines. Returns the path."""
    path = Path(dest) / 'totk.ini'
    if path.is_file():
        text = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8-sig')
    elif example and Path(example).is_file():
        text = Path(example).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    else:
        text = ''
    new = set_language(text, lang)
    if path.is_file() and new == text:
        return path
    tmp = path.with_name('totk.ini.tmp')
    tmp.write_text(new, encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')
    os.replace(tmp, path)
    return path

```

`installer/launcher/launcher.c`:

```c
/* TotK-Setup.exe: starts python\pythonw.exe -m installer.gui with this exe's folder as the working directory.

   No console window. The two message strings come from the catalog (installer/text/<lang>.json, ids launcher.title and
   launcher.python_missing); tools/make_release.py writes them into launcher_text.h before it compiles this file.
   Build: llvm/bin/llvm-windres -I runtime -O coff launcher.rc -o launcher_rc.o, then
   llvm/bin/clang -O2 -mwindows launcher.c launcher_rc.o -o TotK-Setup.exe */
#include <windows.h>
#include <wchar.h>

#include "launcher_text.h"

#define LANGID_RUSSIAN 0x19
#define PATH_CHARS (MAX_PATH * 2)

static void fail(void)
{
    int russian = (GetUserDefaultUILanguage() & 0x3ff) == LANGID_RUSSIAN;
    MessageBoxW(NULL, russian ? LAUNCHER_PYTHON_MISSING_RU : LAUNCHER_PYTHON_MISSING_EN,
                russian ? LAUNCHER_TITLE_RU : LAUNCHER_TITLE_EN, MB_OK | MB_ICONERROR);
}

int WINAPI WinMain(HINSTANCE instance, HINSTANCE previous, LPSTR command_line, int show)
{
    wchar_t folder[PATH_CHARS], python[PATH_CHARS], command[PATH_CHARS + 64];
    DWORD n = GetModuleFileNameW(NULL, folder, PATH_CHARS);
    STARTUPINFOW si = { sizeof si };
    PROCESS_INFORMATION pi;
    (void)instance; (void)previous; (void)command_line; (void)show;
    if (n == 0 || n >= PATH_CHARS) { fail(); return 1; }
    while (n > 0 && folder[n - 1] != L'\\') n--;
    folder[n > 0 ? n - 1 : 0] = 0;
    if (swprintf(python, PATH_CHARS, L"%ls\\python\\pythonw.exe", folder) < 0 ||
        GetFileAttributesW(python) == INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES) { fail(); return 1; }
    if (swprintf(command, PATH_CHARS + 64, L"\"%ls\" -m installer.gui", python) < 0) { fail(); return 1; }
    if (!CreateProcessW(python, command, NULL, NULL, FALSE, 0, NULL, folder, &si, &pi)) { fail(); return 1; }
    CloseHandle(pi.hThread);
    CloseHandle(pi.hProcess);
    return 0;
}
```

`installer/layout.py`:

```py
"""Where the installer finds what it runs: the one place that maps the release folder and a repository checkout.

Release (docs/installer.md "Release layout"), root = the unpacked folder:

    python/python.exe       runs every tool (numpy, lz4, cryptography, compression.zstd); its ._pth puts .., ../tools
                            and ../recomp on sys.path, so `python -m installer` imports from the release folder
    recomp/, tools/         the lifter and the scripts; recomp/patches-<v>.txt, tools/data/expected-v<version>.json for
                            each supported update (SUPPORTED)
    llvm/                   llvm-mingw (bin/clang.exe)
    runtime/                libtotkrt.a, the headers, install-side sources (romfs.c, patches.c, ov_zstd.c) and totk.ico; runtime/deps/ holds
                            include/ + lib/ of Vulkan, SDL3, Opus, libvpx and VMA (build_game.py --deps)
    bin/                    totk_xlate.exe (+ totk_xlate.id), hactool.exe, ninja.exe, SDL3.dll, libopus-0.dll
    data/shader_list.tsv    the MacNativeGames shader list
    totk.ini.example
    VERSION                 the release version, one line
    temp/                   the default temp folder (created)

Dev mode, root = a repository checkout (no python/python.exe): build/py314-embed/py/python.exe (the embeddable
Python the release ships, with the same packages), else this Python; toolchain/llvm-mingw-*/ and toolchain/deps-mingw;
runtime/ as the sources with build/install-rtlib/libtotkrt.a (tools/build_game.py --make-runtime-lib --out
build/install-rtlib); MSYS2 UCRT64 ninja.exe; toolchain/hactool; build/xlate/totk_xlate.exe; the shader list from
refs/MacNativeGames; build/install-temp. The version is VERSION with -dev and the commit: 0.1.0-dev+973c626.
"""
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

EXE = '.exe' if os.name == 'nt' else ''
UCRT = Path(r'C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin')
SUPPORTED = ('1.2.1', '1.4.3')   # updates the installer builds; the check identifies the player's by hash


def version_tag(version):
    """'1.4.3' -> 'v143': the version name of build_game.py, make_romfs_patches.py and the patch tables."""
    return 'v' + version.replace('.', '')


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Layout:
    root: Path
    dev: bool
    release: str
    python: Path          # runs the tools
    tools: Path
    recomp: Path
    llvm: Path            # llvm-mingw tree
    deps: Path            # include/ and lib/ for the link
    runtime: Path         # runtime headers and install-side sources
    runtime_lib: Path     # libtotkrt.a
    ninja: Path
    hactool: Path
    xlate: Path           # totk_xlate.exe; a totk_xlate.id beside it is copied too
    dlls: tuple = field(default_factory=tuple)
    shader_list: Path | None = None   # None: dev, read from refs/MacNativeGames through git
    ini_example: Path | None = None
    temp: Path | None = None

    @property
    def clang(self):
        return self.llvm / 'bin' / ('clang' + EXE)

    def patches(self, version):
        """The code patch table for recomp/gen.py."""
        return self.recomp / f'patches-{version_tag(version)}.txt'

    def expected(self, version):
        """The expected hashes of the update."""
        return self.tools / 'data' / f'expected-v{version}.json'

    def missing(self):
        """Paths the steps need that do not exist."""
        need = [self.python, self.tools / 'extract.py', self.tools / 'build_game.py', self.tools / 'prepare_shaders.py',
                self.tools / 'pack_shader_cache.py', self.tools / 'make_romfs_patches.py', self.tools / 'ultrawide_layout.py',
                self.recomp / 'gen.py',
                self.clang,
                self.deps / 'include', self.deps / 'lib', self.runtime, self.runtime_lib, self.ninja, self.hactool,
                self.xlate, *self.dlls, *(f(v) for v in SUPPORTED for f in (self.patches, self.expected))]
        if self.shader_list:
            need.append(self.shader_list)
        return [str(p) for p in need if not p.exists()]


def is_release(root):
    return (root / 'python' / ('python' + EXE)).is_file()


def release_layout(root):
    version = root / 'VERSION'
    return Layout(
        root=root, dev=False,
        release=version.read_text(encoding='utf-8').strip() if version.is_file() else 'unknown',
        python=root / 'python' / ('python' + EXE),
        tools=root / 'tools', recomp=root / 'recomp',
        llvm=root / 'llvm', deps=root / 'runtime' / 'deps', runtime=root / 'runtime',
        runtime_lib=root / 'runtime' / 'libtotkrt.a',
        ninja=root / 'bin' / ('ninja' + EXE), hactool=root / 'bin' / ('hactool' + EXE),
        xlate=root / 'bin' / ('totk_xlate' + EXE),
        dlls=(root / 'bin' / 'SDL3.dll', root / 'bin' / 'libopus-0.dll'),
        shader_list=root / 'data' / 'shader_list.tsv', ini_example=root / 'totk.ini.example', temp=root / 'temp')


def dev_layout(root):
    commit = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(root), 'rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'], capture_output=True,
                            text=True).stdout.strip()
    embed = root / 'build' / 'py314-embed' / 'py' / ('python' + EXE)
    trees = sorted(p.parent.parent for p in (root / 'toolchain').glob('llvm-mingw-*/llvm-mingw-*/bin/clang' + EXE))
    deps = root / 'toolchain' / 'deps-mingw'
    semver = (root / 'VERSION').read_text(encoding='utf-8').strip()
    return Layout(
        root=root, dev=True, release=f'{semver}-dev+{commit or "unknown"}',
        python=embed if embed.is_file() else Path(sys.executable),
        tools=root / 'tools', recomp=root / 'recomp',
        llvm=trees[-1] if trees else root / 'toolchain' / 'llvm-mingw-missing', deps=deps,
        runtime=root / 'runtime', runtime_lib=root / 'build' / 'install-rtlib' / 'libtotkrt.a',
        ninja=UCRT / ('ninja' + EXE), hactool=root / 'toolchain' / 'hactool' / ('hactool' + EXE),
        xlate=root / 'build' / 'xlate' / ('totk_xlate' + EXE),
        dlls=tuple(sorted((deps / 'bin').glob('*.dll'))),
        shader_list=None, ini_example=root / 'totk.ini.example', temp=root / 'build' / 'install-temp')


def find(root=None):
    """The layout of root (default: the folder above this package)."""
    root = Path(root or Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent).resolve()
    return release_layout(root) if is_release(root) else dev_layout(root)
```

`installer/runner.py`:

```py
"""Which steps run, in what order, and the bookkeeping around them: fresh install, resume and update are one rule.

Each step has a key: a fingerprint of everything its output depends on, computed before anything runs (a step's key
includes the keys of the steps it reads from, so a change upstream reaches every step below it). A step is skipped
when totk-install.json records it with the same key and its output still matches the record (Step.current, cheap).
Otherwise it runs. A transient step (its output lives in the temp folder and only the next step reads it) runs only
when the next step runs. `always` steps (check, cleanup) run every time.

Update mode is the same rule with a newer release: the extraction's key depends only on the expected hashes, so a
release that changes the lifter or the runtime keeps romfs/ and exefs/ and rebuilds from lift on. Before keeping the
output of a step recorded by another release (or with --verify), the check step calls Step.verify (expensive: the full
RomFS hash); a mismatch makes the step run again.

A failed or cancelled run leaves the finished steps recorded; the next run starts at the first step that is not.
"""
import datetime
import traceback

from . import state as statefile


class InstallError(Exception):
    """A failure with a message id (installer/text/en.json) and its parameters."""

    def __init__(self, id, **params):
        super().__init__(id)
        self.id, self.params = id, params


class Step:
    id = ''
    transient = False
    always = False

    def key(self, ctx):
        """Fingerprint of the step's inputs; may read ctx.keys of earlier steps."""
        return ''

    def current(self, ctx, record):
        """True when the recorded output is still in place (cheap checks only)."""
        return True

    def verify(self, ctx, record):
        """True when the recorded output passes the full check (hashes); called before keeping another release's
        output."""
        return True

    def run(self, ctx):
        """Do the work. Returns fields to record with the step."""
        return {}


class Context:
    def __init__(self, layout, dest, temp, reporter, options, state=None, verify=False):
        self.layout, self.dest, self.temp, self.reporter, self.options = layout, dest, temp, reporter, options
        self.state = state or statefile.empty(layout.release)
        self.verify = verify
        self.mode = 'install' if state is None else 'resume' if state.get('release') == layout.release else 'update'
        self.keys, self.runs, self.reasons, self.steps, self.forced = {}, {}, {}, [], set()

    def record(self, step_id):
        return self.state['steps'].get(step_id)

    def will_run(self, step_id):
        return self.runs.get(step_id, False)

    def save(self):
        self.dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        statefile.save(self.dest, self.state)

    def plan(self, forced=()):
        """Fill keys (once), runs and reasons. forced: step ids that must run."""
        if not self.keys:
            for s in self.steps:
                self.keys[s.id] = s.key(self)
        for s in self.steps:
            rec = self.record(s.id)
            if s.always or s.id in forced:
                self.runs[s.id] = True
            else:
                self.runs[s.id] = not (rec and rec.get('key') == self.keys[s.id] and s.current(self, rec))
            self.reasons[s.id] = '' if self.runs[s.id] else 'current'
        for i in range(len(self.steps) - 2, -1, -1):
            s, after = self.steps[i], self.steps[i + 1]
            if s.transient and self.runs[s.id] and not self.runs[after.id]:
                self.runs[s.id], self.reasons[s.id] = False, 'not_needed'
        self.forced = set(forced)

    def verify_kept(self, progress_step):
        """Full check of every kept step output that another release recorded (or of all with --verify). A step that
        fails it is planned to run. Returns the ids that failed."""
        failed = []
        for s in self.steps:
            rec = self.record(s.id)
            if self.runs[s.id] or self.reasons[s.id] != 'current' or s.always:
                continue
            if not (self.verify or rec.get('release') != self.layout.release):
                continue
            if not s.verify(self, rec):
                failed.append(s.id)
        if failed:
            for f in failed:
                self.reporter.warning('state.output_changed', step=f)
            self.plan(self.forced | set(failed))
        return failed


def now_utc():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')


def run_steps(steps, ctx):
    """Run the plan. Returns 'ok', 'failed' or 'cancelled'; events and the log say why."""
    rep = ctx.reporter
    ctx.steps = steps
    current = None
    try:
        ctx.plan()
        rep.emit('plan', run=[s.id for s in steps if ctx.runs[s.id]],
                 skip={s.id: ctx.reasons[s.id] for s in steps if not ctx.runs[s.id]})
        for s in steps:
            if not ctx.runs[s.id]:
                rep.step(s.id, 'skipped', reason=ctx.reasons[s.id])
                continue
            current = s.id
            rep.step(s.id, 'started')
            t0 = rep.elapsed()
            fields = s.run(ctx) or {}
            seconds = round(rep.elapsed() - t0, 1)
            if not s.always:
                ctx.state['steps'][s.id] = {'key': ctx.keys[s.id], 'release': ctx.layout.release,
                                            'finished': now_utc(), 'seconds': seconds, **fields}
            ctx.save()   # the first save, after the check, creates the install folder
            rep.step(s.id, 'done', seconds=seconds)
            current = None
        ctx.state['release'] = ctx.layout.release
        ctx.save()
        return 'ok'
    except InstallError as e:
        rep.error(e.id, e.params, step=current)
        return 'failed'
    except statefile.StateError as e:
        rep.error(e.id, {'path': str(e.path)}, step=current)
        return 'failed'
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        rep.log(f'cancelled during {current}')
        return 'cancelled'
    except Exception as e:
        rep.log(traceback.format_exc())
        rep.error('internal', {'exception': type(e).__name__, 'detail': str(e)}, step=current)
        return 'failed'

```

`installer/state.py`:

```py
"""totk-install.json in the install folder: what built it and which steps finished.

    {"format": 1, "release": "...", "lang": "en-US",
     "inputs": {"base": {"name", "size", "sha256"}, "update": {...}},
     "steps": {"<step>": {"key": "<input fingerprint>", "release": "...", "finished": "<UTC time>", "seconds": 12.3,
                          ...the step's own fields}}}

A step's key fingerprints everything its output depends on (runner.py), so a step whose recorded key equals the
current one and whose output still checks out is not run again. The file is replaced atomically after each step.
No key value or keys file content is ever stored.
"""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

NAME = 'totk-install.json'
FORMAT = 1


class StateError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, id, path):
        super().__init__(id)
        self.id, self.path = id, path


def empty(release):
    return {'format': FORMAT, 'release': release, 'inputs': {}, 'steps': {}}


def load(dest):
    """The state of dest, or None when the folder has none. StateError for an unreadable or newer file."""
    path = Path(dest) / NAME
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        raise StateError('state.unreadable', path) from None
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data.get('steps'), dict):
        raise StateError('state.unreadable', path)
    if data.get('format', 0) > FORMAT:
        raise StateError('state.newer_format', path)
    return data


def save(dest, data):
    path = Path(dest) / NAME
    tmp = path.with_name(NAME + '.tmp')
    with open(tmp, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
        f.write('\n')
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
    os.replace(tmp, path)

```

`installer/steps.py`:

```py
"""The six setup steps of docs/installer.md: check, extract, lift, compile, prepare, cleanup.

Extraction runs in this process through tools/extract.py (the package's sibling tools/, which ships with it); lift,
compile and prepare run the bundled Python on recomp/gen.py, tools/build_game.py, tools/make_romfs_patches.py and
tools/prepare_shaders.py, whose output goes to <temp>/logs/<step>-<tool>.log and is read for progress. No Win32 call
here: the host check is a small C program built with the bundled clang (hostcheck.c).

Install folder: exefs/, romfs/ (romfs.bin, index.json), profile/, totk.exe and its DLLs, romfs-index.bin,
romfs-patches/, romfs-patches-xbox/, totk_xlate.exe, the shader state of totk.exe --prepare-shaders, totk.ini,
totk-install.json.
Temp folder (<temp>/<dest name>-<hash>): check/ (ExeFS of both inputs, the host check), gen/ (C), build/ (objects),
logs/ (kept by the cleanup).
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from pathlib import Path

from . import ini
from .layout import EXE, SUPPORTED, version_tag
from .runner import InstallError, Step

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / 'tools'))
import extract  # noqa: E402
import shader_list  # noqa: E402
from extract_exefs import (common_tickets, container_entries, load_keys, nca_ctr_key, nca_inventory,  # noqa: E402
                           program_nca)

GiB = 1 << 30
DEST_EXTRA = 4 * GiB      # beside the RomFS: shader and pipeline caches (about 2 GB), exefs, totk.exe, seed files
TEMP_NEED = 3 * GiB       # generated C (about 0.9 GB) and objects
HOSTCHECK = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'hostcheck.c'
STAMP = '.install-key'


# ---- helpers

def file_sha256(path, progress=None):
    """SHA-256 hex of a file; progress(done, total) after each block."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    total = path.stat().st_size
    done = 0
    with open(path, 'rb', buffering=0) as f:
        buf = bytearray(8 << 20)
        view = memoryview(buf)
        while n := f.readinto(buf):
            h.update(view[:n])
            done += n
            if progress:
                progress(done, total)
    return h.hexdigest()


def fingerprint(*parts):
    """SHA-256 over strings and the contents of files and directory trees (a missing path counts as missing)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for p in parts:
        if isinstance(p, Path):
            if p.is_dir():
                for f in sorted(p.rglob('*')):
                    if f.is_file() and '__pycache__' not in f.parts:
                        h.update(f.relative_to(p).as_posix().encode() + b'\0' + bytes.fromhex(file_sha256(f)))
            elif p.is_file():
                h.update(p.name.encode() + b'\0' + bytes.fromhex(file_sha256(p)))
            else:
                h.update(b'missing\0' + p.name.encode())
        else:
            h.update(str(p).encode())
        h.update(b'\1')
    return h.hexdigest()


def remove(path):
    if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink():
        shutil.rmtree(path)
    elif path.exists() or path.is_symlink():
        path.unlink()


def replace_file(src, dst):
    """Copy src over dst through a temporary name, so a cancelled copy never leaves half a file under dst's name."""
    tmp = dst.with_name(dst.name + '.tmp')
    shutil.copy2(src, tmp)
    os.replace(tmp, dst)


def kill_tree(proc):
    if proc.poll() is not None:
        return
    if os.name == 'nt':
        subprocess.run(['taskkill', '/T', '/F', '/PID', str(proc.pid)], capture_output=True)
    else:
        proc.kill()


def run_tool(ctx, step, script, args, parse=None, cwd=None):
    """Run a tool script with the bundled Python. Its output goes to <temp>/logs/<step>-<script>.log and, line by line,
    to parse(line). Returns (exit code, log path)."""
    logs = ctx.temp / 'logs'
    logs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    log = logs / f'{step}-{Path(script).stem}.log'
    command = [str(ctx.layout.python), '-c', extract.RUN_SCRIPT, str(script), *map(str, args)]
    ctx.reporter.log('run ' + ' '.join(command[3:]))
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONUNBUFFERED='1', PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8')
    with open(log, 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='\n') as out:
        proc = subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, cwd=cwd or ctx.layout.root,
                                env=env, text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace', bufsize=1)
        try:
            for line in proc.stdout:
                out.write(line)
                if parse:
                    parse(line.rstrip())
            code = proc.wait()
        except BaseException:
            kill_tree(proc)
            raise
    ctx.reporter.log(f'{Path(script).name}: exit code {code}; output in {log}')
    return code, log


def free_bytes(path):
    """Free bytes on the disk of path (its nearest existing parent) and that parent's device."""
    p = Path(path)
    while not p.exists():
        p = p.parent
    return shutil.disk_usage(p).free, os.stat(p).st_dev


def raise_if_damaged(error, name, path):
    """InstallError check.input_damaged when a reader's ValueError says the file's data fails its hashes or ends early
    (extract.DAMAGE_TEXT)."""
    if extract.DAMAGE_TEXT.search(str(error)):
        raise InstallError('check.input_damaged', input=name, path=str(path), detail=str(error)) from None


def game_version(ctx):
    """The update this install is built from: what the check identified, else the recorded one (an install made before
    1.4.3 support records none: 1.2.1)."""
    return ctx.state.get('version', SUPPORTED[0])


def expected_update(ctx):
    return extract.load_expected()[game_version(ctx)]


def shader_list_text(layout):
    if layout.shader_list:
        return layout.shader_list.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    try:
        return shader_list.history(layout.root / 'refs' / 'MacNativeGames')
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        raise InstallError('prepare.shader_list_missing')


class Watch(threading.Thread):
    """Polls a measure() of bytes written while a long call runs and reports it as progress."""

    def __init__(self, reporter, step):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self.reporter, self.step = reporter, step
        self.phase, self.measure, self.total = None, None, None
        self.stopped = threading.Event()

    def set(self, phase, measure=None, total=None):
        self.phase, self.measure, self.total = phase, measure, total
        self.reporter.progress(self.step, phase, 0 if total else None, total, 'bytes' if total else None, force=True)

    def run(self):
        while not self.stopped.wait(1.0):
            phase, measure, total = self.phase, self.measure, self.total
            if phase and measure:
                try:
                    done = min(measure(), total)
                except OSError:
                    continue
                self.reporter.progress(self.step, phase, done, total, 'bytes')

    def stop(self):
        self.stopped.set()


def size_of(paths):
    return sum(p.stat().st_size for p in paths if p.is_file())


# ---- 1. check

class Check(Step):
    id = 'check'
    always = True

    def run(self, ctx):
        layout, rep, dest = ctx.layout, ctx.reporter, ctx.dest
        missing = layout.missing()
        if missing:
            raise InstallError('check.release_incomplete', paths=missing[:5])
        if dest.exists() and not dest.is_dir():
            raise InstallError('check.dest_not_folder', path=str(dest))
        if ctx.mode == 'install' and dest.is_dir() and any(dest.iterdir()):
            raise InstallError('check.dest_not_empty', path=str(dest))
        lang = ini.canonical_language(ctx.options.lang or ctx.state.get('lang'))
        if not lang:
            raise InstallError('check.lang_missing')
        if lang not in ini.LANGUAGES:
            raise InstallError('check.lang_unknown', lang=lang, known=', '.join(ini.LANGUAGES))
        if lang in ini.NEED_SHARED_FONTS:
            rep.warning('warn.lang_needs_fonts', lang=lang)
        ctx.lang = lang
        ctx.temp.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        rep.progress('check', 'host', force=True)
        self.host(ctx)
        rep.progress('check', 'verify', force=True)
        ctx.verify_kept('check')
        ncas = 0
        if ctx.will_run('extract'):
            rep.progress('check', 'inputs', force=True)
            ncas = self.inputs(ctx)
        self.space(ctx, ncas)
        if ctx.will_run('extract'):
            rep.progress('check', 'versions', force=True)
            self.versions(ctx)
        return {}

    def host(self, ctx):
        layout, work = ctx.layout, ctx.temp / 'check'
        work.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        exe = work / ('hostcheck' + EXE)
        command = [str(layout.clang), '-O1', str(HOSTCHECK), '-I', str(layout.deps / 'include'), '-o', str(exe)]
        if os.name != 'nt':
            command.append('-ldl')
        r = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace')
        if r.returncode:
            ctx.reporter.log(r.stdout + r.stderr)
            raise InstallError('check.toolchain_broken', detail=(r.stderr or r.stdout).strip()[-400:])
        r = subprocess.run([str(exe)], capture_output=True, text=True, errors='replace')
        try:
            host = json.loads(r.stdout)
        except ValueError:
            raise InstallError('check.host_probe_failed', code=r.returncode) from None
        ctx.reporter.log(f'host: {r.stdout.strip()}')
        if not host['x86_64_v3']:
            raise InstallError('check.cpu_no_avx2')
        if not host['loader']:
            raise InstallError('check.vulkan_missing')
        devices = host['devices']
        if not devices:
            raise InstallError('check.vulkan_no_device')
        if not any(tuple(d['api'][:2]) >= (1, 3) for d in devices):
            raise InstallError('check.vulkan_too_old',
                               devices=', '.join(f'{d["name"]} ({d["api"][0]}.{d["api"][1]})' for d in devices))
        ctx.host = host

    def inputs(self, ctx):
        """Open both files with the keys as the extraction will. Returns the bytes of both Program NCAs."""
        o = ctx.options
        for name in ('base', 'update', 'keys'):
            path = getattr(o, name)
            if not path:
                raise InstallError('check.inputs_needed')
            if not Path(path).is_file():
                raise InstallError('check.input_missing', input=name, path=str(path))
        try:
            keys = load_keys(Path(o.keys))
        except (ValueError, OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
            raise InstallError('check.keys_unreadable') from None
        if 'header_key' not in keys:
            raise InstallError('check.keys_no_header_key')
        total = 0
        for name, is_update in (('base', False), ('update', True)):
            path = Path(getattr(o, name))
            with path.open('rb') as f:
                total += self.open_input(f, path, keys, name, is_update)
        del keys
        return total

    @staticmethod
    def open_input(f, path, keys, name, is_update):
        try:
            kind, entries = container_entries(f, path.stat().st_size)
        except ValueError as e:
            raise_if_damaged(e, name, path)
            raise InstallError('check.not_game_file', input=name) from None
        if is_update and kind != 'nsp':
            raise InstallError('check.update_not_nsp')
        try:
            tickets = common_tickets(f, entries)
        except ValueError as e:
            if 'Personalized' in str(e):
                raise InstallError('check.ticket_personalized', input=name) from None
            raise_if_damaged(e, name, path)
            raise InstallError('check.file_unreadable', input=name, detail=str(e)) from None
        try:
            records = nca_inventory(f, entries, keys)
        except ValueError as e:
            if 'NCA3' in str(e):
                raise InstallError('check.keys_wrong', input=name) from None
            raise_if_damaged(e, name, path)
            raise InstallError('check.file_unreadable', input=name, detail=str(e)) from None
        try:
            record, header = program_nca(records, update=is_update)
        except ValueError as e:
            if is_update and 'BKTR' in str(e):
                raise InstallError('check.update_is_base') from None
            raise InstallError('check.update_not_totk' if is_update else 'check.base_not_totk', detail=str(e)) from None
        try:
            nca_ctr_key(header, keys, tickets)
        except ValueError as e:
            if 'ticket' in str(e):
                raise InstallError('check.ticket_missing', input=name) from None
            raise InstallError('check.keys_too_old', input=name,
                               generation=max(header[0x206], header[0x220])) from None
        return record['size']

    def space(self, ctx, ncas):
        dest_need = temp_need = 0
        if ctx.will_run('extract'):
            # the update is identified after this estimate: the larger RomFS of the supported ones
            dest_need += max(extract.load_expected()[v]['romfs']['size'] for v in SUPPORTED) + ncas
            romfs = ctx.dest / 'romfs' / 'romfs.bin'
            if romfs.is_file():   # a resumed extraction replaces it
                dest_need -= romfs.stat().st_size
        if ctx.will_run('prepare') or ctx.will_run('extract'):
            dest_need += DEST_EXTRA
        if ctx.will_run('lift') or ctx.will_run('compile'):
            temp_need += TEMP_NEED
        dest_free, dest_dev = free_bytes(ctx.dest)
        temp_free, temp_dev = free_bytes(ctx.temp)
        ctx.reporter.log(f'space: install folder needs {dest_need / GiB:.1f} GiB of {dest_free / GiB:.1f} free, '
                         f'temp folder {temp_need / GiB:.1f} GiB of {temp_free / GiB:.1f}')
        if dest_dev == temp_dev:
            dest_need += temp_need
            temp_need = 0
        ctx.reporter.emit('space', dest=str(ctx.dest), need=dest_need, free=dest_free, temp=str(ctx.temp),
                          temp_need=temp_need, temp_free=temp_free, same_disk=dest_dev == temp_dev)
        for path, need, free in ((ctx.dest, dest_need, dest_free), (ctx.temp, temp_need, temp_free)):
            if need > free:
                raise InstallError('check.disk_space', path=str(path), need_gb=round(need / 1e9, 1),
                                   free_gb=round(free / 1e9, 1))

    def versions(self, ctx):
        """Extract both ExeFS into the temp folder (verifying every block) and identify the versions by hash."""
        o, work = ctx.options, ctx.temp / 'check'
        logs = ctx.temp / 'logs'
        logs.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        versions = extract.load_expected()
        for name, is_update in (('base', False), ('update', True)):
            out = work / name
            remove(out)
            try:
                extract.extract_exefs(Path(getattr(o, name)), Path(o.keys), out, logs, update=is_update)
            except extract.DamagedFile as e:
                raise InstallError('check.input_damaged', input=name, path=str(e.path), detail=e.detail) from None
            except ValueError:
                raise InstallError('check.exefs_failed', input=name, log=str(logs / f'extract_exefs-{name}.log')) \
                    from None
        problems = extract.exefs_problems(work / 'base' / 'exefs', versions['1.0.0'])
        if problems:
            raise InstallError('check.base_wrong_version', modules=', '.join(problems))
        try:
            found = extract.identify_update(work / 'update' / 'exefs', versions)['display_version']
        except ValueError:
            found = 'unknown'
        if found not in SUPPORTED:
            raise InstallError('check.update_wrong_version', found=found, wanted=' / '.join(SUPPORTED))
        if found != game_version(ctx):   # another update than the recorded one: every step builds again from it
            ctx.reporter.log(f'check: update {found} (recorded {game_version(ctx)})')
            ctx.state['version'] = found
            ctx.keys = {}
            ctx.plan(ctx.forced | {'extract', 'lift', 'compile', 'prepare'})
        ctx.state['version'] = found


# ---- 2. extract

class Extract(Step):
    id = 'extract'

    def key(self, ctx):
        # The output is whatever matches the expected hashes, whichever files and tools produced it.
        return fingerprint('extract-1', ctx.layout.expected(game_version(ctx)))

    def current(self, ctx, record):
        # Another update file than the recorded one (1.2.1 -> 1.4.3) extracts again; the check then identifies it.
        update, known = getattr(ctx.options, 'update', None), ctx.state['inputs'].get('update')
        if update and known and Path(update).is_file():
            st = Path(update).stat()
            if (st.st_size, st.st_mtime_ns) != (known.get('size'), known.get('mtime_ns')) \
                    and file_sha256(Path(update)) != known.get('sha256'):
                return False
        expected = expected_update(ctx)
        romfs = ctx.dest / 'romfs'
        if extract.exefs_problems(ctx.dest / 'exefs', expected) or not extract.romfs_verified(romfs, expected):
            return False
        st = (romfs / 'romfs.bin').stat()
        return st.st_size == record.get('romfs_size') and st.st_mtime_ns == record.get('romfs_mtime_ns')

    def verify(self, ctx, record):
        image = ctx.dest / 'romfs' / 'romfs.bin'
        rep = ctx.reporter
        digest = file_sha256(image, lambda d, t: rep.progress('check', 'verify_romfs', d, t, 'bytes'))
        return digest == expected_update(ctx)['romfs']['sha256']

    def run(self, ctx):
        o, dest, rep = ctx.options, ctx.dest, ctx.reporter
        expected = expected_update(ctx)
        base, update, keys = Path(o.base), Path(o.update), Path(o.keys)
        inputs = {}
        for name, path in (('base', base), ('update', update)):
            known = ctx.state['inputs'].get(name, {})
            st = path.stat()
            if known.get('size') == st.st_size and known.get('mtime_ns') == st.st_mtime_ns and known.get('sha256'):
                inputs[name] = known
                continue
            digest = file_sha256(path, lambda d, t, n=name: rep.progress('extract', 'hash_' + n, d, t, 'bytes'))
            inputs[name] = {'name': path.name, 'size': st.st_size, 'mtime_ns': st.st_mtime_ns, 'sha256': digest}
        ctx.state['inputs'] = inputs
        ctx.save()

        dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for stale in dest.glob('update-merge-*'):   # a killed merge leaves its NCA copies (and key copies) behind
            remove(stale)
        rep.progress('extract', 'exefs', force=True)
        staged = ctx.temp / 'check' / 'update' / 'exefs'
        if not staged.is_dir():
            remove(ctx.temp / 'check' / 'update')
            try:
                extract.extract_exefs(update, keys, ctx.temp / 'check' / 'update', ctx.temp / 'logs', update=True)
            except extract.DamagedFile as e:
                raise InstallError('check.input_damaged', input='update', path=str(e.path), detail=e.detail) from None
            except ValueError:
                raise InstallError('check.exefs_failed', input='update',
                                   log=str(ctx.temp / 'logs' / 'extract_exefs-update.log')) from None
        remove(dest / 'exefs')
        shutil.move(staged, dest / 'exefs')
        problems = extract.exefs_problems(dest / 'exefs', expected)
        if problems:
            raise InstallError('extract.exefs_mismatch', version=game_version(ctx), modules=', '.join(problems))
        if extract.sha256(dest / 'exefs' / 'main.npdm') != expected['exefs_sha256']['main.npdm']:
            rep.warning('warn.npdm_differs', version=game_version(ctx))

        romfs = dest / 'romfs'
        if self.id in ctx.forced:
            remove(romfs)   # the full hash failed: index.json still claims the extraction's hash
        if not extract.romfs_verified(romfs, expected):
            self.merge(ctx, base, update, keys, romfs, expected)
        report = json.loads((romfs / 'index.json').read_text())
        if report['romfs_size'] != expected['romfs']['size'] or report['romfs_sha256'] != expected['romfs']['sha256']:
            raise InstallError('extract.romfs_mismatch', version=game_version(ctx), size=report['romfs_size'],
                               sha256=report['romfs_sha256'][:16])
        (dest / 'profile').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        st = (romfs / 'romfs.bin').stat()
        return {'romfs_size': st.st_size, 'romfs_mtime_ns': st.st_mtime_ns}

    def merge(self, ctx, base, update, keys, romfs, expected):
        dest, logs = ctx.dest, ctx.temp / 'logs'
        ncas = extract.merge_space(base, update, keys)
        watch = Watch(ctx.reporter, 'extract')

        def phase(name):
            if name == 'copy':
                watch.set('copy', lambda: size_of(dest.glob('update-merge-*/*.nca')), ncas)
            elif name == 'merge':
                watch.set('merge', lambda: size_of(dest.glob('update-merge-*/result/romfs.bin')),
                          expected['romfs']['size'])
            else:
                watch.set(name)

        watch.start()
        try:
            extract.merge_update_romfs(base, update, keys, ctx.layout.hactool, romfs, logs, phase=phase)
        except extract.DamagedFile as e:
            raise InstallError('check.input_damaged', input='base' if e.path == base else 'update', path=str(e.path),
                               detail=e.detail) from None
        except ValueError as e:
            raise InstallError('extract.romfs_merge_failed', detail=str(e), log=str(logs / 'merge_romfs-'
                                                                                     f'{dest.name}.log')) from None
        finally:
            watch.stop()


# ---- 3. lift

EMITTED = re.compile(r'^emitted (\d+)/(\d+) chunks')
DISCOVERED = re.compile(r'^(\w+): \d+ functions \(.*discovery')


class Lift(Step):
    id = 'lift'
    transient = True

    def key(self, ctx):
        return fingerprint('lift-1', ctx.keys['extract'], ctx.layout.recomp, ctx.layout.patches(game_version(ctx)))

    def current(self, ctx, record):
        gen = ctx.temp / 'gen'
        stamp = gen / STAMP
        return (gen / 'layout.json').is_file() and stamp.is_file() and stamp.read_text().strip() == ctx.keys['lift']

    def run(self, ctx):
        layout, rep, gen = ctx.layout, ctx.reporter, ctx.temp / 'gen'
        remove(gen)
        rep.progress('lift', 'discover', force=True)

        def parse(line):
            m = EMITTED.match(line)
            if m:
                rep.progress('lift', 'emit', int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), 'chunks')

        code, log = run_tool(ctx, 'lift', layout.recomp / 'gen.py',
                             ['--exefs', ctx.dest / 'exefs', '--out', gen, '--patches', layout.patches(game_version(ctx))], parse)
        if code:
            raise InstallError('lift.failed', code=code, log=str(log))
        (gen / STAMP).write_text(ctx.keys['lift'] + '\n')
        return {}


# ---- 4. compile

NINJA_LINE = re.compile(r'^\[(\d+)/(\d+)\] ')


class Compile(Step):
    id = 'compile'

    def key(self, ctx):
        layout = ctx.layout
        clang = subprocess.run([str(layout.clang), '--version'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        tools = [layout.tools / n for n in ('build_game.py', 'romfs_index.py', 'check_content.py')]
        return fingerprint('compile-1', ctx.keys['lift'], layout.runtime, layout.runtime_lib, layout.deps, *tools,
                           clang, *[d.name for d in layout.dlls])

    def current(self, ctx, record):
        exe = ctx.dest / ('totk' + EXE)
        if not exe.is_file() or not (ctx.dest / 'romfs-index.bin').is_file():
            return False
        if not all((ctx.dest / d.name).is_file() for d in ctx.layout.dlls):
            return False
        return file_sha256(exe) == record.get('exe_sha256')

    def run(self, ctx):
        layout, rep, dest = ctx.layout, ctx.reporter, ctx.dest
        build = ctx.temp / 'build'
        phase = ['compile']

        def parse(line):
            m = NINJA_LINE.match(line)
            if m:
                rep.progress('compile', phase[0], int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), 'objects')
            elif line.startswith('compile: '):
                phase[0] = 'link'
                rep.progress('compile', 'link', force=True)

        rep.progress('compile', 'compile', force=True)
        code, log = run_tool(ctx, 'compile', layout.tools / 'build_game.py', [
            '--gen', ctx.temp / 'gen', '--out', build, '--toolchain', layout.llvm, '--deps', layout.deps,
            '--runtime', layout.runtime, '--runtime-lib', layout.runtime_lib, '--ninja', layout.ninja,
            '--version', version_tag(game_version(ctx)), '--expected', layout.expected(game_version(ctx)),
            '--exefs', dest / 'exefs', '--romfs', dest / 'romfs',
            '--profile', dest / 'profile'], parse)
        exe = build / ('totk' + EXE)
        if code or not exe.is_file():
            raise InstallError('compile.failed', code=code, log=str(log))
        try:
            replace_file(exe, dest / exe.name)
        except PermissionError:
            raise InstallError('compile.exe_in_use', path=str(dest / exe.name)) from None
        replace_file(build / 'romfs-index.bin', dest / 'romfs-index.bin')
        for dll in layout.dlls:
            replace_file(dll, dest / dll.name)
        return {'exe_sha256': file_sha256(dest / exe.name)}


# ---- 5. prepare

TRANSLATED = re.compile(r'gfx_shader: prepare: (\d+) of (\d+) pairs')


WIDE_SIZES = ('2560x1080', '3440x1440', '3840x1600', '5120x2160')   # runtime/ui/menu.cpp row_output_res


class Prepare(Step):
    id = 'prepare'

    def key(self, ctx):
        layout = ctx.layout
        xlate_id = layout.xlate.with_suffix('.id')
        tools = [layout.tools / n for n in ('prepare_shaders.py', 'shader_census.py', 'make_romfs_patches.py',
                                            'pack_shader_cache.py', 'ultrawide_layout.py')]
        return fingerprint('prepare-1', ctx.keys['compile'], layout.xlate, xlate_id, shader_list_text(layout), *tools)

    def current(self, ctx, record):
        dest = ctx.dest
        xlate = dest / ctx.layout.xlate.name
        return ((dest / 'shader-prepared.bin').is_file() and (dest / 'romfs-patches' / 'manifest.tsv').is_file()
                and xlate.is_file() and file_sha256(xlate) == record.get('xlate_sha256'))

    def run(self, ctx):
        layout, rep, dest = ctx.layout, ctx.reporter, ctx.dest
        xlate = dest / layout.xlate.name
        if xlate.is_file() and file_sha256(xlate) != file_sha256(layout.xlate):
            # Another translator: its cache keys differ, so the old translations would only take space.
            for name in ('shader-cache', 'shader-prepared.bin'):
                remove(dest / name)
        replace_file(layout.xlate, xlate)
        xlate_id = layout.xlate.with_suffix('.id')
        if xlate_id.is_file():
            replace_file(xlate_id, xlate.with_suffix('.id'))
        else:
            remove(xlate.with_suffix('.id'))

        rep.progress('prepare', 'romfs_patches', force=True)
        remove(dest / 'romfs-patches')
        code, log = run_tool(ctx, 'prepare', layout.tools / 'make_romfs_patches.py',
                             ['--version', version_tag(game_version(ctx)), '--romfs', dest / 'romfs', '--out',
                              dest / 'romfs-patches'])
        if code:
            raise InstallError('prepare.romfs_patches_failed', code=code, log=str(log))
        # The same overlay with the UI laid out for the 21:9 game resolutions the settings menu offers (runtime/romfs.c
        # overlay_init picks the one that matches). Only 1.4.3 has the camera aspect patch (recomp/patches-v143.txt) the
        # layouts go with, and ultrawide_layout.py is checked against 1.4.3's layout archive: 1.2.1 builds none.
        for size in WIDE_SIZES:
            remove(dest / f'romfs-patches-{size}')
            if version_tag(game_version(ctx)) != 'v143':
                continue
            code, log = run_tool(ctx, 'prepare', layout.tools / 'make_romfs_patches.py',
                                 ['--version', 'v143', '--romfs', dest / 'romfs', '--out',
                                  dest / f'romfs-patches-{size}', '--aspect', size])
            if code:
                raise InstallError('prepare.romfs_patches_failed', code=code, log=str(log))
        # romfs-patches-xbox: the same with the A/B and X/Y prompts swapped, for pad_layout = xbox_prompts (written on
        # every install, so the menu choice works without another run of the setup). Optional: when it fails, the game
        # keeps the Switch prompts and the menu says the files are missing, so the setup warns and goes on.
        remove(dest / 'romfs-patches-xbox')
        code, log = run_tool(ctx, 'prepare-xbox', layout.tools / 'make_romfs_patches.py',
                             ['--version', version_tag(game_version(ctx)), '--romfs', dest / 'romfs', '--out',
                              dest / 'romfs-patches-xbox', '--xbox-prompts'])
        if code:
            remove(dest / 'romfs-patches-xbox')
            rep.warning('warn.xbox_prompts_failed', code=code, log=str(log))

        shader_list = layout.shader_list
        if not shader_list:
            shader_list = ctx.temp / 'shader_list.tsv'
            shader_list.write_text(shader_list_text(layout), encoding='utf-8', newline='\n')

        def parse(line):
            m = TRANSLATED.search(line)
            if m:
                rep.progress('prepare', 'translate', int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), 'shaders')
            elif 'listed variants' in line:
                rep.progress('prepare', 'translate', force=True)
            elif 'gfx_shader: prepare:' in line and 'translated' in line and 'programs' in line:
                rep.progress('prepare', 'libraries', force=True)

        rep.progress('prepare', 'seed', force=True)
        code, log = run_tool(ctx, 'prepare', layout.tools / 'prepare_shaders.py',
                             [dest, '--version', version_tag(game_version(ctx)), '--romfs', dest / 'romfs', '--exefs',
                              dest / 'exefs', '--list', shader_list], parse)
        if code or not (dest / 'shader-prepared.bin').is_file():
            raise InstallError('prepare.shaders_failed', code=code, log=str(log))

        # One shader-cache.pack instead of four files per shader (~117,000): totk.exe reads the pack first.
        rep.progress('prepare', 'pack', force=True)
        code, log = run_tool(ctx, 'prepare', layout.tools / 'pack_shader_cache.py', [dest / 'shader-cache'])
        if code:
            raise InstallError('prepare.pack_failed', code=code, log=str(log))
        return {'xlate_sha256': file_sha256(xlate)}


# ---- 6. clean up

class Cleanup(Step):
    id = 'cleanup'
    always = True

    def run(self, ctx):
        rep, dest = ctx.reporter, ctx.dest
        rep.progress('cleanup', 'ini', force=True)
        try:
            ini.write(dest, ctx.lang, ctx.layout.ini_example)
        except OSError as e:
            raise InstallError('cleanup.ini_failed', detail=str(e)) from None
        ctx.state['lang'] = ctx.lang
        (dest / 'profile').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        rep.progress('cleanup', 'temp', force=True)
        for stale in dest.glob('update-merge-*'):
            remove(stale)
        for name in ('gen', 'build', 'check', 'shader_list.tsv'):
            remove(ctx.temp / name)
        romfs_problem(dest / 'romfs', expected_update(ctx))
        return {}


def romfs_problem(romfs, expected):
    """Raise cleanup.romfs_unreadable unless romfs/ still holds the verified image. The game opens romfs.bin at start;
    an install whose romfs/ went empty and unreadable after the extraction verified it (a folder Windows was still
    deleting, #107) reported success and the game stopped at its first file read."""
    try:
        ok = extract.romfs_verified(romfs, expected) and (romfs / 'romfs.bin').stat().st_size == expected['romfs']['size']
        if ok:
            with open(romfs / 'romfs.bin', 'rb') as f:
                f.read(1)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        ok = False
    if not ok:
        raise InstallError('cleanup.romfs_unreadable', path=str(romfs))


def all_steps():
    return [Check(), Extract(), Lift(), Compile(), Prepare(), Cleanup()]
```

`recomp/flags.py`:

```py
"""Function-local NZCV for recomp/gen.py.

The lifter writes flags the way the guest does: every flag-setting instruction packs N, Z, C and V into c->nzcv
(subs64() and friends in runtime/cpu.h) and every reader unpacks them (COND_xx(c)). Compilers keep NZCV inside a
function, and AAPCS64 neither passes it to a callee nor preserves it across a call. So a generated function keeps its
flags in a local `Flags F` (runtime/cpu.h), which clang holds in registers, and writes c->nzcv only where it leaves
for another function other than by a call or a return (see plan()).

A flag-setting instruction of a known kind (subtract, add or logic result; 32 or 64 bits) stores its operands in F.a
and F.b. A reader all of whose reaching definitions are of one kind computes its condition from those operands, so
`cmp x1, x2; b.lt` becomes a signed compare in C. Instructions whose result is only known packed (CCMP, FCMP, MSR
NZCV, ADCS) write F.nz, the packed form; a reader whose definitions are of several kinds reads F.nz, and those
definitions then also write it.

A read that can see flags a callee left reads the caller's flags from before the call instead. AAPCS64 code never
reads a callee's flags, so such a read only sits on a path that does not run: in TotK it follows calls to noreturn
functions (asserts) that the compiler placed before another branch's target. Plan.after_call counts them.
"""
import re

KIND_DEF = re.compile(r'\b(subs|adds|logic)(32|64)\(c, ')
CARRY_DEF = re.compile(r'\b(adcs|sbcs)(32|64)\(c, ')
CARRY_USE = re.compile(r'\b(adc|sbc)(32|64)\(c, ')
COND = re.compile(r'COND_([A-Z]{2})\(c\)')
NZ_DEF = 'c->nzcv = '
NZ_USE = '(c->nzcv)'
KIND_NAME = {'subs': 'sub', 'adds': 'add', 'logic': 'logic'}

ENTRY, CALL = 'entry', 'call'


class FlagError(Exception):
    pass


def effect(code):
    """(reads flags, kind of the flags written or None) of one instruction's C."""
    reads = bool(COND.search(code) or CARRY_USE.search(code) or CARRY_DEF.search(code) or NZ_USE in code)
    if NZ_DEF in code or CARRY_DEF.search(code):
        return reads, 'nz'
    defs = KIND_DEF.findall(code)
    if len(defs) > 1:
        raise FlagError(f'several flag definitions in one instruction: {code}')
    if defs:
        op, size = defs[0]
        return reads, KIND_NAME[op] + size
    return reads, None


class Plan:
    """Per instruction: the kind its flag reads use, whether its flag definition also writes F.nz, and what it writes
    to c->nzcv before it leaves for another function."""

    def __init__(self, n):
        self.reader = [None] * n
        self.pack = [False] * n
        self.exit = [None] * n      # kind of the flags to publish in c->nzcv at a tail exit, or None
        self.entry = False          # F.nz starts as c->nzcv: flags from the entry reach a read or an exit
        self.entry_read = False     # they reach a read, not only an exit
        self.after_call = 0         # reads that can see flags a callee left (see the module docstring)
        self.used = False

    def decl(self):
        """Declaration of F at the top of the function."""
        return 'Flags F = {.nz = c->nzcv};' if self.entry else 'Flags F = {0};'

    def publish(self, i):
        """Statement writing the flags to c->nzcv at instruction i's tail exit ('' when it need not)."""
        k = self.exit[i]
        return f'c->nzcv = fnz_{k}(&F); ' if k else ''

    def rewrite(self, i, code):
        """code of instruction i with its flag reads and writes on F."""
        rk = self.reader[i]
        _, dk = effect(code)
        if rk:
            code = COND.sub(lambda m: f'fc_{rk}(&F, CC_{m.group(1)})', code)
            code = CARRY_DEF.sub(lambda m: f'{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}f(&F, fc_{rk}(&F, CC_CS), ', code)
            code = CARRY_USE.sub(lambda m: f'{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}f(fc_{rk}(&F, CC_CS), ', code)
            code = code.replace(NZ_USE, f'(fnz_{rk}(&F))')
        if dk == 'nz':
            code = code.replace(NZ_DEF, 'F.nz = ')
            code = re.sub(r'\(void\)(subs|adds)(32|64)\(c, ', lambda m: f'F.nz = nz_{KIND_NAME[m.group(1)]}{m.group(2)}(',
                          code)
        elif dk:
            code = KIND_DEF.sub(lambda m: f'f{KIND_NAME[m.group(1)]}{m.group(2)}(&F, ', code)
            if self.pack[i]:
                code += f' F.nz = fnz_{dk}(&F);'
        if 'c->nzcv' in code or COND.search(code) or KIND_DEF.search(code) or CARRY_USE.search(code):
            raise FlagError(f'flag access left after the rewrite: {code}')
        return code


def plan(effects, succ, calls, exits):
    """effects[i]: (reads, kind or None); succ[i]: successor indices inside the function; calls: indices of calls,
    whose callee may leave any flags; exits: indices that can leave for another function other than by a call or a
    return (a tail branch, falling into the next function, a br through rt_dispatch).

    Discovery can start a function inside another one (a branch target, a materialised address), and the code
    before it then falls or branches into it with live flags. So a tail exit publishes the flags in c->nzcv, and a
    function whose reads can see its entry flags starts F.nz from c->nzcv. Calls and returns publish nothing: AAPCS64
    code neither passes flags to a callee nor reads a callee's, so a call's flags count as no definition."""
    n = len(effects)
    p = Plan(n)
    if not any(r or k for r, k in effects):
        return p
    p.used = True
    reach = [set() for _ in range(n)]
    reach[0].add(ENTRY)
    work = [0]
    while work:
        i = work.pop()
        out = {i} if effects[i][1] else ({CALL} if i in calls else reach[i])
        for s in succ[i]:
            if not out <= reach[s]:
                reach[s] |= out
                work.append(s)

    def kind(d):
        return 'nz' if d == ENTRY else effects[d][1]

    def use(r):
        """Kind a use of the definitions r reads; several kinds read the packed form, which they then all write."""
        kinds = {kind(d) for d in r}
        if ENTRY in r:
            p.entry = True
        if len(kinds) == 1:
            return kinds.pop()
        for d in r:
            if d != ENTRY:
                p.pack[d] = True
        return 'nz'   # several kinds, or none (unreachable)

    for i, (reads, _) in enumerate(effects):
        if reads:
            p.after_call += CALL in reach[i]
            p.reader[i] = use(reach[i] - {CALL})
            p.entry_read |= ENTRY in reach[i]
    for i in exits:
        # Entry flags alone are still in c->nzcv.
        r = reach[i] - {CALL}
        if r and r != {ENTRY}:
            p.exit[i] = use(r)
    return p

```

`recomp/gen.py`:

```py
# Adapted from LAS Recomp tools/gen.py @ da35b83 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Peiikai).
"""Generate C for the ExeFS modules: function discovery, then parallel emission into chunked C files.

Usage: gen.py --exefs build/extracted/v121/exefs --out generated/v121 [--modules main,subsdk0,sdk] [--jobs N]
              [--limit N] [--chunk-fns N] [--chunk-bytes B] [--big-fn B] [--patches FILE]

Output, under --out:
  layout.h, layout.json        module bases (recomp/layout.py)
  <mod>/<mod>_NNNN.c           one `void f_<addr>(Cpu *c)` per guest function, about --chunk-bytes of C per file
  <mod>/<mod>_table.c          sorted <mod>_fn_addrs[] / <mod>_fn_ptrs[] / <mod>_fn_count for rt_dispatch
  <mod>/manifest.json          chunk list, function count, statistics and timings
  patches.h                    code patch sets for the runtime (recomp/patches.py; no sets without --patches)

Function discovery runs in this process, vectorised over the module's .text words. Function starts are the module
seeds (.eh_frame_hdr, exported FUNC symbols, RELATIVE relocation targets), every BL target, and code addresses
materialised by ADR or ADRP+ADD (except an ADR that anchors a jump table: one with a `br` in the next 16
instructions, or one an ADD register form uses as its base right after). A function is [start, next start). A direct branch whose target lies outside its
function makes the target a new start, until no new start appears.

Emission runs in worker processes, one chunk per task. Each worker loads the modules itself, lifts one function at a
time and resolves its jump tables (recomp/jumptables.py), so memory per worker does not grow with the module.
Chunks are sized from a per-instruction estimate of the C they produce, so their names and contents only depend on
the input; a chunk whose text did not change is not rewritten and keeps its mtime.
"""
import argparse
import json
import multiprocessing as mp
import os
import re
import sys
import time
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'tools'))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / 'recomp'))

import flags  # noqa: E402
import hostmem  # noqa: E402
import jumptables  # noqa: E402
import patches  # noqa: E402
import regs  # noqa: E402
from check_content import GENERATED_MARKER  # noqa: E402
from layout import layout, write as write_layout  # noqa: E402
from lifter import hx  # noqa: E402
from module import Module  # noqa: E402

TERMINATORS = ('b', 'br', 'ret', 'trap')
MUSTTAIL = '__attribute__((musttail)) return'

# Estimated bytes of C per instruction, by class, for chunking (estimate_sizes()).
# Least squares over every function of main, subsdk0 and sdk (1.2.1) gives 62 / 75 / 48 bytes per instruction, 38
# per function and 4.5 per instruction of a function with a `br` (switches; the all-label fallback costs about 60
# per instruction but is rare); the median error per function is 7 %.
EST_INT = 62
EST_SIMD = 75
EST_SIMD_LDST = 48
EST_FN = 38          # per function: signature, FN_ENTER, closing brace
EST_BR_LABELS = 10   # per instruction of a function with a `br`: switch cases, or labels if it falls back


def fname(a):
    return f'f_{a:x}'


def header(what):
    return f'// {GENERATED_MARKER}: {what}, generated by recomp/gen.py from game code. Do not edit or commit.\n'


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ discovery

def _sext(v, n):
    v = v.astype(np.int64)
    return np.where(v & (1 << (n - 1)), v - (1 << n), v)


def discover(mod):
    """Function starts of mod as a sorted int64 array of word indices into mod.words, plus discovery statistics."""
    w = mod.words
    n = len(w)

    def idx(mask):
        return np.flatnonzero(mask).astype(np.int64)

    seeds = (np.asarray(mod.seeds(), dtype=np.int64) - mod.lo) >> 2

    # B and BL: imm26. BL targets are function starts; B targets join the fixpoint below.
    b_all = idx((w & 0x7C000000) == 0x14000000)
    imm = _sext(w[b_all] & 0x03FFFFFF, 26)
    is_bl = (w[b_all] >> 31).astype(bool)
    bl_tgt = b_all[is_bl] + imm[is_bl]
    br_src, br_tgt = [b_all[~is_bl]], [b_all[~is_bl] + imm[~is_bl]]
    # B.cond (the lifter accepts o1 = 1 too), CBZ/CBNZ: imm19 at bit 5. TBZ/TBNZ: imm14 at bit 5.
    for mask, val, nb in ((0xFE000010, 0x54000000, 19), (0x7E000000, 0x34000000, 19), (0x7E000000, 0x36000000, 14)):
        s = idx((w & mask) == val)
        br_src.append(s)
        br_tgt.append(s + _sext((w[s] >> 5) & ((1 << nb) - 1), nb))
    br_src, br_tgt = np.concatenate(br_src), np.concatenate(br_tgt)
    ok = (br_tgt >= 0) & (br_tgt < n)
    br_src, br_tgt = br_src[ok], br_tgt[ok]

    # ADR: pc + imm21. ADRP: page + (imm21 << 12), then ADD (imm, 64-bit, unshifted) of the same register within
    # 8 instructions. Targets must be aligned and in .text.
    def imm21(s):
        v = w[s]
        return _sext(((v >> 5) & 0x7FFFF) << 2 | ((v >> 29) & 3), 21)

    pc0 = np.int64(mod.lo)
    adr = idx((w & 0x9F000000) == 0x10000000)
    # Clang's jump tables add a table entry to an ADR anchor, the first case block, then `br`. That anchor is not a
    # function (it would split the switch): an ADR with a `br` in the next 16 instructions is not a seed, nor is one
    # whose register is the base of an ADD (shifted or extended register) in the next 4 instructions
    # (`adr xA, L; ldrb wO, [..]; add xA, xA, wO, lsl #2`), however far the scheduler moved the `br`.
    br = idx((w & 0xFFFFFC1F) == 0xD61F0000)
    nxt = np.searchsorted(br, adr)
    has_br = nxt < len(br)
    near = np.zeros(len(adr), dtype=bool)
    near[has_br] = br[nxt[has_br]] - adr[has_br] <= 16
    rd = w[adr] & 31
    for k in range(1, 5):
        x = w[np.minimum(adr + k, n - 1)]
        near |= (((x & 0xFF200000) == 0x8B000000) | ((x & 0xFFE00000) == 0x8B200000)) & (((x >> 5) & 31) == rd)
    adr = adr[~near]
    adr_bytes = pc0 + adr * 4 + imm21(adr)
    is_adrp = (w & 0x9F000000) == 0x90000000
    add = idx((w & 0xFFC00000) == 0x91000000)
    rn = ((w[add] >> 5) & 31).astype(np.int64)
    found = np.full(len(add), -1, dtype=np.int64)
    for k in range(1, 9):
        p = add - k
        cand = (found < 0) & (p >= 0)
        pc = np.where(cand, p, 0)
        cand &= is_adrp[pc] & ((w[pc] & 31).astype(np.int64) == rn)
        found[cand] = p[cand]
    hit = found >= 0
    p = found[hit]
    page = ((pc0 + p * 4) & ~np.int64(0xFFF)) + (imm21(p) << 12)
    add_bytes = page + ((w[add[hit]] >> 10) & 0xFFF).astype(np.int64)
    mat = np.concatenate([adr_bytes, add_bytes])
    mat = mat[(mat >= mod.lo) & (mat < mod.hi) & (mat % 4 == 0)]
    mat = (mat - pc0) >> 2

    bl_tgt = bl_tgt[(bl_tgt >= 0) & (bl_tgt < n)]
    starts = np.unique(np.concatenate([seeds, bl_tgt, mat]))
    stats = {'seeds': int(len(seeds)), 'bl_targets': int(len(np.unique(bl_tgt))),
             'materialised_targets': int(len(np.unique(mat))), 'initial_starts': int(len(starts))}

    rounds = 0
    while True:
        rounds += 1
        f = np.searchsorted(starts, br_src, side='right') - 1
        live = f >= 0
        f = np.where(live, f, 0)
        lo = starts[f]
        hi = np.where(f + 1 < len(starts), starts[np.minimum(f + 1, len(starts) - 1)], n)
        out = live & ((br_tgt < lo) | (br_tgt >= hi))
        new = np.setdiff1d(br_tgt[out], starts, assume_unique=False)
        if not len(new):
            break
        starts = np.union1d(starts, new)
    stats['rounds'] = rounds
    stats['functions'] = int(len(starts))
    return starts, stats


def estimate_sizes(mod, starts):
    """Estimated bytes of C per function (for chunking only; the manifest records the real sizes)."""
    w = mod.words
    cost = np.full(len(w), EST_INT, dtype=np.int64)
    cost[(w & 0x0E000000) == 0x0E000000] = EST_SIMD                    # FP/AdvSIMD data processing
    cost[((w & 0x0A000000) == 0x08000000) & (((w >> 26) & 1) == 1)] = EST_SIMD_LDST  # FP/SIMD load/store
    has_br = np.zeros(len(w), dtype=np.int64)
    has_br[np.flatnonzero((w & 0xFFFFFC1F) == 0xD61F0000)] = 1           # BR Xn
    csum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(cost)])
    bsum = np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(has_br)])
    ends = np.append(starts[1:], len(w))
    size = csum[ends] - csum[starts] + EST_FN
    with_br = (bsum[ends] - bsum[starts]) > 0
    size[with_br] += (ends[with_br] - starts[with_br]) * EST_BR_LABELS
    return size


def partition(est, max_fns, max_bytes, big_fn):
    """Contiguous [i0, i1) function ranges: at most max_fns functions and about max_bytes of C each; a function
    estimated above big_fn gets a file of its own so large functions compile in parallel."""
    chunks, i0, size = [], 0, 0
    for i, s in enumerate(est.tolist()):
        if s > big_fn:
            if i > i0:
                chunks.append((i0, i))
            chunks.append((i, i + 1))
            i0, size = i + 1, 0
            continue
        if i > i0 and (i - i0 >= max_fns or size + s > max_bytes):
            chunks.append((i0, i))
            i0, size = i, 0
        size += s
    if len(est) > i0:
        chunks.append((i0, len(est)))
    return chunks


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ emission

class Emitter:
    """C for the functions of one module. starts is the set of every function start of the module."""

    def __init__(self, mod, starts, patched=None, reg_locals=regs.LOCALS, callee_saved=True, spins=None):
        self.mod = mod
        self.starts = starts
        self.patched = patched or {}   # {address: (set index, [replacement words])} (recomp/patches.py)
        self.spins = spins or {}       # {spin wait back-edge: its head} (recomp/patches.py `spin`)
        self.reg_locals = reg_locals   # recomp/regs.py: registers per function in C locals
        self.kept = regs.CALLEE_SAVED if callee_saved else frozenset()   # not reloaded after a call
        self.uses_patches = False
        self.stats = Counter()
        self.unsupported = Counter()

    def scan(self, insns, entry, end):
        """Labels and jump tables of one function: {pc: sorted targets} for resolved tables, 'all' for an
        unresolved computed br."""
        mod, labels, tables = self.mod, set(), {}
        for i, ins in enumerate(insns):
            k = ins.kind
            if k in ('b', 'bcond'):
                if entry <= ins.target < end:
                    labels.add(ins.target)
            elif k == 'br':
                a = entry + 4 * i
                jt = jumptables.resolve(mod, a, entry, end)
                if jt:
                    tables[a] = jt
                    labels.update(jt)
                    self.stats['jump_tables'] += 1
                    self.stats['jump_table_targets'] += len(jt)
                elif jumptables.is_computed(mod, a, entry):
                    tables[a] = 'all'
                    self.stats['all_label_fallbacks'] += 1
                else:
                    self.stats['br_dispatch'] += 1
            elif k == 'trap':
                self.stats['traps'] += 1
                c = ins.code
                if c.startswith('rt_udf') and '/*' in c:
                    self.stats['unsupported'] += 1
                    msg = c[c.index('/*') + 2:c.rindex('*/')].strip()
                    self.unsupported[re.sub(r'\b[0-9a-f]{8}\b', '', msg).strip()] += 1
            elif k == 'asm':
                raise ValueError(f'{entry + 4 * i:#x}: asm instruction from the portable lifter')
        return labels, tables

    def replacements(self, a):
        """Lifted replacement words of the patched site a."""
        return [self.mod.lifter.lift(w, a) for w in self.patched[a][1]]

    @staticmethod
    def flow(insns, entry, end, tables):
        """Successors of each instruction inside the function [entry, end). Index len(insns) stands for falling
        through into the next function and has none."""
        def idx(t):
            return [(t - entry) // 4] if entry <= t < end else []

        succ = []
        for i, ins in enumerate(insns):
            k = ins.kind
            if k in ('op', 'bl', 'blr'):
                succ.append([i + 1])
            elif k == 'b':
                succ.append(idx(ins.target))
            elif k == 'bcond':
                succ.append(idx(ins.target) + [i + 1])
            elif k == 'br':
                jt = tables.get(entry + 4 * i)
                succ.append([t for x in jt for t in idx(x)] if jt and jt != 'all' else [])
            else:   # ret, trap
                succ.append([])
        succ.append([])
        return succ

    def flag_plan(self, insns, entry, end, tables, succ):
        """recomp/flags.py plan for the function: each instruction's flag use over the flow succ (flow())."""
        n = len(insns)
        calls, effects, exits = set(), [], {n}
        for i, ins in enumerate(insns):
            k, a = ins.kind, entry + 4 * i
            if k in ('bl', 'blr'):
                calls.add(i)
            elif k in ('b', 'bcond') and not entry <= ins.target < end:
                exits.add(i)
            elif k == 'br':
                exits.add(i)   # through rt_dispatch, also a table's default
            if a in self.patched:
                effects.append(self.patched_effect(ins, a))
                if any(r.kind == 'bl' for r in self.replacements(a)):
                    calls.add(i)
            else:
                effects.append(flags.effect(ins.cond if k == 'bcond' else ins.code or ''))
        effects.append((False, None))
        return flags.plan(effects, succ, calls, exits)

    def patched_effect(self, ins, a):
        """Flag effect of a patched site: both alternatives must have the same one, in at most one word each."""
        alts = []
        for words in ([ins], self.replacements(a)):
            fx = [flags.effect(w.code or '') for w in words if w.kind == 'op']
            fx = [e for e in fx if e[0] or e[1]]
            if len(fx) > 1:
                raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: several flag-using words in one alternative')
            alts.append(fx[0] if fx else (False, None))
        if alts[0][1] != alts[1][1]:
            raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: the alternatives write different flags ({alts[0][1]}, {alts[1][1]})')
        if (alts[0][1] or alts[0][0] or alts[1][0]) and ins.kind == 'bl':
            raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: a patched call that uses flags')
        return alts[0][0] or alts[1][0], alts[0][1]

    def function(self, entry, end):
        """(lines of C, referenced function starts) for the guest function [entry, end)."""
        mod, starts = self.mod, self.starts
        insns = [mod.lift(a) for a in range(entry, end, 4)]
        labels, tables = self.scan(insns, entry, end)
        refs = set()
        all_labels = 'all' in tables.values()
        if all_labels:
            labels = set(range(entry, end, 4))
        # An unresolved computed br re-enters the function through fb_<entry>, a C function of its own, which local
        # flags would not survive; such functions keep NZCV in c->nzcv.
        # The same holds for registers in locals (recomp/regs.py): fb_<entry> keeps them in the Cpu too.
        local = not all_labels
        spill, reload, reload_call = (regs.SPILL, regs.RELOAD, regs.RELOAD_CALL) if local else ('', '', '')
        succ = self.flow(insns, entry, end, tables) if local else None
        fp = self.flag_plan(insns, entry, end, tables, succ) if local else None
        if fp and fp.used:
            self.stats['local_flag_functions'] += 1
            self.stats['flag_reads_direct'] += sum(1 for k in fp.reader if k and k != 'nz')
            self.stats['flag_reads_packed'] += sum(1 for k in fp.reader if k == 'nz')
            self.stats['flag_entry_functions'] += fp.entry
            self.stats['flag_entry_reads'] += fp.entry_read
            self.stats['flag_reads_after_call'] += fp.after_call
            self.stats['flag_publishing_exits'] += sum(1 for k in fp.exit if k)

        def fx(i, code):
            return fp.rewrite(i, code) if fp and fp.used else code

        def publish(i):
            return fp.publish(i) if fp and fp.used else ''

        def jump(t, i):
            if entry <= t < end:
                return f'goto L_{t:x};'
            if t in starts:
                refs.add(t)
                return f'{publish(i)}{spill}{MUSTTAIL} {fname(t)}(c);'
            self.stats['external_branches'] += 1
            return f'{publish(i)}{spill}c->pc = {hx(t)}; {MUSTTAIL} rt_dispatch(c);'

        if all_labels:
            # An unresolved computed br re-enters the function through fb_<entry>, which switches on c->pc to any
            # instruction. A goto to a shared dispatch block inside the body instead turns every instruction into
            # a loop header, and clang's loop passes then take tens of seconds on one function.
            fb = f'fb_{entry:x}'
            cases = ' '.join(f'case {hx(t)}: goto L_{t:x};' for t in range(entry, end, 4))
            redispatch = f'{MUSTTAIL} {fb}(c);'
            out = [f'static void {fb}(Cpu *c);',
                   f'void {fname(entry)}(Cpu *c) {{', f'    FN_ENTER({hx(entry)});', f'    c->pc = {hx(entry)};',
                   f'    {redispatch}', '}',
                   f'static void {fb}(Cpu *c) {{', f'    switch (c->pc) {{ {cases} default: break; }}',
                   f'    {MUSTTAIL} rt_dispatch(c);']
        else:
            redispatch = f'{MUSTTAIL} rt_dispatch(c);'
            out = [f'void {fname(entry)}(Cpu *c) {{', f'    FN_ENTER({hx(entry)});']
            if fp.used:
                out.append('    ' + fp.decl())

        def call(t, a):
            if t in starts:
                refs.add(t)
                return f'c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {spill}{fname(t)}(c);{reload_call}'
            self.stats['external_calls'] += 1
            return f'c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {spill}c->pc = {hx(t)}; rt_dispatch(c);{reload_call}'

        def op(i, code):
            code = fx(i, code)
            return f'{spill}{code}{reload}' if regs.ESCAPE.search(code) else code

        def patch(i, ins, a):
            """if (switch) { replacement } else { original } for a patched site (recomp/patches.py)."""
            k, words = self.patched[a]
            if ins.kind not in ('op', 'bl'):
                raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: patched instruction is a {ins.kind}')
            repl = []
            for j, (w, r) in enumerate(zip(words, self.replacements(a))):
                if r.kind == 'op':
                    repl.append(op(i, r.code))
                elif r.kind == 'bl' and j == len(words) - 1:
                    repl.append(call(r.target, a))
                else:
                    raise patches.PatchError(f'{a:#x}: replacement word {w:08x} is a {r.kind}')
            orig = op(i, ins.code) if ins.kind == 'op' else call(ins.target, a)
            self.uses_patches = True
            self.stats['patched_sites'] += 1
            return f'    if (rt_patch_on[{k}]) {{ {" ".join(repl)} }} else {{ {orig} }}'

        body = []   # (instruction index or None for a label, line); a line belongs to the instruction it lifts

        def emit(i, line):
            body.append((i, line))

        k = None
        for i, ins in enumerate(insns):
            a = entry + 4 * i
            if a in labels:
                emit(None, f'L_{a:x}:;')
            k = ins.kind
            if a in self.patched:
                emit(i, patch(i, ins, a))
            elif k == 'op':
                emit(i, '    ' + op(i, ins.code))
            elif k == 'trap':
                emit(i, f'    {spill}{fx(i, ins.code)}')
            elif k in ('b', 'bcond'):
                j = jump(ins.target, i)
                if self.spins.get(a) == ins.target and entry <= ins.target < end:
                    j = f'rt_spin_gate(c, {hx(ins.target)}); {j}'   # a pass of a spin wait
                    self.stats['spin_gates'] += 1
                emit(i, '    ' + j if k == 'b' else f'    if ({fx(i, ins.cond)}) {{ {j} }}')
            elif k == 'bl':
                emit(i, '    ' + call(ins.target, a))
            elif k == 'blr':
                emit(i, f'    c->pc = {ins.target}; c->x[30] = {hx(a + 4)}; {spill}rt_dispatch(c);{reload_call}')
            elif k == 'br':
                jt = tables.get(a)
                if jt == 'all':
                    emit(i, f'    c->pc = {ins.target}; {redispatch}')
                elif jt:
                    cases = ' '.join(f'case {hx(t)}: goto L_{t:x};' for t in jt)
                    emit(i, f'    switch ({ins.target}) {{ {cases} default: break; }}')
```
