`runtime/resolution.c`:

```c
// Game resolution: the size the game composes its frame in (its output: canvas, UI and swapchain) and the size of its
// 3D scene, above the shipped 1920x1080 and 1600x900. The game does the rendering itself, as with the community
// resolution mods (UltraCam, Visual Fixes): the patch sets output and scene (recomp/patches-v121.txt,
// patches-v143.txt; MacNativeGames games/totk/runtime/game_patches.c and game_patches_v143.c, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026
// MacNativeGames contributors) make the game read both sizes from the patch page, and the texture heap that holds the
// output- and scene-sized render targets grows with them.
//
// Settings, read at start: TOTK_OUTPUT_RES = <w>x<h> (default 1920x1080, the game's own), TOTK_RENDER_SCALE = the
// scene's size relative to the output: "game" (default, 5/6, the game's 1600x900 at 1080p) or a percentage; above 100
// the game supersamples its scene, which smooths edges (anti-aliasing) at the cost of GPU time. The game's own final
// pass (FSR 1 EASU) scales the scene to the output; the present scales the output to the window (vk_fsr.c).
//
// Patch page: +16 the scene size {w, h} as floats, +32 the output size and +48 the swapchain size as {w, h} in one
// 64-bit word, +40 the renderer (1.2.1) or display configuration (1.4.3) the patched code stores there.
// +56 the camera's aspect ratio as a float when the output is not 16:9 (1.4.3, set aspect).
// 1.4.3 scales the scene it reads by output width / 1920 (a 2560x1440 output renders its 1600x900 scene at 2128x1200;
// MacNativeGames measured the same), so its page holds the wanted size divided by that factor and the game's 5/6 needs
// no scene patch. 1.2.1 renders the size it reads (1600x900 on a 2560x1440 output): its page holds the wanted size, and
// the scene set is on whenever the output differs from 1920x1080.
//
// Heap: agl's DynamicTextureAllocator is one fixed heap, "DynamicTextureAllocatorMem" in
// System/HeapSize/Product.Nin_NX_NVN.HeapDef.byml.zs (113664 KiB, carved from "Graphics", 201728 KiB). At 2560x1440
// the shipped size runs out at the title screen. Both heaps grow by the same amount: the shipped size times the output's
// pixel ratio above 1920x1080 plus the scene's above 1600x900 (MacNativeGames' measurement: a 3440x1440 canvas with a
// 4620x1935 scene crashed at +258 MiB and loaded at +400 MiB; this formula gives +750 MiB there). romfs.c serves the
// rewritten table (res_heapdef_build) in place of the original; memory.c adds the amount to the application pool, so
// no other heap shrinks. Without the rewritten table (a RomFS that lacks it, a format this code does not know) the
// patch sets stay off and the game keeps its own sizes.
#include <math.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <zstd.h>

#include "cfg.h"
#include "host.h"

#define BASE_W 1920
#define BASE_H 1080
#define SCENE_W 1600
#define SCENE_H 900
#define DTA_KIB 113664u      // DynamicTextureAllocatorMem, shipped
#define SCENE_MAX 4096       // per side, as MacNativeGames' TOTK_RENDER_RES

static struct {
    int decided;
    unsigned ow, oh, sw, sh;   // output and scene
    int scene_set;             // the scene differs from the game's 5/6 of the output
    int heapdef_ok;            // romfs.c serves the grown HeapDef
    int on;                    // res_init switched the patch sets on
} R;

static void decide(void) {
    if (R.decided) return;
    R.decided = 1;
    R.ow = BASE_W;
    R.oh = BASE_H;
    const char *o = cfg_value("TOTK_OUTPUT_RES");
    unsigned w = 0, h = 0;
    char tail;
    if (sscanf(o, "%ux%u%c", &w, &h, &tail) == 2 && w >= 1280 && h >= 720 && w <= 7680 && h <= 4320) {
        R.ow = w & ~1u;
        R.oh = h & ~1u;
    } else {
        rt_log("resolution: TOTK_OUTPUT_RES=%s is not <width>x<height> in 1280x720..7680x4320; 1920x1080", o);
    }
    const char *s = cfg_value("TOTK_RENDER_SCALE");
    double k = 5.0 / 6.0;
    if (strcmp(s, "game")) {
        char *end;
        double pct = strtod(s, &end);
        if (end != s && !*end && pct >= 25 && pct <= 400) {
            k = pct / 100.0;
            R.scene_set = 1;
        } else {
            rt_log("resolution: TOTK_RENDER_SCALE=%s is not game or a percentage 25..400; game", s);
        }
    }
    double sw = R.ow * k, sh = R.oh * k;
    double fit = fmin(1.0, fmin(SCENE_MAX / sw, SCENE_MAX / sh));
    if (fit < 1.0) R.scene_set = 1;
    R.sw = (unsigned)(sw * fit + 0.5);
    R.sh = (unsigned)(sh * fit + 0.5);
}

static int bigger(void) {
    decide();
    return R.ow != BASE_W || R.oh != BASE_H || R.scene_set;
}

uint64_t res_heap_extra_kib(void) {
    if (!bigger()) return 0;
    double grow = fmax(0.0, (double)R.ow * R.oh / (BASE_W * BASE_H) - 1.0) +
                  fmax(0.0, (double)R.sw * R.sh / (SCENE_W * SCENE_H) - 1.0);
    if (grow <= 0) return 0;
    return (uint64_t)ceil(DTA_KIB * (1.0 + grow) / 1024.0) * 1024 - DTA_KIB;
}

uint64_t res_heap_extra_bytes(void) { return ((res_heap_extra_kib() << 10) + 0x1fffff) & ~0x1fffffull; }

// ---- the HeapDef table. BYML version 2..7, little endian ("YB"): a hash node is {u8 0xC1, u24 count} and count
// entries {u24 key index, u8 type, u32 value}; an int (type 0xD1) is stored in the entry, so a size changes in place.
typedef struct { uint8_t *p; size_t n; uint32_t keys; } Byml;

static int u32_at(const Byml *b, size_t off, uint32_t *v) {
    if (off + 4 > b->n) return 0;
    memcpy(v, b->p + off, 4);
    return 1;
}

static const char *key_name(const Byml *b, uint32_t k) {
    uint32_t head, at;
    if (!u32_at(b, b->keys, &head) || (head & 0xff) != 0xc2 || k >= head >> 8 || !u32_at(b, b->keys + 4 + 4 * k, &at) ||
        b->keys + at >= b->n || !memchr(b->p + b->keys + at, 0, b->n - b->keys - at))
        return NULL;
    return (const char *)b->p + b->keys + at;
}

// The offset of the value of hash node `node`'s entry `name`, which must have type `type`; 0 when there is none.
static size_t field(const Byml *b, uint32_t node, const char *name, uint8_t type) {
    uint32_t head;
    if (!u32_at(b, node, &head) || (head & 0xff) != 0xc1) return 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < head >> 8; i++) {
        uint32_t e;
        if (!u32_at(b, node + 4 + 8 * (size_t)i, &e)) return 0;
        const char *k = key_name(b, e & 0xffffff);
        if (k && !strcmp(k, name)) return e >> 24 == type ? node + 8 + 8 * (size_t)i : 0;
    }
    return 0;
}

static size_t heap_size_field(const Byml *b, uint32_t heaps, const char *heap) {
    size_t at = field(b, heaps, heap, 0xc1);
    uint32_t node;
    return at && u32_at(b, at, &node) ? field(b, node, "Size", 0xd1) : 0;
}

int res_heapdef_build(const void *in, size_t n, void **out, size_t *out_n) {
    uint64_t extra = res_heap_extra_kib();
    *out = NULL;
    if (!extra) return 0;
    if (ZSTD_getDictID_fromFrame(in, n)) {
        rt_log("resolution: the HeapDef table needs a zstd dictionary; the game keeps its own resolution");
        return 0;
    }
    unsigned long long raw = ZSTD_getFrameContentSize(in, n);
    if (raw == ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN || raw == ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_ERROR || raw > (64u << 20)) {
        rt_log("resolution: the HeapDef table is not a zstd frame with a size; the game keeps its own resolution");
        return 0;
    }
    Byml b = {malloc((size_t)raw), (size_t)raw, 0};
    if (!b.p) return 0;
    size_t got = ZSTD_decompress(b.p, b.n, in, n);
    uint32_t root, heaps = 0;
    uint16_t ver = 0;
    if (!ZSTD_isError(got) && got == b.n && b.n >= 16) memcpy(&ver, b.p + 2, 2);
    size_t heaps_at = 0, dta_at = 0, gfx_at = 0;
    if (ver >= 2 && ver <= 7 && !memcmp(b.p, "YB", 2) && u32_at(&b, 4, &b.keys) && u32_at(&b, 12, &root) &&
        (heaps_at = field(&b, root, "Heaps", 0xc1)) && u32_at(&b, heaps_at, &heaps)) {
        dta_at = heap_size_field(&b, heaps, "DynamicTextureAllocatorMem");
        gfx_at = heap_size_field(&b, heaps, "Graphics");
    }
    if (!dta_at || !gfx_at) {
        rt_log("resolution: the HeapDef table has no DynamicTextureAllocatorMem / Graphics sizes; the game keeps its own "
               "resolution");
        free(b.p);
        return 0;
    }
    int32_t dta, gfx;
    memcpy(&dta, b.p + dta_at, 4);
    memcpy(&gfx, b.p + gfx_at, 4);
    int32_t dta2 = dta + (int32_t)extra, gfx2 = gfx + (int32_t)extra;
    memcpy(b.p + dta_at, &dta2, 4);
    memcpy(b.p + gfx_at, &gfx2, 4);
    size_t cap = ZSTD_compressBound(b.n);
    void *z = malloc(cap);
    size_t zn = z ? ZSTD_compress(z, cap, b.p, b.n, 9) : 0;
    free(b.p);
    if (!z || ZSTD_isError(zn)) {
        free(z);
        return 0;
    }
    *out = z;
    *out_n = zn;
    rt_log("resolution: HeapDef DynamicTextureAllocatorMem %d -> %d KiB, Graphics %d -> %d KiB", dta, dta2, gfx, gfx2);
    return 1;
}

void res_heapdef_served(void) { R.heapdef_ok = 1; }

// ---- start: the patch page and the sets
static uint64_t pack(unsigned w, unsigned h) { return (uint64_t)h << 32 | w; }

void res_init(void) {
    if (!bigger()) {
        rt_log("resolution: the game's own (output 1920x1080, scene 1600x900)");
        return;
    }
    int output = rt_patch_set("output"), scene = rt_patch_set("scene");
    if (output < 0 || scene < 0) {
        rt_log("resolution: the generated C has no output and scene patch sets; the game keeps its own resolution");
        return;
    }
    fs_init();   // romfs.c serves the grown HeapDef from here on (res_heapdef_served)
    if (res_heap_extra_kib() && !R.heapdef_ok) {   // sizes at or below the shipped ones fit the shipped heaps
        rt_log("resolution: no grown HeapDef table; the game keeps its own resolution");
        return;
    }
    uint8_t *page = rt_patch_page();
    double k = RT_V143 ? (double)R.ow / BASE_W : 1.0;   // 1.4.3's own scaling of the scene with the output width
    int scene_on = R.scene_set || (!RT_V143 && (R.ow != BASE_W || R.oh != BASE_H));
    float sc[2] = {(float)(R.sw / k), (float)(R.sh / k)};
    uint64_t out = pack(R.ow, R.oh), none = 0;
    memcpy(page + 16, sc, sizeof sc);
    memcpy(page + 32, &out, 8);
    memcpy(page + 40, &none, 8);
    memcpy(page + 48, &out, 8);
    rt_patch_switch(output, R.ow != BASE_W || R.oh != BASE_H);
    rt_patch_switch(scene, scene_on);
    R.on = 1;
    // Another shape than 16:9 (more than 1% off): the camera takes the output's ratio (recomp/patches-v143.txt, set
    // aspect), so a 21:9 output shows more of the world at the sides instead of a stretched 16:9 view. The HUD's layouts
    // for that shape come from romfs-patches-<w>x<h> (romfs.c overlay_init, tools/make_romfs_patches.py --aspect).
    double ratio = (double)R.ow / R.oh, game = (double)BASE_W / BASE_H;
    int aspect = rt_patch_set("aspect");
    if (!res_is_16x9(R.ow, R.oh)) {
        if (aspect < 0) {
            rt_log("resolution: output %ux%u is not 16:9 and this game version has no camera aspect patch; the view "
                   "is stretched", R.ow, R.oh);
        } else {
            float r = (float)ratio;
            memcpy(page + 56, &r, sizeof r);
            rt_patch_switch(aspect, 1);
            rt_log("resolution: camera aspect ratio %.4f (16:9 is %.4f)", ratio, game);
        }
    } else {
        rt_patch_switch(aspect, 0);   // the page holds no ratio
    }
    rt_log("resolution: output %ux%u, scene %ux%u%s; texture heap +%llu KiB", R.ow, R.oh, R.sw, R.sh,
           scene_on ? "" : " (the game's own 5/6 of the output)", (unsigned long long)res_heap_extra_kib());
}

// 16:9 within 1% (1366x768 counts): the shape the game's own layouts and camera are made for.
int res_is_16x9(unsigned w, unsigned h) {
    double rel = ((double)w / h) / ((double)BASE_W / BASE_H);
    return rel >= 0.99 && rel <= 1.01;
}

// The game resolution asks for a romfs-patches-<w>x<h> overlay: it is not 16:9 and the game version has the camera
// aspect patch (set aspect, 1.4.3 only); the wide UI layouts only fit a camera that follows the same shape.
int res_wants_wide_overlay(const unsigned out[2]) {
    return !res_is_16x9(out[0], out[1]) && rt_patch_set("aspect") >= 0;
}

void res_wanted(unsigned out[2]) {
    decide();
    out[0] = R.ow, out[1] = R.oh;
}

void res_sizes(unsigned out[2], unsigned scene[2]) {
    decide();
    out[0] = R.on ? R.ow : BASE_W, out[1] = R.on ? R.oh : BASE_H;
    scene[0] = R.on ? R.sw : SCENE_W, scene[1] = R.on ? R.sh : SCENE_H;
}

```

`runtime/romfs.c`:

```c
// Adapted from MacNativeGames games/totk/runtime/romfs.c @ b75be8cf (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 MacNativeGames
// contributors).
// Read-only game RomFS backed by the player's extracted image.
//
// Input: <romfs>/romfs.bin (rt_config()->romfs), whose six IVFC levels and SHA-256 tools/extract.py verified, and
// romfs-index.bin next to totk.exe (TOTK_ROMFS_INDEX overrides), which tools/romfs_index.py wrote together with
// romfs_config.h. fs_init checks the index's SHA-256 and layout and the image size. The full 17 GB hash runs only with
// TOTK_ROMFS_VERIFY=full; a proof file (.romfs-verified-v1 next to the index, or in TOTK_ROMFS_PROOF_DIR) keyed by
// the file's volume, file id, size and times skips it on later starts, TOTK_ROMFS_VERIFY=force ignores the proof.
//
// Reads are positional (ReadFile with an OVERLAPPED offset on a FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED handle, one event per thread),
// so threads read the image in parallel without a file-pointer lock. TOTK_ROMFS_MMAP=1 maps the image instead.
//
// Overlays: files listed in a directory's manifest.tsv are served in place of the originals. Each line names a RomFS
// path, the overlay's size and SHA-256 and the original's SHA-256 ("-" adds a file the RomFS lacks; it is numbered
// after the RomFS's own files, file_count + k in path order). The directories, in this order: TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES and
// TOTK_ROMFS_MODS; unset or "0" = none. A missing path, a size or hash mismatch or a changed original stops the start.
// An overlay file is opened when the game opens it; its identity (volume, file id, size, last write) is kept from the
// start check, and an open that finds another file there stops the game.
#include <windows.h>
#include <bcrypt.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "cfg.h"
#include "fs.h"
#include "host.h"
#include "romfs_config.h"
#include "romfs_path.h"

#define NH 65536                     // RomFS handle slots
#define READ_CHUNK (64u << 20)       // largest single ReadFile
#define HASH_CHUNK (8u << 20)
#define ADDED UINT64_MAX             // an added overlay file's index until overlay_init numbers it

typedef struct { uint64_t offset, size; uint32_t name, len; } Entry;
_Static_assert(sizeof(Entry) == 24, "index entry layout");

typedef struct { uint32_t volume, pad; uint64_t file_id, size, write_time, create_time; } Identity;   // no padding
typedef struct { uint64_t index, size; char *path, *name; Identity id; } Overlay;

static uint8_t *index_bytes;
static size_t index_size;
static uint64_t file_count, strings_offset;
static HANDLE image = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
static const uint8_t *image_map;
static char image_file[2048];
static char index_dir[2048];         // the directory of romfs-index.bin: the proof file's default place
static char mount_name[32];
static SRWLOCK lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
static uint64_t handles[NH];         // file index + 1; 0 is free
static uint32_t handle_ovl[NH];      // overlay slot + 1 of an open handle, 0 = original
static HANDLE handle_file[NH];       // the handle's open overlay file, when handle_ovl is set
static Overlay *overlays;            // sorted by RomFS index after overlay_init
static size_t noverlay, overlay_cap;
static char **added;                 // RomFS paths of the added files, sorted; added[k] is index file_count + k
static size_t nadded;

static void need(int c, const char *m) {
    if (!c) rt_fatal("RomFS: %s", m);
}

static Entry entry(uint64_t i) {
    Entry e;
    memcpy(&e, index_bytes + 24 + i * 24, 24);
    return e;
}
static const char *entry_name(Entry e) { return (const char *)index_bytes + strings_offset + e.name; }

static double now_s(void) {
    LARGE_INTEGER t, f;
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&t);
    QueryPerformanceFrequency(&f);
    return (double)t.QuadPart / (double)f.QuadPart;
}

// ---- positional reads
// Bytes read at off (0 at or past the end of the file), -1 on an I/O error. Works on synchronous and
// FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED handles; the event is per thread, so concurrent reads on one handle do not share it.
static int64_t read_at(HANDLE f, void *buf, uint32_t n, uint64_t off) {
    static _Thread_local HANDLE ev;
    if (!ev && !(ev = CreateEventW(NULL, TRUE, FALSE, NULL)))
        rt_fatal("RomFS: CreateEvent failed (%lu)", GetLastError());
    OVERLAPPED ov = {.Offset = (DWORD)off, .OffsetHigh = (DWORD)(off >> 32), .hEvent = ev};
    DWORD got = 0;
    mem_thaw((uintptr_t)buf, n);   // the kernel's write would fail on a frozen page instead of faulting
    if (!ReadFile(f, buf, n, &got, &ov)) {
        DWORD e = GetLastError();
        if (e == ERROR_HANDLE_EOF) return 0;
        if (e == ERROR_IO_PENDING && !GetOverlappedResult(f, &ov, &got, TRUE)) e = GetLastError();
        else if (e == ERROR_IO_PENDING) return got;
        if (e == ERROR_HANDLE_EOF) return 0;
        if (e == ERROR_NOACCESS)   // a read-only page in the buffer: a frozen region missed its thaw
            rt_log("RomFS: read of %u bytes into %p refused: the buffer is not writable", n, buf);
        return -1;
    }
    return got;
}

static HANDLE open_read(const char *path, int overlapped) {
    wchar_t *w = fs_wide(path);
    HANDLE h = CreateFileW(w, GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ, NULL, OPEN_EXISTING,
                           FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL | (overlapped ? FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED : 0), NULL);
    free(w);
    return h;
}

static Identity identity_of(HANDLE f) {
    BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION i;
    need(GetFileInformationByHandle(f, &i), "file information");
    return (Identity){i.dwVolumeSerialNumber, 0, (uint64_t)i.nFileIndexHigh << 32 | i.nFileIndexLow,
                      (uint64_t)i.nFileSizeHigh << 32 | i.nFileSizeLow,
                      (uint64_t)i.ftLastWriteTime.dwHighDateTime << 32 | i.ftLastWriteTime.dwLowDateTime,
                      (uint64_t)i.ftCreationTime.dwHighDateTime << 32 | i.ftCreationTime.dwLowDateTime};
}

// ---- SHA-256 over a file range (BCrypt, streaming)
static void hex32(const uint8_t d[32], char out[65]) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) snprintf(out + 2 * i, 3, "%02x", d[i]);
}

static void sha_range(HANDLE f, uint64_t offset, uint64_t size, char hex[65], int progress) {
    BCRYPT_ALG_HANDLE alg;
    BCRYPT_HASH_HANDLE h;
    need(!BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider(&alg, BCRYPT_SHA256_ALGORITHM, NULL, 0) &&
         !BCryptCreateHash(alg, &h, NULL, 0, NULL, 0, 0), "SHA-256 provider");
    uint8_t *buf = malloc(HASH_CHUNK);
    need(buf != NULL, "hash buffer");
    double t0 = now_s();
    for (uint64_t done = 0; done < size;) {
        uint32_t want = size - done > HASH_CHUNK ? HASH_CHUNK : (uint32_t)(size - done);
        int64_t n = read_at(f, buf, want, offset + done);
        need(n > 0, "read of hash input");
        need(!BCryptHashData(h, buf, (ULONG)n, 0), "SHA-256 update");
        done += (uint64_t)n;
        if (progress && (done % (2ull << 30) < (uint64_t)n || done == size))
            rt_log("RomFS: hashed %.1f of %.1f GiB (%.0f MiB/s)", done / 1073741824.0, size / 1073741824.0,
                   done / 1048576.0 / (now_s() - t0 + 1e-9));
    }
    uint8_t d[32];
    need(!BCryptFinishHash(h, d, 32, 0), "SHA-256 final");
    BCryptDestroyHash(h);
    BCryptCloseAlgorithmProvider(alg, 0);
    free(buf);
    hex32(d, hex);
}

// ---- full image verification with a proof file
typedef struct { char magic[16], sha256[65]; uint8_t pad[7]; Identity id; } RomfsProof;

static void verify_image(const char *dir) {
    const char *mode = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_VERIFY");
    if (!mode || (strcmp(mode, "full") && strcmp(mode, "force"))) return;
    const char *pdir = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_PROOF_DIR");
    if (pdir && *pdir) dir = pdir;
    RomfsProof want = {0}, saved;
    memcpy(want.magic, "TOTKRFS-PROOF-1", 16);
    memcpy(want.sha256, ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256, sizeof ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256 < 65 ? sizeof ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256 : 65);
    want.id = identity_of(image);
    char path[2100], tmp[2200];
    need(snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/.romfs-verified-v1", dir) < (int)sizeof path, "proof path");
    if (strcmp(mode, "force")) {
        HANDLE p = open_read(path, 0);
        DWORD got = 0;
        if (p != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
            int ok = ReadFile(p, &saved, sizeof saved, &got, NULL) && got == sizeof saved;
            CloseHandle(p);
            if (ok && !memcmp(&saved, &want, sizeof want)) {
                rt_log("RomFS unchanged since its full SHA-256 check (%s)", path);
                return;
            }
        }
    }
    rt_log("RomFS: verifying the SHA-256 of %s (%llu bytes)", image_file, (unsigned long long)want.id.size);
    char hex[65];
    sha_range(image, 0, want.id.size, hex, 1);
    if (strcmp(hex, ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256))
        rt_fatal("RomFS image %s has SHA-256 %s, the extraction recorded %s (extract it again)", image_file, hex,
                 ROMFS_IMAGE_SHA256);
    Identity after = identity_of(image);
    need(!memcmp(&after, &want.id, sizeof after), "image changed during verification");
    snprintf(tmp, sizeof tmp, "%s.%lu.tmp", path, GetCurrentProcessId());
    wchar_t *wt = fs_wide(tmp), *wp = fs_wide(path);
    HANDLE out = CreateFileW(wt, GENERIC_WRITE, 0, NULL, CREATE_NEW, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, NULL);
    if (out != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        DWORD put = 0;
        int ok = WriteFile(out, &want, sizeof want, &put, NULL) && put == sizeof want && FlushFileBuffers(out);
        CloseHandle(out);
        if (!ok || !MoveFileExW(wt, wp, MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH)) DeleteFileW(wt);
    }
    free(wt);
    free(wp);
    rt_log("RomFS: image SHA-256 ok");
}

// ---- index lookup
static uint64_t lower(const char *name) {
    uint64_t lo = 0, hi = file_count;
    while (lo < hi) {
        uint64_t m = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (strcmp(entry_name(entry(m)), name) < 0) lo = m + 1;
        else hi = m;
    }
    return lo;
}

static size_t added_lower(const char *p) {
    size_t lo = 0, hi = nadded;
    while (lo < hi) {
        size_t m = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (strcmp(added[m], p) < 0) lo = m + 1;
        else hi = m;
    }
    return lo;
}

// The index of RomFS path p (an added file: file_count + k), or UINT64_MAX.
static uint64_t file_index(const char *p) {
    uint64_t i = lower(p);
    if (i < file_count && !strcmp(p, entry_name(entry(i)))) return i;
    size_t k = added_lower(p);
    return k < nadded && !strcmp(added[k], p) ? file_count + k : UINT64_MAX;
}

// 1 when a RomFS file or an added one lies under folder (a path ending in '/').
static int folder_exists(const char *folder) {
    size_t n = strlen(folder);
    uint64_t i = lower(folder);
    if (i < file_count && !strncmp(entry_name(entry(i)), folder, n)) return 1;
    size_t k = added_lower(folder);
    return k < nadded && !strncmp(added[k], folder, n);
}

// The overlay slot + 1 that replaces RomFS file i, or 0.
static uint32_t overlay_slot(uint64_t i) {
    size_t lo = 0, hi = noverlay;
    while (lo < hi) {
        size_t m = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
        if (overlays[m].index < i) lo = m + 1;
        else hi = m;
    }
    return lo < noverlay && overlays[lo].index == i ? (uint32_t)(lo + 1) : 0;
}

// ---- overlays
// Loads and checks one overlay folder. A failed check stops the game, except with optional set (the Xbox prompts
// folder): the folder is dropped, the reason logged, and 0 returned. Returns 1 when the folder is loaded or has no
// manifest.
static int overlay_load(const char *dir, int optional) {
#define BAD(...) do { if (!optional) rt_fatal(__VA_ARGS__); rt_log(__VA_ARGS__); goto bad; } while (0)
    char path[2100];
    need(snprintf(path, sizeof path, "%s/manifest.tsv", dir) < (int)sizeof path, "overlay path");
    wchar_t *w = fs_wide(path);
    FILE *m = _wfopen(w, L"rb");
    free(w);
    if (!m) {
        rt_log("RomFS overlay: none (%s)", path);
        return 1;
    }
    char line[8192];
    size_t first = noverlay;
    uint64_t hashed = 0;
    double t0 = now_s();
    while (fgets(line, sizeof line, m)) {
        if (line[0] == '#' || line[0] == '\n' || line[0] == '\r') continue;
        char name[4096], sha[65], orig[65], hex[65];
        unsigned long long size = 0;
        need(sscanf(line, "%4095[^\t]\t%llu\t%64[0-9a-f]\t%64[0-9a-f-]", name, &size, sha, orig) == 4 &&
             strlen(sha) == 64 && (strlen(orig) == 64 || !strcmp(orig, "-")), "overlay manifest line");
        need(romfs_path_valid_relative(name), "overlay path");
        uint64_t i = lower(name);
        int known = i < file_count && !strcmp(entry_name(entry(i)), name), add = !strcmp(orig, "-");
        if (!known && !add)
            BAD("RomFS overlay: %s/manifest.tsv names %s, which the RomFS lacks; a new file has \"-\" as its "
                "original's SHA-256", dir, name);
        if (known && add)
            BAD("RomFS overlay: %s/manifest.tsv adds %s, which the RomFS already has; give its original's SHA-256",
                dir, name);
        Entry e = {0};
        if (known) {
            e = entry(i);
            sha_range(image, e.offset, e.size, hex, 0);
            if (strcmp(hex, orig)) BAD("RomFS overlay: the original of %s has SHA-256 %s, %s/manifest.tsv says %s",
                                       name, hex, dir, orig);
        } else {
            i = ADDED;
        }
        char file[8200];
        need(snprintf(file, sizeof file, "%s/%s", dir, name) < (int)sizeof file, "overlay file path");
        HANDLE f = open_read(file, 1);
        if (f == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) BAD("RomFS overlay: %s missing", file);
        Identity id = identity_of(f);
        if (id.size != size) {
            CloseHandle(f);
            BAD("RomFS overlay: %s has %llu bytes, its manifest says %llu", file, (unsigned long long)id.size, size);
        }
        sha_range(f, 0, size, hex, 0);
        CloseHandle(f);
        if (strcmp(hex, sha)) BAD("RomFS overlay: %s has SHA-256 %s, its manifest says %s", file, hex, sha);
        hashed += e.size + size;
        if (noverlay == overlay_cap) {
            overlay_cap = overlay_cap ? overlay_cap * 2 : 16;
            overlays = realloc(overlays, overlay_cap * sizeof *overlays);
            need(overlays != NULL, "overlay table");
        }
        char *copy = _strdup(file), *rel = _strdup(name);
        need(copy && rel, "overlay path copy");
        overlays[noverlay++] = (Overlay){i, size, copy, rel, id};
        if (noverlay - first <= 16)
            rt_log("RomFS overlay: %s (%llu bytes) %s", name, size, add ? "is added" : "replaces the original");
    }
    fclose(m);
    if (noverlay - first > 16) rt_log("RomFS overlay: %zu files from %s (%zu not listed)", noverlay - first, dir,
                                      noverlay - first - 16);
    if (noverlay > first) rt_log("RomFS overlay: %s checked, %zu files, %.1f MiB hashed in %.2f s", dir,
                                 noverlay - first, hashed / 1048576.0, now_s() - t0);
    return 1;
bad:
    fclose(m);
    for (size_t k = first; k < noverlay; k++) {
        free((void *)overlays[k].path);
        free((void *)overlays[k].name);
    }
    noverlay = first;
    return 0;
#undef BAD
}

static int overlay_order(const void *a, const void *b) {
    uint64_t x = ((const Overlay *)a)->index, y = ((const Overlay *)b)->index;
    return (x > y) - (x < y);
}

static int added_order(const void *a, const void *b) {
    return strcmp((*(Overlay *const *)a)->name, (*(Overlay *const *)b)->name);
}

// Number the added files in path order after the RomFS's own (file_count + k); two overlays adding one path stop.
static void added_init(void) {
    Overlay **list = NULL;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < noverlay; k++)
        if (overlays[k].index == ADDED) {
            list = realloc(list, (nadded + 1) * sizeof *list);
            need(list != NULL, "added files");
            list[nadded++] = &overlays[k];
        }
    if (!nadded) return;
    qsort(list, nadded, sizeof *list, added_order);
    added = malloc(nadded * sizeof *added);
    need(added != NULL, "added files");
    for (size_t k = 0; k < nadded; k++) {
        if (k && !strcmp(list[k]->name, list[k - 1]->name))
            rt_fatal("RomFS overlay: %s and %s both add %s", list[k - 1]->path, list[k]->path, list[k]->name);
        list[k]->index = file_count + k;
        added[k] = list[k]->name;
    }
    free(list);
    rt_log("RomFS overlay: %zu files added to the RomFS", nadded);
}

// The HeapDef table a bigger game resolution needs (resolution.c): its texture heap and that heap's parent grow. The
// base is an overlay that replaces the table (a mod's heap sizes stay), else the RomFS original; the grown table is
// written to <profile>/resolution/ and served in the base's place.
#define HEAPDEF "System/HeapSize/Product.Nin_NX_NVN.HeapDef.byml.zs"
static void heapdef_overlay(void) {
    if (!res_heap_extra_kib()) return;
    uint64_t i = lower(HEAPDEF);
    if (i >= file_count || strcmp(entry_name(entry(i)), HEAPDEF)) {
        rt_log("RomFS: %s missing; the game keeps its own resolution", HEAPDEF);
        return;
    }
    Overlay *base = NULL;
    for (size_t k = 0; k < noverlay; k++)
        if (overlays[k].index == i) base = &overlays[k];
    HANDLE f = base ? open_read(base->path, 1) : image;
    uint64_t off = base ? 0 : entry(i).offset, n = base ? base->size : entry(i).size;
    void *in = n && n < (16u << 20) && f != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE ? malloc((size_t)n) : NULL;
    int ok = in && read_at(f, in, (uint32_t)n, off) == (int64_t)n;
    if (base && f != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) CloseHandle(f);
    void *out = NULL;
    size_t out_n = 0;
    ok = ok && res_heapdef_build(in, (size_t)n, &out, &out_n);
    free(in);
    if (!ok) return;
    char dir[2100], file[2200];
    need(snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, "%s/resolution", rt_config()->profile) < (int)sizeof dir, "resolution path");
    need(snprintf(file, sizeof file, "%s/Product.Nin_NX_NVN.HeapDef.byml.zs", dir) < (int)sizeof file, "resolution path");
    wchar_t *wd = fs_wide(dir), *wf = fs_wide(file);
    CreateDirectoryW(wd, NULL);
    HANDLE w = CreateFileW(wf, GENERIC_WRITE, 0, NULL, CREATE_ALWAYS, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, NULL);
    DWORD put = 0;
    ok = w != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE && WriteFile(w, out, (DWORD)out_n, &put, NULL) && put == out_n;
    if (w != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) CloseHandle(w);
    free(wd);
    free(wf);
    free(out);
    HANDLE r = ok ? open_read(file, 1) : INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
    if (r == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        rt_log("RomFS: cannot write %s (error %lu); the game keeps its own resolution", file, GetLastError());
        return;
    }
    Identity id = identity_of(r);
    CloseHandle(r);
    char *copy = _strdup(file);
    need(copy != NULL, "overlay path copy");
    if (base) {
        free(base->path);
        base->path = copy;
        base->size = out_n;
        base->id = id;
    } else {
        if (noverlay == overlay_cap) {
            overlay_cap = overlay_cap ? overlay_cap * 2 : 16;
            overlays = realloc(overlays, overlay_cap * sizeof *overlays);
            need(overlays != NULL, "overlay table");
        }
        char *rel = _strdup(HEAPDEF);
        need(rel != NULL, "overlay path copy");
        overlays[noverlay++] = (Overlay){i, out_n, copy, rel, id};
    }
    rt_log("RomFS overlay: %s (%zu bytes, grown heaps) replaces %s", file, out_n, base ? "the mod's table" : "the original");
    res_heapdef_served();
}

static int xbox_prompts_ready;    // romfs-patches-xbox/manifest.tsv was next to romfs-index.bin at start
static int xbox_prompts_active;   // and overlay_init loaded it

int romfs_xbox_prompts_ready(void) { return xbox_prompts_ready; }
int romfs_xbox_prompts_active(void) { return xbox_prompts_active; }

static void overlay_init(void) {
    // TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES unset: romfs-patches next to romfs-index.bin if it has a manifest (tools/make_romfs_patches.py).
    // A game resolution that is not 16:9 takes romfs-patches-<w>x<h> instead when it is there: the same overlay with
    // the UI laid out for that shape (make_romfs_patches.py --aspect). 1.2.1 has no camera aspect patch, so it keeps
    // the 16:9 layout (res_wants_wide_overlay).
    // With pad_layout = xbox_prompts, romfs-patches-xbox in its place: the same patches with the A/B and X/Y prompts
    // swapped (make_romfs_patches.py --xbox-prompts). The game reads the archives once at boot, so the prompts stay
    // until restart even though the layout itself changes live. Each folder replaces romfs-patches as a whole and the
    // setup builds no wide folder with Xbox prompts, so a wide game resolution keeps the Switch prompts.
    char def[2100], xbox[2100];
    const char *patches = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES");
    int wide = 0;
    unsigned out[2];
    res_wanted(out);
    if (!patches && res_wants_wide_overlay(out)) {
        if (snprintf(def, sizeof def, "%s/romfs-patches-%ux%u/manifest.tsv", index_dir, out[0], out[1]) < (int)sizeof def &&
            GetFileAttributesA(def) != INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES) {
            def[strlen(def) - strlen("/manifest.tsv")] = 0;
            patches = def, wide = 1;
        } else {
            rt_log("RomFS overlay: no romfs-patches-%ux%u for this game resolution, the UI keeps its 16:9 layout "
                   "(tools/make_romfs_patches.py --aspect %ux%u)", out[0], out[1], out[0], out[1]);
        }
    }
    xbox_prompts_ready =
        snprintf(xbox, sizeof xbox, "%s/romfs-patches-xbox/manifest.tsv", index_dir) < (int)sizeof xbox &&
        GetFileAttributesA(xbox) != INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES;
    int want_xbox = !_stricmp(cfg_value("TOTK_PAD_LAYOUT"), "xbox_prompts");
    if (!patches && want_xbox && xbox_prompts_ready) {
        xbox[strlen(xbox) - strlen("/manifest.tsv")] = 0;
        xbox_prompts_active = overlay_load(xbox, 1);
        if (xbox_prompts_active) rt_log("RomFS overlay: Xbox button prompts (%s)", xbox);
        else rt_log("RomFS overlay: %s failed its check (run the setup again); romfs-patches loads instead", xbox);
    } else if (want_xbox) {
        rt_log("RomFS overlay: pad_layout = xbox_prompts, but %s; Switch prompts stay",
               wide      ? "the game resolution takes the wide UI layout"
               : patches ? "TOTK_ROMFS_PATCHES is set"
                         : "romfs-patches-xbox has no manifest.tsv (run the setup again)");
    }
    if (!patches && !xbox_prompts_active && snprintf(def, sizeof def, "%s/romfs-patches/manifest.tsv", index_dir) < (int)sizeof def &&
        GetFileAttributesA(def) != INVALID_FILE_ATTRIBUTES) {
        def[strlen(def) - strlen("/manifest.tsv")] = 0;
        patches = def;
    }
    const char *dirs[2] = {patches, cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_MODS")};
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)
        if (dirs[i] && *dirs[i] && strcmp(dirs[i], "0")) overlay_load(dirs[i], 0);
    heapdef_overlay();
    added_init();
    if (noverlay) qsort(overlays, noverlay, sizeof *overlays, overlay_order);
    for (size_t k = 1; k < noverlay; k++)
        if (overlays[k].index == overlays[k - 1].index)
            rt_fatal("RomFS overlay: %s and %s replace the same file %s", overlays[k - 1].path, overlays[k].path,
                     overlays[k].name);
}

// ---- start
// romfs-index.bin next to totk.exe, or TOTK_ROMFS_INDEX.
static void index_path(char *out, size_t cap) {
    const char *e = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_INDEX");
    if (e && *e) {
        need(snprintf(out, cap, "%s", e) < (int)cap, "index path");
        return;
    }
    wchar_t exe[MAX_PATH * 2];
    DWORD n = GetModuleFileNameW(NULL, exe, MAX_PATH * 2);
    need(n && n < MAX_PATH * 2, "executable path");
    while (n && exe[n - 1] != L'\\' && exe[n - 1] != L'/') n--;
    exe[n] = 0;
    int k = WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, exe, -1, out, (int)cap, NULL, NULL);
    need(k > 0 && (size_t)k + 16 < cap, "executable path");
    strcat(out, "romfs-index.bin");
}

static void load_index(void) {
    char path[2100];
    index_path(path, sizeof path);
    snprintf(index_dir, sizeof index_dir, "%s", path);
    char *sep = strrchr(index_dir, '\\'), *slash = strrchr(index_dir, '/');
    if (slash > sep) sep = slash;
    if (sep) *sep = 0;
    else strcpy(index_dir, ".");
    HANDLE f = open_read(path, 0);
    if (f == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE)
        rt_fatal("RomFS index %s missing (tools/build_game.py writes it next to totk.exe)", path);
    LARGE_INTEGER sz;
    need(GetFileSizeEx(f, &sz) && sz.QuadPart >= 24 && sz.QuadPart < (128 << 20), "index size");
    index_size = (size_t)sz.QuadPart;
    index_bytes = malloc(index_size);
    need(index_bytes != NULL, "index allocation");
    for (size_t done = 0; done < index_size;) {
        DWORD got = 0;
        need(ReadFile(f, index_bytes + done, (DWORD)(index_size - done), &got, NULL) && got, "index read");
        done += got;
    }
    CloseHandle(f);
    uint8_t d[32];
    char hex[65];
    rt_sha256(index_bytes, index_size, d);
    hex32(d, hex);
    if (strcmp(hex, ROMFS_INDEX_SHA256))
        rt_fatal("RomFS index %s has SHA-256 %s, this build expects %s (rebuild with tools/build_game.py)", path, hex,
                 ROMFS_INDEX_SHA256);
    need(!memcmp(index_bytes, "TOTKRFS1", 8), "index format");
    memcpy(&file_count, index_bytes + 8, 8);
    memcpy(&strings_offset, index_bytes + 16, 8);
    need(file_count == ROMFS_FILE_COUNT && file_count < 1000000 && strings_offset == 24 + file_count * 24 &&
         strings_offset < index_size, "index layout");
    const char *previous = NULL;
    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < file_count; i++) {
        Entry e = entry(i);
        need(e.offset <= ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE && e.size <= ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE - e.offset, "file bounds");
        need(e.name < index_size - strings_offset && e.len > 1 && e.len <= index_size - strings_offset - e.name,
             "name bounds");
        const char *name = entry_name(e);
        need(name[e.len - 1] == 0 && strlen(name) == e.len - 1 && (!previous || strcmp(previous, name) < 0),
             "sorted paths");
        previous = name;
    }
    rt_log("RomFS index %s: SHA-256 ok, %llu files, %zu bytes", path, (unsigned long long)file_count, index_size);
}

static BOOL CALLBACK init_once(PINIT_ONCE once, PVOID param, PVOID *ctx) {
    (void)once, (void)param, (void)ctx;
#ifdef ROMFS_MISSING
    rt_fatal("this build has no RomFS: tools/build_game.py found no index.json in its --romfs directory");
#else
    double t0 = now_s();
    load_index();
    const char *dir = rt_config()->romfs;
    need(snprintf(image_file, sizeof image_file, "%s/romfs.bin", dir) < (int)sizeof image_file, "image path");
    image = open_read(image_file, 1);
    if (image == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) rt_fatal("RomFS image %s missing (error %lu); put romfs.bin into the romfs folder next to totk.exe or set TOTK_ROMFS",
                                          image_file, GetLastError());
    LARGE_INTEGER sz;
    need(GetFileSizeEx(image, &sz), "image size");
    if ((uint64_t)sz.QuadPart != ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE)
        rt_fatal("RomFS image %s has %llu bytes, the index was built for %llu", image_file,
                 (unsigned long long)sz.QuadPart, (unsigned long long)ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE);
    rt_log("RomFS image %s: size ok (%llu bytes)", image_file, (unsigned long long)ROMFS_IMAGE_SIZE);
    verify_image(index_dir);
    const char *mm = cfg_get("TOTK_ROMFS_MMAP");
    if (mm && strcmp(mm, "0")) {
        HANDLE map = CreateFileMappingW(image, NULL, PAGE_READONLY, 0, 0, NULL);
        const void *v = map ? MapViewOfFile(map, FILE_MAP_READ, 0, 0, 0) : NULL;
        if (map) CloseHandle(map);   // the view keeps the mapping alive
        if (v) {
            image_map = v;
            rt_log("RomFS: mapped read path enabled");
        } else {
            rt_log("RomFS: mapping failed (error %lu); using ReadFile", GetLastError());
        }
    }
    overlay_init();
    rt_log("RomFS ready: %llu files, %zu overlays, %zu added, %.2f s", (unsigned long long)file_count, noverlay,
           nadded, now_s() - t0);
#endif
    return TRUE;
}

void fs_init(void) {
    static INIT_ONCE once = INIT_ONCE_STATIC_INIT;
    InitOnceExecuteOnce(&once, init_once, NULL, NULL);
}

// ---- the RomFS interface (fs.h)
void fs_trace(const char *what, const char *path) {
    static double t0;
    if (!(rt_trace & RT_TRACE_FS)) return;
    if (!t0) t0 = now_s();
    rt_log("fs %8.3f %s %s", now_s() - t0, what, path ? path : "(null)");
}

uint64_t romfs_file_count(void) { return file_count; }

const char *romfs_entry(uint64_t i, uint64_t *offset, uint64_t *size) {
    if (i >= file_count) return NULL;
    Entry e = entry(i);
    if (offset) *offset = e.offset;
    if (size) *size = e.size;
    return entry_name(e);
}

const char *romfs_image_path(void) { return image_file; }

size_t romfs_overlay_count(void) { return noverlay; }

const char *romfs_overlay(size_t k, const char **file, uint64_t *size, int *is_added) {
    if (k >= noverlay) return NULL;
    *file = overlays[k].path;
    *size = overlays[k].size;
    *is_added = overlays[k].index >= file_count;
    return overlays[k].name;
}

int romfs_owns(const char *path) {
    size_t n = strlen(mount_name);
    return n && path && !strncmp(path, mount_name, n) && path[n] == ':';
}

int romfs_handle(uint64_t h) { return h > ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE && h < ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE + NH; }

uint32_t romfs_mount(const char *name) {
    fs_init();
    if (!name || !romfs_path_valid_relative(name) || strlen(name) >= sizeof mount_name || strchr(name, '/') ||
        strchr(name, ':'))
        return FS_R_INVALID;
    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
    if (*mount_name && strcmp(name, mount_name)) rt_fatal("second RomFS mount %s (%s is mounted)", name, mount_name);
    strcpy(mount_name, name);
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
    rt_log("fs mount %s: -> RomFS", name);
    return 0;
}

uint32_t romfs_open(uint64_t *out, const char *path, int mode) {
    fs_trace("rom", path);
    if (!out || mode != FS_OPEN_READ) return FS_R_UNSUPPORTED_OPEN;
    const char *p = romfs_path_relative(mount_name, path);
    if (!p) return FS_R_PATH_NOT_FOUND;
    uint64_t i = file_index(p);
    if (i == UINT64_MAX) return FS_R_PATH_NOT_FOUND;
    uint32_t ov = overlay_slot(i);
    HANDLE f = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
    if (ov) {
        const Overlay *o = &overlays[ov - 1];
        f = open_read(o->path, 1);
        Identity id;
        if (f != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) id = identity_of(f);
        if (f == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE || memcmp(&id, &o->id, sizeof id))
            rt_fatal("RomFS overlay %s is missing or changed since the start check (restart the game)", o->path);
    }
    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
    for (unsigned j = 1; j < NH; j++)
        if (!handles[j]) {
            handles[j] = i + 1;
            handle_ovl[j] = ov;
            handle_file[j] = f;
            *out = ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE + j;
            ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
            return 0;
        }
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
    rt_fatal("RomFS file handle table full (%d)", NH);
}

// The handle's index row (an added file's is empty: its bytes are all in its overlay), and where its bytes come from:
// the overlay file, or the original's range of the image.
static int handle_source(uint64_t h, HANDLE *f, uint64_t *base, uint64_t *size) {
    if (!romfs_handle(h)) return 0;
    uint64_t j = h - ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE;
    AcquireSRWLockShared(&lock);
    uint64_t i = handles[j];
    uint32_t ov = handle_ovl[j];
    HANDLE of = handle_file[j];
    ReleaseSRWLockShared(&lock);
    if (!i) return 0;
    if (ov) {
        *f = of;
        *base = 0;
        *size = overlays[ov - 1].size;
    } else {
        Entry e = entry(i - 1);
        *f = image;
        *base = e.offset;
        *size = e.size;
    }
    return 1;
}

uint32_t romfs_read(uint64_t *out, uint64_t h, int64_t offset, void *buffer, uint64_t size) {
    HANDLE f;
    uint64_t base, fsize;
    if (!out || offset < 0 || !handle_source(h, &f, &base, &fsize)) return FS_R_INVALID;
    if ((uint64_t)offset > fsize || (!buffer && size)) return FS_R_INVALID;
    uint64_t n = size < fsize - (uint64_t)offset ? size : fsize - (uint64_t)offset, done = 0;
    if (f == image && image_map) {
        memcpy(buffer, image_map + base + (uint64_t)offset, (size_t)n);
        done = n;
    }
    while (done < n) {
        uint32_t chunk = n - done > READ_CHUNK ? READ_CHUNK : (uint32_t)(n - done);
        int64_t r = read_at(f, (uint8_t *)buffer + done, chunk, base + (uint64_t)offset + done);
        if (r <= 0) rt_fatal("RomFS read failure at %#llx (error %lu)", (unsigned long long)(base + offset + done),
                             GetLastError());
        done += (uint64_t)r;
    }
    *out = done;
    return 0;
}

uint32_t romfs_size(int64_t *out, uint64_t h) {
    HANDLE f;
    uint64_t base, size;
    if (!out || !handle_source(h, &f, &base, &size)) return FS_R_INVALID;
    *out = (int64_t)size;
    return 0;
}

void romfs_close(uint64_t h) {
    HANDLE f;
    uint64_t base, size;
    if (!handle_source(h, &f, &base, &size))
        rt_fatal("RomFS: close of invalid file handle %#llx", (unsigned long long)h);
    uint64_t j = h - ROMFS_HANDLE_BASE;
    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
    HANDLE of = handle_ovl[j] ? handle_file[j] : INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
    handles[j] = 0;
    handle_ovl[j] = 0;
    handle_file[j] = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
    if (of != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) CloseHandle(of);
}

uint32_t romfs_entry_type(int *out, const char *path) {
    if (!out) return FS_R_INVALID;
    const char *p = romfs_path_relative(mount_name, path);
    if (!p) return FS_R_PATH_NOT_FOUND;
    if (file_index(p) != UINT64_MAX) {
        *out = FS_ENTRY_FILE;
        return 0;
    }
    char dir[4096];
    if (snprintf(dir, sizeof dir, "%s/", p) >= (int)sizeof dir) return FS_R_INVALID;
    if (folder_exists(dir)) {
        *out = FS_ENTRY_DIRECTORY;
        return 0;
    }
    return FS_R_PATH_NOT_FOUND;
}

// ---- overrides
// nn::Result nn::fs::MountRom(const char *name, void *cache, size_t cache_size)
static void ov_mount_rom(Cpu *c) { ret_x(c, romfs_mount(arg_p(c, 0))); }
// nn::Result nn::fs::QueryMountRomCacheSize(size_t *out): no cache needed, the host reads the image directly
static void ov_query_cache(Cpu *c) {
    uint64_t *out = arg_p(c, 0);
    if (out) *out = 0;
    ret_x(c, out ? 0 : FS_R_INVALID);
}
// void nn::fs::InitializeForApplication(): SDK-internal; opens the index instead of the fs service session
static void ov_initialize(Cpu *c) {
    (void)c;
    fs_init();
}

HOST_OVERRIDE("_ZN2nn2fs8MountRomEPKcPvm", ov_mount_rom);
HOST_OVERRIDE("_ZN2nn2fs22QueryMountRomCacheSizeEPm", ov_query_cache);
HOST_OVERRIDE("_ZN2nn2fs24InitializeForApplicationEv", ov_initialize);
```

`runtime/romfs_path.h`:

```h
// From MacNativeGames games/totk/runtime/romfs_path.h @ b75be8cf (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 MacNativeGames
// contributors).
// RomFS path validation shared by the runtime (romfs.c) and its probe (fs_host.c probe_fs).
#pragma once
#include <stddef.h>
#include <string.h>

// A RomFS-relative path: non-empty, no leading '/', no '\', no empty, "." or ".." component.
static inline int romfs_path_valid_relative(const char *path) {
    if (!path || !*path || *path == '/' || strchr(path, '\\')) return 0;
    for (const char *part = path; *part;) {
        const char *end = strchr(part, '/');
        size_t size = end ? (size_t)(end - part) : strlen(part);
        if (!size || (size == 1 && part[0] == '.') || (size == 2 && part[0] == '.' && part[1] == '.')) return 0;
        if (!end) break;
        part = end + 1;
    }
    return 1;
}

// "<mount>:/<path>" -> "<path>", or NULL. Audio stream requests join a mount root and a leading-slash resource,
// producing "content://Sound/...": repeated root separators are skipped; traversal, backslashes and empty interior
// components are still rejected.
static inline const char *romfs_path_relative(const char *mount, const char *path) {
    if (!mount || !*mount || !path) return NULL;
    size_t size = strlen(mount);
    if (strncmp(path, mount, size) || path[size] != ':' || path[size + 1] != '/') return NULL;
    path += size + 2;
    while (*path == '/') ++path;
    return romfs_path_valid_relative(path) ? path : NULL;
}
```

`runtime/shaders/astc_decode.comp`:

```comp
// ASTC LDR 2D decode to RGBA8 on the GPU, one invocation per texel. Ported from runtime/tex_astc.c (itself from LAS
// Recomp runtime/nvn/astc.c @ da35b83a, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Peiikai), so the output is the same bytes as
// astc_decode_ldr and astcenc's 8-bit decode: endpoints expand to 16 bits (linear v * 257, sRGB v << 8 | 0x80),
// texel = (e0 * (64 - w) + e1 * w + 32) >> 6, top 8 bits. Error blocks are magenta; HDR endpoint modes give magenta
// endpoints for their partition.
//
// A workgroup of 64 lanes takes up to four blocks of one block row (main below): every lane decodes its block's header,
// the block's lanes share the integer-sequence decode of its weights and colour values through shared memory, and
// each lane then interpolates its own texels.
// Compiled to runtime/astc_decode_spv.h by tools/build_shaders.py; vk_astc.c records the dispatch.
#version 450

layout(local_size_x = 64, local_size_y = 1, local_size_z = 1) in;

layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer Blocks { uvec4 blk[]; };
layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 1) writeonly buffer Texels { uint px[]; };
// uint 0..11: byte offsets of the weight unquantization rows (QUANT_2..QUANT_32), 12..27: of the colour rows
// (QUANT_6..QUANT_256 minus one); the bytes follow (vk_astc.c astc_tables).
layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 2) readonly buffer Tables { uint tab[]; };

layout(push_constant) uniform Params {
    uint in_base;    // first block of slice 0 (uvec4 index into blk)
    uint out_base;   // first texel of slice 0 (index into px)
    uint width, height;
    uint bw, bh;     // block footprint
    uint bx;         // blocks per row
    uint bslice;     // blocks per slice
    uint srgb;
} pc;

uint tab_byte(uint i) { return (tab[i >> 2] >> ((i & 3u) * 8u)) & 0xFFu; }

// n (<= 32) bits at pos; bits past 127 read as zero.
uint rbits(uvec4 b, int pos, int n) {
    if (n == 0 || pos >= 128) return 0u;
    int wi = pos >> 5, sh = pos & 31;
    uint v = b[wi] >> uint(sh);
    if (sh != 0 && wi < 3) v |= b[wi + 1] << uint(32 - sh);
    return n >= 32 ? v : v & ((1u << uint(n)) - 1u);
}

// Quantization levels QUANT_2 .. QUANT_256 (0..20): bits, trits, quints of tex_astc.c q_bits / q_trits / q_quints.
int q_bits(int q) {
    if (q < 2) return q == 0 ? 1 : 0;
    int g = (q - 2) / 3, r = (q - 2) - 3 * g;
    return r == 0 ? g + 2 : r == 1 ? g : g + 1;
}
bool q_trit(int q) { return q == 1 || (q >= 2 && (q - 2) % 3 == 2); }
bool q_quint(int q) { return q >= 2 && (q - 2) % 3 == 1; }

int ise_bitcount(int count, int q) {
    int n = count * q_bits(q);
    if (q_trit(q)) n += (8 * count + 4) / 5;
    if (q_quint(q)) n += (7 * count + 2) / 3;
    return n;
}

int trit_at(uint T, int k) {
    uint C;
    int t0, t1, t2, t3, t4;
    if (((T >> 2) & 7u) == 7u) {
        C = ((T >> 5) & 7u) << 2 | (T & 3u);
        t4 = 2; t3 = 2;
    } else {
        C = T & 0x1Fu;
        if (((T >> 5) & 3u) == 3u) { t4 = 2; t3 = int((T >> 7) & 1u); }
        else { t4 = int((T >> 7) & 1u); t3 = int((T >> 5) & 3u); }
    }
    if ((C & 3u) == 3u) {
        t2 = 2; t1 = int((C >> 4) & 1u);
        t0 = int(((C >> 3) & 1u) << 1 | (((C >> 2) & 1u) & ~(C >> 3) & 1u));
    } else if (((C >> 2) & 3u) == 3u) {
        t2 = 2; t1 = 2; t0 = int(C & 3u);
    } else {
        t2 = int((C >> 4) & 1u); t1 = int((C >> 2) & 3u);
        t0 = int(((C >> 1) & 1u) << 1 | ((C & 1u) & ~(C >> 1) & 1u));
    }
    return k == 0 ? t0 : k == 1 ? t1 : k == 2 ? t2 : k == 3 ? t3 : t4;
}

int quint_at(uint Q, int k) {
    int q0, q1, q2;
    if (((Q >> 1) & 3u) == 3u && ((Q >> 5) & 3u) == 0u) {
        uint b0 = Q & 1u;
        q2 = int(b0 << 2 | (((Q >> 4) & 1u) & ~b0 & 1u) << 1 | (((Q >> 3) & 1u) & ~b0 & 1u));
        q1 = 4; q0 = 4;
    } else {
        uint C;
        if (((Q >> 1) & 3u) == 3u) { q2 = 4; C = ((Q >> 3) & 3u) << 3 | (~(Q >> 5) & 3u) << 1 | (Q & 1u); }
        else { q2 = int((Q >> 5) & 3u); C = Q & 0x1Fu; }
        if ((C & 7u) == 5u) { q1 = 4; q0 = int((C >> 3) & 3u); }
        else { q1 = int((C >> 3) & 3u); q0 = int(C & 7u); }
    }
    return k == 0 ? q0 : k == 1 ? q1 : q2;
}

// Raw ISE value idx (trit/quint << bits | bits) of a sequence of count values at bit start; tex_astc.c ise_decode
// reads the sequence front to back, this reads one value's group only. Bits of values past count are not read.
uint ise_at(uvec4 b, int start, int count, int q, int idx) {
    int nb = q_bits(q);
    if (q_trit(q)) {
        // value k of a group: nb bits at k * nb + ts[k], then tb[k] trit bits; ts = {0, 2, 4, 5, 7}, tb = {2, 2, 1, 2, 1}
        int g = idx / 5, k = idx - 5 * g, gs = start + g * (5 * nb + 8);
        uint m = rbits(b, gs + k * nb + (k * 7 + 2) / 4, nb);
        uint T = 0u;
        for (int j = 0; j < 5; j++) {
            int ts = (j * 7 + 2) / 4, tb = j == 2 || j == 4 ? 1 : 2;
            if (5 * g + j < count) T |= rbits(b, gs + (j + 1) * nb + ts, tb) << uint(ts);
        }
        return uint(trit_at(T, k)) << uint(nb) | m;
    }
    if (q_quint(q)) {
        // qs = {0, 3, 5}, qb = {3, 2, 2}
        int g = idx / 3, k = idx - 3 * g, gs = start + g * (3 * nb + 7);
        uint m = rbits(b, gs + k * nb + (k == 0 ? 0 : k == 1 ? 3 : 5), nb);
        uint Q = 0u;
        for (int j = 0; j < 3; j++) {
            int qs = j == 0 ? 0 : j == 1 ? 3 : 5, qb = j == 0 ? 3 : 2;
            if (3 * g + j < count) Q |= rbits(b, gs + (j + 1) * nb + qs, qb) << uint(qs);
        }
        return uint(quint_at(Q, k)) << uint(nb) | m;
    }
    return rbits(b, start + idx * nb, nb);
}

uint hash52(uint p) {
    p ^= p >> 15; p -= p << 17; p += p << 7; p += p << 4;
    p ^= p >> 5;  p += p << 16; p ^= p >> 7; p ^= p >> 3;
    p ^= p << 6;  p ^= p >> 17;
    return p;
}

int part_of(int seed, int count, int x, int y) {
    seed += (count - 1) * 1024;
    uint rnum = hash52(uint(seed));
    int sh1, sh2;
    if ((seed & 1) != 0) { sh1 = (seed & 2) != 0 ? 4 : 5; sh2 = count == 3 ? 6 : 5; }
    else { sh1 = count == 3 ? 6 : 5; sh2 = (seed & 2) != 0 ? 4 : 5; }
    int s[8];
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
        int v = int((rnum >> uint(4 * i)) & 0xFu);
        s[i] = (v * v) >> ((i & 1) != 0 ? sh2 : sh1);
    }
    int a = int((uint(s[0] * x + s[1] * y) + (rnum >> 14)) & 0x3Fu);
    int b = int((uint(s[2] * x + s[3] * y) + (rnum >> 10)) & 0x3Fu);
    int c = count >= 3 ? int((uint(s[4] * x + s[5] * y) + (rnum >> 6)) & 0x3Fu) : 0;
    int d = count >= 4 ? int((uint(s[6] * x + s[7] * y) + (rnum >> 2)) & 0x3Fu) : 0;
    if (a >= b && a >= c && a >= d) return 0;
    if (b >= c && b >= d) return 1;
    if (c >= d) return 2;
    return 3;
}

int clamp255(int v) { return clamp(v, 0, 255); }

// v: the partition's unquantized colour values. False for an HDR mode.
bool unpack_endpoints(int cem, int v[8], out ivec4 e0, out ivec4 e1) {
    e0 = ivec4(0); e1 = ivec4(0);
    switch (cem) {
    case 0:
        e0 = ivec4(v[0], v[0], v[0], 255); e1 = ivec4(v[1], v[1], v[1], 255);
        return true;
    case 1: {
        int l0 = v[0] >> 2 | (v[1] & 0xC0);
        int l1 = min(l0 + (v[1] & 0x3F), 255);
        e0 = ivec4(l0, l0, l0, 255); e1 = ivec4(l1, l1, l1, 255);
        return true;
    }
    case 4:
        e0 = ivec4(v[0], v[0], v[0], v[2]); e1 = ivec4(v[1], v[1], v[1], v[3]);
        return true;
    case 5: {
        int l0 = v[0], l1 = v[1], a0 = v[2], a1 = v[3];
        l0 |= (l1 & 0x80) << 1; a0 |= (a1 & 0x80) << 1;
        l1 &= 0x7F; a1 &= 0x7F;
        if ((l1 & 0x40) != 0) l1 -= 0x80;
        if ((a1 & 0x40) != 0) a1 -= 0x80;
        l0 >>= 1; a0 >>= 1; l1 >>= 1; a1 >>= 1;
        l1 = clamp255(l1 + l0); a1 = clamp255(a1 + a0);
        e0 = ivec4(l0, l0, l0, a0); e1 = ivec4(l1, l1, l1, a1);
        return true;
    }
    case 6:
    case 10: {
        int s = v[3];
        e1 = ivec4(v[0], v[1], v[2], 255);
        e0 = ivec4(v[0] * s >> 8, v[1] * s >> 8, v[2] * s >> 8, 255);
        if (cem == 10) { e0.w = v[4]; e1.w = v[5]; }
        return true;
    }
    case 8:
    case 12: {
        ivec4 a = ivec4(v[0], v[2], v[4], cem == 12 ? v[6] : 0);
        ivec4 b = ivec4(v[1], v[3], v[5], cem == 12 ? v[7] : 0);
        if (a.x + a.y + a.z > b.x + b.y + b.z) {
            e0 = b; e1 = a;
            e0.x = (e0.x + e0.z) >> 1; e0.y = (e0.y + e0.z) >> 1;
            e1.x = (e1.x + e1.z) >> 1; e1.y = (e1.y + e1.z) >> 1;
        } else {
            e0 = a; e1 = b;
        }
        if (cem == 8) { e0.w = 255; e1.w = 255; }
        return true;
    }
    case 9:
    case 13: {
        ivec4 a = ivec4(0), b = ivec4(0);
        for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
            if (c == 3 && cem != 13) break;
            int base = v[2 * c], delta = v[2 * c + 1];
            a[c] = base >> 1 | (delta & 0x80);
            int d = (delta >> 1) & 0x3F;
            if ((d & 0x20) != 0) d -= 0x40;
            b[c] = d;
        }
        int sum = b.x + b.y + b.z;
        b += a;
        if (sum < 0) {
            e0 = b; e1 = a;
            e0.x = (e0.x + e0.z) >> 1; e0.y = (e0.y + e0.z) >> 1;
            e1.x = (e1.x + e1.z) >> 1; e1.y = (e1.y + e1.z) >> 1;
        } else {
            e0 = a; e1 = b;
        }
        e0 = clamp(e0, ivec4(0), ivec4(255)); e1 = clamp(e1, ivec4(0), ivec4(255));
        if (cem == 9) { e0.w = 255; e1.w = 255; }
        return true;
    }
    default:
        return false;
    }
}

const uint MAGENTA = 0xFFFF00FFu;

// What every texel of a block needs from its header (tex_astc.c astc_decode_block up to the weight infill).
struct Hdr {
    uint konst;      // the colour of a void-extent or error block
    bool solid;      // konst is the whole block
    int wx, wy, dual, quant, wtotal, pcount, cem0, cem1, cem2, cem3, n0, n1, n2, ccount, cq, ccs;
};

Hdr header(uvec4 b, int bw, int bh) {
    Hdr H;
    H.solid = true; H.konst = MAGENTA;
    H.wx = 0; H.wy = 0; H.dual = 0; H.quant = 0; H.wtotal = 0; H.pcount = 1;
    H.cem0 = 0; H.cem1 = 0; H.cem2 = 0; H.cem3 = 0; H.n0 = 0; H.n1 = 0; H.n2 = 0; H.ccount = 0; H.cq = 20; H.ccs = -1;
    uint mode = b.x & 0x7FFu;
    if ((mode & 0x1FFu) == 0x1FCu) {   // void extent
        if ((mode & 0x200u) != 0u || ((b.x >> 10) & 3u) != 3u) return H;
        uint s0 = rbits(b, 12, 13), s1 = rbits(b, 25, 13), t0 = rbits(b, 38, 13), t1 = rbits(b, 51, 13);
        bool all_ones = s0 == 0x1FFFu && s1 == 0x1FFFu && t0 == 0x1FFFu && t1 == 0x1FFFu;
        if ((s0 >= s1 || t0 >= t1) && !all_ones) return H;
        H.konst = (b.z >> 8 & 0xFFu) | (b.z >> 24) << 8 | (b.w >> 8 & 0xFFu) << 16 | (b.w >> 24) << 24;
        return H;
    }

    // block mode (tex_astc.c block_mode_2d)
    uint m = mode;
    uint r = (m >> 4) & 1u, h = (m >> 9) & 1u, d = (m >> 10) & 1u, a = (m >> 5) & 3u;
    int wx, wy;
    if ((m & 3u) != 0u) {
        r |= (m & 3u) << 1;
        uint bb = (m >> 7) & 3u;
        uint sel = (m >> 2) & 3u;
        if (sel == 0u) { wx = int(bb) + 4; wy = int(a) + 2; }
        else if (sel == 1u) { wx = int(bb) + 8; wy = int(a) + 2; }
        else if (sel == 2u) { wx = int(a) + 2; wy = int(bb) + 8; }
        else {
            bb &= 1u;
            if ((m & 0x100u) != 0u) { wx = int(bb) + 2; wy = int(a) + 2; }
            else { wx = int(a) + 2; wy = int(bb) + 6; }
        }
    } else {
        r |= ((m >> 2) & 3u) << 1;
        if (((m >> 2) & 3u) == 0u) return H;
        uint bb = (m >> 9) & 3u;
        uint sel = (m >> 7) & 3u;
        if (sel == 0u) { wx = 12; wy = int(a) + 2; }
        else if (sel == 1u) { wx = int(a) + 2; wy = 12; }
        else if (sel == 2u) { wx = int(a) + 6; wy = int(bb) + 6; d = 0u; h = 0u; }
        else {
            if (a == 0u) { wx = 6; wy = 10; }
            else if (a == 1u) { wx = 10; wy = 6; }
            else return H;
        }
    }
    int dual = int(d);
    int wtotal = (wx * wy) << dual;
    int quant = int(r) - 2 + 6 * int(h);
    int wbits = ise_bitcount(wtotal, quant);
    if (wtotal > 64 || wbits < 24 || wbits > 96 || wx > bw || wy > bh) return H;
    int pcount = int((b.x >> 11) & 3u) + 1;
    if (dual != 0 && pcount == 4) return H;

    // colour endpoint modes
    int cem0, cem1 = 0, cem2 = 0, cem3 = 0;
    int below = 128 - wbits, high = 0;
    if (pcount == 1) {
        cem0 = int((b.x >> 13) & 0xFu);
    } else {
        high = 3 * pcount - 4;
        below -= high;
        uint enc = ((b.x >> 23) & 0x3Fu) | rbits(b, below, high) << 6;
        uint base = enc & 3u;
        if (base == 0u) {
            cem0 = cem1 = cem2 = cem3 = int((enc >> 2) & 0xFu);
            below += high;
            high = 0;
        } else {
            base--;
            cem0 = int((((enc >> 2) & 1u) + base) << 2 | ((enc >> uint(2 + pcount)) & 3u));
            cem1 = int((((enc >> 3) & 1u) + base) << 2 | ((enc >> uint(4 + pcount)) & 3u));
            cem2 = int((((enc >> 4) & 1u) + base) << 2 | ((enc >> uint(6 + pcount)) & 3u));
            cem3 = int((((enc >> 5) & 1u) + base) << 2 | ((enc >> uint(8 + pcount)) & 3u));
        }
    }
    int n0 = ((cem0 >> 2) + 1) * 2, n1 = pcount > 1 ? ((cem1 >> 2) + 1) * 2 : 0;
    int n2 = pcount > 2 ? ((cem2 >> 2) + 1) * 2 : 0, n3 = pcount > 3 ? ((cem3 >> 2) + 1) * 2 : 0;
    int ccount = n0 + n1 + n2 + n3;
    if (ccount > 18) return H;
    int cbits = max((pcount == 1 ? 111 : 99) - wbits - high - (dual != 0 ? 2 : 0), 0);
    int cq = -1;
    for (int q = 20; q >= 0; q--) {
        if (ise_bitcount(ccount, q) <= cbits) { cq = q; break; }
    }
    if (cq < 4) return H;   // QUANT_6

    H.solid = false;
    H.wx = wx; H.wy = wy; H.dual = dual; H.quant = quant; H.wtotal = wtotal; H.pcount = pcount;
    H.cem0 = cem0; H.cem1 = cem1; H.cem2 = cem2; H.cem3 = cem3; H.n0 = n0; H.n1 = n1; H.n2 = n2;
    H.ccount = ccount; H.cq = cq;
    H.ccs = dual != 0 ? int(rbits(b, below - 2, 2)) : -1;
    return H;
}

// A workgroup decodes BPW blocks of one block row when a block has 64 texels or fewer (64 / texels of them), else one
// block: S lanes per block (its texels, at most 64). The lanes of a block decode its weights and colour values into
// shared memory, the first pcount lanes then unpack the endpoints, and each lane writes its texels.
const int MAXB = 4;   // 4x4: 4 blocks of 16 lanes
shared uint s_w[MAXB][64];       // unquantized weights 0..64 (dual plane: interleaved as in the bit stream)
shared int s_cv[MAXB][18];       // unquantized colour values
shared uvec2 s_e0[MAXB][4], s_e1[MAXB][4];   // 16-bit endpoints, two channels per uint

uvec2 pack16(ivec4 e) { return uvec2(uint(e.x) | uint(e.y) << 16, uint(e.z) | uint(e.w) << 16); }
int ch16(uvec2 p, int c) { return int(((c < 2 ? p.x : p.y) >> (16 * (c & 1))) & 0xFFFFu); }

void main() {
    int bw = int(pc.bw), bh = int(pc.bh), G = bw * bh;
    int bpw = G <= 64 ? 64 / G : 1, S = G <= 64 ? G : 64;
    int l = int(gl_LocalInvocationID.x), lb = l / S, lane = l - lb * S;
    bool live = lb < bpw;
    int bxi = int(gl_WorkGroupID.x) * bpw + lb, byi = int(gl_WorkGroupID.y);
    live = live && bxi < int(pc.bx);
    lb = min(lb, MAXB - 1);
    uvec4 b = live ? blk[pc.in_base + gl_WorkGroupID.z * pc.bslice + uint(byi) * pc.bx + uint(bxi)] : uvec4(0u);
    Hdr H = header(b, bw, bh);
    bool work = live && !H.solid;

    if (work) {
        uvec4 rev = uvec4(bitfieldReverse(b.w), bitfieldReverse(b.z), bitfieldReverse(b.y), bitfieldReverse(b.x));
        uint wrow = tab[H.quant];
        for (int j = lane; j < H.wtotal; j += S) s_w[lb][j] = tab_byte(wrow + ise_at(rev, 0, H.wtotal, H.quant, j));
        uint crow = H.cq == 20 ? 0u : tab[12 + H.cq - 4];
        int cstart = H.pcount == 1 ? 17 : 29;
        for (int j = lane; j < H.ccount; j += S) {
            uint raw = ise_at(b, cstart, H.ccount, H.cq, j);
            s_cv[lb][j] = H.cq == 20 ? int(raw) : int(tab_byte(crow + raw));
        }
    }
    barrier();
    if (work && lane < H.pcount) {
        int p = lane;
        int cem = p == 0 ? H.cem0 : p == 1 ? H.cem1 : p == 2 ? H.cem2 : H.cem3;
        int k = p == 0 ? 0 : p == 1 ? H.n0 : p == 2 ? H.n0 + H.n1 : H.n0 + H.n1 + H.n2;
        int n = ((cem >> 2) + 1) * 2;
        int v[8];
        for (int j = 0; j < 8; j++) {
            v[j] = 0;
            if (j < n) v[j] = s_cv[lb][k + j];
        }
        ivec4 e0, e1;
        if (!unpack_endpoints(cem, v, e0, e1)) { e0 = ivec4(0xFF, 0, 0xFF, 0xFF); e1 = e0; }
        if (pc.srgb != 0u) { e0 = e0 << 8 | 0x80; e1 = e1 << 8 | 0x80; }
        else { e0 *= 257; e1 *= 257; }
        s_e0[lb][p] = pack16(e0);
        s_e1[lb][p] = pack16(e1);
    }
    barrier();
    if (!live) return;

    bool small = G < 32;
    int seed = int((b.x >> 13) & 0x3FFu);
    int sx = int((1024 + bw / 2) / (bw - 1)), sy = int((1024 + bh / 2) / (bh - 1));
    for (int t = lane; t < G; t += S) {
        int x = t % bw, y = t / bw;
        uint gx = uint(bxi * bw + x), gy = uint(byi * bh + y);
        if (gx >= pc.width || gy >= pc.height) continue;
        uint o = H.konst;
        if (!H.solid) {
            int p = H.pcount > 1 ? part_of(seed, H.pcount, small ? x << 1 : x, small ? y << 1 : y) : 0;
            int vx = (sx * x * (H.wx - 1) + 32) >> 6, vy = (sy * y * (H.wy - 1) + 32) >> 6;
            int fs = vx & 0xF, ft = vy & 0xF;
            int i0 = (vy >> 4) * H.wx + (vx >> 4);
            int w11 = (fs * ft + 8) >> 4, w10 = fs - w11, w01 = ft - w11, w00 = 16 - fs - ft + w11;
            int wcount = H.wx * H.wy;
            int w[2];
            for (int pl = 0; pl < 2; pl++) {
                w[pl] = 0;
                if (pl > H.dual) continue;
                int acc = 0;
                for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
                    int idx = i0 + (c == 0 ? 0 : c == 1 ? 1 : c == 2 ? H.wx : H.wx + 1);
                    int f = c == 0 ? w00 : c == 1 ? w10 : c == 2 ? w01 : w11;
                    if (f == 0 || idx >= wcount) continue;
                    acc += int(s_w[lb][H.dual != 0 ? 2 * idx + pl : idx]) * f;
                }
                w[pl] = (acc + 8) >> 4;
            }
            uvec2 q0 = s_e0[lb][p], q1 = s_e1[lb][p];
            o = 0u;
            for (int c = 0; c < 4; c++) {
                int wc = c == H.ccs ? w[1] : w[0];
                o |= uint((ch16(q0, c) * (64 - wc) + ch16(q1, c) * wc + 32) >> 14) << uint(8 * c);
            }
        }
        px[pc.out_base + (gl_WorkGroupID.z * pc.height + gy) * pc.width + gx] = o;
    }
}
```

`runtime/shaders/bc3_encode.comp`:

```comp
// RGBA8 texels to BC3 blocks on the GPU, one invocation per 4x4 block: the second pass of the ASTC decode when
// TOTK_ASTC_BC is on (vk_astc.c), so a decoded ASTC texture takes 8 bits per texel in video memory instead of 32.
// Texels past the right or bottom edge repeat the last column or row.
//
// Colour: the BC1 four-colour block of the box around the block's colours, its diagonal turned to the sign of the
// colours' covariance and inset by 1/16 of the range (the bounding-box method of stb_dxt and of yuzu's BC1 recompression),
// then each texel takes the nearest of the four palette entries along that axis. Alpha: the eight-value BC3 alpha
// block between the block's smallest and largest alpha. The bytes are what the texels hold, so an sRGB image keeps
// sRGB-encoded values, as BC3_SRGB expects.
// Compiled to runtime/bc3_encode_spv.h by tools/build_shaders.py; vk_astc.c records the dispatch.
#version 450

layout(local_size_x = 8, local_size_y = 8, local_size_z = 1) in;

layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 0) readonly buffer Texels { uint px[]; };
layout(std430, set = 0, binding = 1) writeonly buffer Blocks { uvec4 blk[]; };

layout(push_constant) uniform Params {
    uint in_base;    // first texel of slice 0 (index into px)
    uint out_base;   // first block of slice 0 (uvec4 index into blk)
    uint width, height;
    uint bx;         // blocks per row
    uint bslice;     // blocks per slice
} pc;

vec4 texel(uint x, uint y, uint z) {
    x = min(x, pc.width - 1u), y = min(y, pc.height - 1u);
    return unpackUnorm4x8(px[pc.in_base + (z * pc.height + y) * pc.width + x]) * 255.0;
}

uint to565(vec3 c) {
    uvec3 q = uvec3(round(clamp(c, 0.0, 255.0) * vec3(31.0, 63.0, 31.0) / 255.0));
    return q.r << 11 | q.g << 5 | q.b;
}

vec3 from565(uint v) {
    return vec3(float(v >> 11 & 31u) * 255.0 / 31.0, float(v >> 5 & 63u) * 255.0 / 63.0, float(v & 31u) * 255.0 / 31.0);
}

void main() {
    uvec3 id = gl_GlobalInvocationID;
    uint by = (pc.height + 3u) / 4u;
    if (id.x >= pc.bx || id.y >= by) return;
    vec4 t[16];
    vec4 lo = vec4(255.0), hi = vec4(0.0), mean = vec4(0.0);
    for (uint i = 0u; i < 16u; i++) {
        t[i] = texel(id.x * 4u + (i & 3u), id.y * 4u + (i >> 2), id.z);
        lo = min(lo, t[i]), hi = max(hi, t[i]), mean += t[i];
    }
    mean /= 16.0;

    // alpha: a0 > a1 selects the eight-value mode; index 0 is a0, 1 is a1, 2..7 the six steps from a0 to a1
    uint a0 = uint(hi.a), a1 = uint(lo.a);
    uvec2 ab = uvec2(a0 | a1 << 8, 0u);
    if (a0 > a1) {
        float range = float(a0 - a1);
        for (uint i = 0u; i < 16u; i++) {
            uint s = uint(clamp(round((float(a0) - t[i].a) * 7.0 / range), 0.0, 7.0));   // 0 = a0 .. 7 = a1
            uint code = s == 0u ? 0u : s == 7u ? 1u : s + 1u;
            uint bit = 16u + 3u * i;
            if (bit < 32u) ab.x |= code << bit;
            if (bit + 3u > 32u) ab.y |= code >> (32u - min(bit, 32u)) << (bit > 32u ? bit - 32u : 0u);
        }
    }

    // colour: the box diagonal along the covariance of red and blue with green
    vec3 cmin = lo.rgb, cmax = hi.rgb;
    float crg = 0.0, cbg = 0.0;
    for (uint i = 0u; i < 16u; i++) {
        vec3 d = t[i].rgb - mean.rgb;
        crg += d.r * d.g, cbg += d.b * d.g;
    }
    if (crg < 0.0) { float s = cmin.r; cmin.r = cmax.r; cmax.r = s; }
    if (cbg < 0.0) { float s = cmin.b; cmin.b = cmax.b; cmax.b = s; }
    vec3 inset = (cmax - cmin) / 16.0;
    uint c0 = to565(cmax - inset), c1 = to565(cmin + inset);
    uint idx = 0u;
    if (c0 != c1) {
        if (c0 < c1) { uint s = c0; c0 = c1; c1 = s; }   // c0 > c1: the four-colour mode
        vec3 e0 = from565(c0), e1 = from565(c1), axis = e1 - e0;
        float len2 = max(dot(axis, axis), 1e-6);
        for (uint i = 0u; i < 16u; i++) {
            uint s = uint(clamp(round(dot(t[i].rgb - e0, axis) / len2 * 3.0), 0.0, 3.0));   // 0 = e0 .. 3 = e1
            uint code = s == 0u ? 0u : s == 3u ? 1u : s + 1u;   // palette order e0, e1, 2/3 e0 + 1/3 e1, 1/3 e0 + 2/3 e1
            idx |= code << (2u * i);
        }
    }
    blk[pc.out_base + id.z * pc.bslice + id.y * pc.bx + id.x] = uvec4(ab.x, ab.y, c0 | c1 << 16, idx);
}
```

```h
 A_STATIC AD1 APowD1(AD1 a,AD1 b){return AExp2D1(b*ALog2D1(a));}
 A_STATIC AF1 APowF1(AF1 a,AF1 b){return AExp2F1(b*ALog2F1(a));}
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 A_STATIC AD1 ARsqD1(AD1 a){return ARcpD1(ASqrtD1(a));}
 A_STATIC AF1 ARsqF1(AF1 a){return ARcpF1(ASqrtF1(a));}
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 A_STATIC AD1 ASatD1(AD1 a){return AMinD1(1.0,AMaxD1(0.0,a));}
 A_STATIC AF1 ASatF1(AF1 a){return AMinF1(1.0f,AMaxF1(0.0f,a));}

 AU1 ABfi(AU1 src,AU1 ins,AU1 mask){return (ins&mask)|(src&(~mask));}
 // Proxy for V_BFI_B32 where the 'mask' is set as 'bits', 'mask=(1<<bits)-1', and 'bits' needs to be an immediate.
 AU1 ABfiM(AU1 src,AU1 ins,AU1 bits){return bitfieldInsert(src,ins,0,ASU1(bits));}

 // V_MED3_F32.

  #endif
//==============================================================================================================================
  // Need to use manual unpack to get optimal execution (don't use packed types in buffers directly).
  // Unpack requires this pattern: https://gpuopen.com/first-steps-implementing-fp16/
  AH2 AH2_AU1_x(AU1 x){AF2 t=f16tof32(AU2(x&0xFFFF,x>>16));return AH2(t);}
  AH4 AH4_AU2_x(AU2 x){return AH4(AH2_AU1_x(x.x),AH2_AU1_x(x.y));}
  AW2 AW2_AU1_x(AU1 x){AU2 t=AU2(x&0xFFFF,x>>16);return AW2(t);}
  AW4 AW4_AU2_x(AU2 x){return AW4(AW2_AU1_x(x.x),AW2_AU1_x(x.y));}
  #define AH2_AU1(x) AH2_AU1_x(AU1(x))
  #define AH4_AU2(x) AH4_AU2_x(AU2(x))
  #define AW2_AU1(x) AW2_AU1_x(AU1(x))
  #define AW4_AU2(x) AW4_AU2_x(AU2(x))
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AU1 AU1_AH2_x(AH2 x){return f32tof16(x.x)+(f32tof16(x.y)<<16);}
  AU2 AU2_AH4_x(AH4 x){return AU2(AU1_AH2_x(x.xy),AU1_AH2_x(x.zw));}
  AU1 AU1_AW2_x(AW2 x){return AU1(x.x)+(AU1(x.y)<<16);}
  AU2 AU2_AW4_x(AW4 x){return AU2(AU1_AW2_x(x.xy),AU1_AW2_x(x.zw));}
  #define AU1_AH2(x) AU1_AH2_x(AH2(x))
  #define AU2_AH4(x) AU2_AH4_x(AH4(x))
  #define AU1_AW2(x) AU1_AW2_x(AW2(x))
  #define AU2_AW4(x) AU2_AW4_x(AW4(x))
//==============================================================================================================================
  #if defined(A_HLSL_6_2) && !defined(A_NO_16_BIT_CAST)
   #define AW1_AH1(x) asuint16(x)
   #define AW2_AH2(x) asuint16(x)
   #define AW3_AH3(x) asuint16(x)
   #define AW4_AH4(x) asuint16(x)
  #else
   #define AW1_AH1(a) AW1(f32tof16(AF1(a)))
   #define AW2_AH2(a) AW2(AW1_AH1((a).x),AW1_AH1((a).y))
   #define AW3_AH3(a) AW3(AW1_AH1((a).x),AW1_AH1((a).y),AW1_AH1((a).z))
   #define AW4_AH4(a) AW4(AW1_AH1((a).x),AW1_AH1((a).y),AW1_AH1((a).z),AW1_AH1((a).w))
  #endif
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  #if defined(A_HLSL_6_2) && !defined(A_NO_16_BIT_CAST)
   #define AH1_AW1(x) asfloat16(x)
   #define AH2_AW2(x) asfloat16(x)
   #define AH3_AW3(x) asfloat16(x)
   #define AH4_AW4(x) asfloat16(x)
  #else
   #define AH1_AW1(a) AH1(f16tof32(AU1(a)))
   #define AH2_AW2(a) AH2(AH1_AW1((a).x),AH1_AW1((a).y))
   #define AH3_AW3(a) AH3(AH1_AW1((a).x),AH1_AW1((a).y),AH1_AW1((a).z))
   #define AH4_AW4(a) AH4(AH1_AW1((a).x),AH1_AW1((a).y),AH1_AW1((a).z),AH1_AW1((a).w))
  #endif
//==============================================================================================================================
  AH1 AH1_x(AH1 a){return AH1(a);}
  AH2 AH2_x(AH1 a){return AH2(a,a);}
  AH3 AH3_x(AH1 a){return AH3(a,a,a);}

#ifdef A_GPU
 // Negative and positive infinity.
 #define A_INFP_F AF1_AU1(0x7f800000u)
 #define A_INFN_F AF1_AU1(0xff800000u)
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 // Copy sign from 's' to positive 'd'.
 AF1 ACpySgnF1(AF1 d,AF1 s){return AF1_AU1(AU1_AF1(d)|(AU1_AF1(s)&AU1_(0x80000000u)));}
 AF2 ACpySgnF2(AF2 d,AF2 s){return AF2_AU2(AU2_AF2(d)|(AU2_AF2(s)&AU2_(0x80000000u)));}
 AF3 ACpySgnF3(AF3 d,AF3 s){return AF3_AU3(AU3_AF3(d)|(AU3_AF3(s)&AU3_(0x80000000u)));}
 AF4 ACpySgnF4(AF4 d,AF4 s){return AF4_AU4(AU4_AF4(d)|(AU4_AF4(s)&AU4_(0x80000000u)));}
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 // Single operation to return (useful to create a mask to use in lerp for branch free logic),
 //  m=NaN := 0
 //  m>=0  := 0
 //  m<0   := 1
 // Uses the following useful floating point logic,
 //  saturate(+a*(-INF)==-INF) := 0
 //  saturate( 0*(-INF)== NaN) := 0
 //  saturate(-a*(-INF)==+INF) := 1
 AF1 ASignedF1(AF1 m){return ASatF1(m*AF1_(A_INFN_F));}
 AF2 ASignedF2(AF2 m){return ASatF2(m*AF2_(A_INFN_F));}
 AF3 ASignedF3(AF3 m){return ASatF3(m*AF3_(A_INFN_F));}
 AF4 ASignedF4(AF4 m){return ASatF4(m*AF4_(A_INFN_F));}
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 AF1 AGtZeroF1(AF1 m){return ASatF1(m*AF1_(A_INFP_F));}
 AF2 AGtZeroF2(AF2 m){return ASatF2(m*AF2_(A_INFP_F));}
 AF3 AGtZeroF3(AF3 m){return ASatF3(m*AF3_(A_INFP_F));}
 AF4 AGtZeroF4(AF4 m){return ASatF4(m*AF4_(A_INFP_F));}
//==============================================================================================================================
 #ifdef A_HALF
  #ifdef A_HLSL_6_2
   #define A_INFP_H AH1_AW1((uint16_t)0x7c00u)
   #define A_INFN_H AH1_AW1((uint16_t)0xfc00u)
  #else
   #define A_INFP_H AH1_AW1(0x7c00u)
   #define A_INFN_H AH1_AW1(0xfc00u)
  #endif

//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AH1 ACpySgnH1(AH1 d,AH1 s){return AH1_AW1(AW1_AH1(d)|(AW1_AH1(s)&AW1_(0x8000u)));}
  AH2 ACpySgnH2(AH2 d,AH2 s){return AH2_AW2(AW2_AH2(d)|(AW2_AH2(s)&AW2_(0x8000u)));}
  AH3 ACpySgnH3(AH3 d,AH3 s){return AH3_AW3(AW3_AH3(d)|(AW3_AH3(s)&AW3_(0x8000u)));}
  AH4 ACpySgnH4(AH4 d,AH4 s){return AH4_AW4(AW4_AH4(d)|(AW4_AH4(s)&AW4_(0x8000u)));}
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AH1 ASignedH1(AH1 m){return ASatH1(m*AH1_(A_INFN_H));}

//_____________________________________________________________/\_______________________________________________________________
//==============================================================================================================================
//                                                [FIS] FLOAT INTEGER SORTABLE
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Float to integer sortable.
//  - If sign bit=0, flip the sign bit (positives).
//  - If sign bit=1, flip all bits     (negatives).
// Integer sortable to float.
//  - If sign bit=1, flip the sign bit (positives).
//  - If sign bit=0, flip all bits     (negatives).
// Has nice side effects.
//  - Larger integers are more positive values.
//  - Float zero is mapped to center of integers (so clear to integer zero is a nice default for atomic max usage).
// Burns 3 ops for conversion {shift,or,xor}.
//==============================================================================================================================
 AU1 AFisToU1(AU1 x){return x^(( AShrSU1(x,AU1_(31)))|AU1_(0x80000000));}
 AU1 AFisFromU1(AU1 x){return x^((~AShrSU1(x,AU1_(31)))|AU1_(0x80000000));}
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 // Just adjust high 16-bit value (useful when upper part of 32-bit word is a 16-bit float value).
 AU1 AFisToHiU1(AU1 x){return x^(( AShrSU1(x,AU1_(15)))|AU1_(0x80000000));}
 AU1 AFisFromHiU1(AU1 x){return x^((~AShrSU1(x,AU1_(15)))|AU1_(0x80000000));}
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 #ifdef A_HALF
  AW1 AFisToW1(AW1 x){return x^(( AShrSW1(x,AW1_(15)))|AW1_(0x8000));}
  AW1 AFisFromW1(AW1 x){return x^((~AShrSW1(x,AW1_(15)))|AW1_(0x8000));}
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AW2 AFisToW2(AW2 x){return x^(( AShrSW2(x,AW2_(15)))|AW2_(0x8000));}
  AW2 AFisFromW2(AW2 x){return x^((~AShrSW2(x,AW2_(15)))|AW2_(0x8000));}
 #endif

//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// yyyyxxxx - The 'i' input.
// 76543210
// ========
// HGFEDCBA - Naming on permutation.
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```
